desc: A neighborhood-history walk through Vesterbro’s shift from red-light district to creative quarter. From the central station, it passes a red-light street with a wartime hideout and a converted meatpacking district, ending at a brewery’s elephant gate.

title: Copenhagen with Context: An Introduction to the City’s Bustling Center
creator: Context Travel
desc: An expert-led heritage walk through Copenhagen’s royal and cultural landmarks. In a royal garden before a crown-jewels castle, it passes an old astronomical tower and a former royal palace turned parliament, ending at a 17th-century harbor.

title: Copenhagen Insights: A Walk of Self-Discovery and Urban Change in Kalvebod Pier
creator: Eliana Cobos
desc: A mindful architecture walk exploring Copenhagen’s transformed harborfront. Starting at a café inside a modern hotel, it passes a historic police headquarters and an underwater sea farm, ending at a geometric glass office building.

title: The Castle Island’s Royal History: Slotsholmen and Christiansborg
creator: James Cowan
desc: A history walk through 900 years of royal power on Copenhagen’s castle island. Starting at the square where the city was founded, it passes the grounds of a grand royal palace and a hidden library garden, ending at a museum dedicated to a sculptor.

title: Copenhagen’s Storybook Christmas: A Hans Christian Andersen Tour
creator: Pernille Schlander
desc: A seasonal literary walk tracing Hans Christian Andersen’s Copenhagen and its Christmas traditions. Near the old harbor, it passes an attic room where he lived as a student and the house where he wrote his tales, ending at his monument near city hall.

title: Copenhagen’s Little Amsterdam: A Mindful Walk through Christianshavn
creator: Eliana Cobos
desc: A mindful neighborhood walk through Copenhagen’s canal-laced Christianshavn district. Starting at a bakery by the main canal, it passes a central square with ties to Greenland and hidden 17th-century courtyards, ending at a waterside ferry café.

title: Turtle Bunbury’s Dublin: St Stephen’s Green to Trinity College
place: Wolfe Tone memorial, St Stephen’s Green
creator: Turtle Bunbury
desc: A literary walk tracing Dublin’s writers and rebels, from Oscar Wilde to Joyce. From a city-park memorial, it passes a Georgian hotel tied to a famous general and a statue built from stones sourced worldwide, ending at a historic university.

title: Ireland’s Oldest Railway: Dublin Bay By Train
creator: John Twomey
desc: A scenic train journey along Ireland’s first railway, tracing Dublin Bay’s coast. From a station near Trinity College, it passes a mill tied to a failed rebellion and a fortified Napoleonic-era tower, ending at a seaside town in the Wicklow foothills.

title: Inner City Dublin: A Revolutionary Walk from O’Connell Bridge to Abbey Theatre
creator: Jack Redmond
desc: A history walk tracing the Irish struggle for independence through Dublin’s inner city. Starting at a bridge over the River Liffey, it passes a grand post office tied to a failed rebellion and a towering steel monument, ending at the national theatre.

title: Stories of Dublin: A Heritage Walk from St Patrick’s Cathedral to Merrion Square
creator: Dave Kavanagh
desc: A heritage walk through Dublin’s landmarks, pubs, and characters. Starting at the city’s tallest cathedral, it passes a medieval Viking-founded cathedral and a famous shopping street, ending at a Georgian garden square.

title: A Dublin Docklands Tour: From Famine Ships to Ireland’s Silicon Harbour
creator: Jack Redmond
desc: A history walk tracing 200 years along Dublin’s docklands, from famine emigration to a modern tech hub. From an 18th-century customs building on the river, it passes a replica famine ship and a playwright’s bridge, ending at a harborside square.

title: Howth Harbour Walk: Explore the UNESCO Biosphere of Dublin Bay
creator: Shane O’Doherty
desc: A coastal walk through a fishing harbor’s Viking, monastic, and rock ’n’ roll history. From the harbor’s train station, it passes an 800-year-old abbey and a lighthouse guarding an offshore island’s monastery ruins, ending near the harbor entrance.

title: A Dublin Walking Tour: 1,000 Years of Patriots, Poets and Pubs in Temple Bar
creator: Jack Redmond
desc: A neighborhood walk through Temple Bar’s Viking origins and music history. From a square across from Dublin’s oldest university, it passes a pub named for the district’s founding family and a Viking longboat statue, ending in the cobbled heart.

title: Marlay Park’s Heritage: A Stroll through Dublin’s Playground
creator: John Twomey
desc: A heritage walk through a 500-year-old estate turned public park. From a historic walking trail, it passes ornamental lakes designed by a wealthy banking family and a converted stable yard of artisans, ending at a Georgian manor house.

title: A Town of Kings and Rebels: A Stroll Along Dún Laoghaire’s East Pier
creator: Jack Redmond
desc: A history walk tracing a seaside town’s royal name-changes and rebel legacy. Starting at a 19th-century parish church, it passes a monument to a British king and a captured Crimean War cannon, ending near a statue of an executed Irish revolutionary.

title: Dublin’s Breweries and Back Alleys: A Guide to The Liberties
place: The Lord Edward pub, Christchurch Place
creator: Jack Redmond
desc: A neighborhood-history walk through Dublin’s medieval Liberties. From a pub opposite a Viking-era cathedral, it passes an old library with reading cages to deter book thieves and a whiskey-and-stout quarter, ending at a public fountain.

title: The Mystical Hill of Tara: A Guide to the Hill of Heroes
creator: Derek Spillane
desc: An ancient-history walk through Ireland’s legendary seat of the High Kings. At a Stone Age ceremonial hilltop’s entrance, it passes an ancient passage tomb and a fairy tree tied to folk healing, ending back near the entrance.

title: Empires Fell, Cats Stayed: Istanbul’s Spice Bazaar to Topkapi Tour
creator: Heidi Nicklaus
desc: A history walk through Sultanahmet’s landmarks, framed through the city’s famous street cats. From a 17th-century spice market, it passes the Sultan’s private pavilion and the palace courtyard that once ran an empire, ending at the Blue Mosque’s courtyard.

title: Istanbul Through Time: Stories of Byzantines and Ottomans in the Old Town
creator: Yasemin Gurer
desc: A history walk through Sultanahmet, tracing the city’s shift from Byzantine capital to Ottoman power. From a park between two great mosques, it passes a 3,500-year-old obelisk and a working 16th-century hammam, ending at the ancient zero-mile marker.

title: Stepping Back Through Chalcedon: A Kadikoy Walking Tour
creator: Lisa Morrow
desc: A history walk through Kadıköy, Istanbul’s Asian-side district, tracing its Greek, Armenian, and Ottoman layers. From the ferry pier, it passes a 19th-century Armenian church on 5th-century foundations and a historic confectionery, ending at a busy square.

title: The Hippodrome and the Blue Mosque
creator: Arzu Tutuk
desc: A focused walk through the chariot-racing grounds of Byzantine Constantinople and one of Istanbul’s most iconic mosques. It passes hieroglyphs on a 3,500-year-old obelisk and a domed fountain gifted by a German emperor, ending at a Grand Vizier’s palace.

title: Vondelpark and Old West Neighbourhood: Amsterdam’s Green Heart
creator: Wilhelmus
desc: A local’s-eye view of the city’s biggest park and its surrounding neighborhood: starting at the park’s grand 19th-century entrance, wind past Gothic Revival churches and a multicultural market, ending at a century-old street market.

title: Art and Architecture in Amsterdam’s Golden Age: A Tour with Context
creator: Context Travel
desc: An art-historian’s walk through the city’s artistic peak: starting at the foot of a landmark church tower, pass ornate canal houses and a painter’s former home, ending along the canal ring’s grandest address.

title: Space Tourist Amsterdam: Explore the City’s Cosmic Side by Public Transport
creator: Alexandra Sokolowski
desc: An unusual tour of the city’s space industry: starting at a historic windmill, hop trams and buses past a science museum, a university’s planetary-science lab, and a modern art museum, ending at a golden astronaut statue.

title: Old Amsterdam: A Walking Tour through the East Side and Jewish District
creator: Edmond Van Putte
desc: A two-hour dive into maritime and Jewish history: starting at the city’s only intact medieval gate, hop across artificial islands past dockside warehouses and Holocaust memorials, ending near the old waterfront.

title: Power and Politics: An Amsterdam Audio Tour with Context
creator: Context Travel
desc: A historian’s tour of the city’s wealthiest era: starting at a medieval square outside an old weighing house, trace trading-company warehouses and a grand synagogue, ending near the main central square.

title: Red Light District
creator: Republic of Amsterdam Radio
desc: A candid history tour of the city’s most notorious neighborhood: starting at the main central square, weave through medieval alleys past a hidden church and the city’s oldest surviving building, ending at a statue honoring sex workers worldwide.

title: Red Lights, Trade and Tolerance: A Tour of Amsterdam’s Old Centre
creator: Time Travel Amsterdam
desc: A sweeping eight-century history walk through the old center: starting at the city’s main central square beside a WWII memorial, pass the red-light windows and old trading streets, tracing how tolerance shaped commerce here.

title: Vibrant Amsterdam East: A Story of Urban Revival Beyond the Canals
creator: Bart
desc: An urban-revival walk through the multicultural east side: pass a converted 18th-century dockside warehouse district and a market street named for a former Dutch colony, as a working-class quarter becomes one of the city’s most diverse.

title: An Amsterdam Introduction: From Fishing Hamlet to Trading Centre
creator: Edmond Van Putte
desc: A history-lover’s origin story for the city: starting at the grand central train station, follow the old waterfront and a surviving medieval tower into a maze of narrow streets, ending at a lively square marking a 15th-century city gate.

title: The Dutch Invented That: An Irreverent Amsterdam Tour
creator: Greg Shapiro
desc: A comedic tour of Dutch inventions: starting outside the city’s grand main train station, pass the site of the world’s first stock exchange and marvel at fearless local cyclists, ending at one of the city’s oldest gin bars.

title: Family-Friendly Amsterdam: A Walking Tour for Adults and Kids
desc: A playful, character-narrated tour built for kids and parents together: walk from the main station down a street built over a buried river, past a fairy-tale-like clock tower, to the city’s floating flower market.

title: Medieval and Modern Brussels: A Tour through the Heart of Europe
creator: Isaac
desc: A history walk tracing Brussels from medieval trade city to diplomatic capital. Starting at a grand royal palace, it passes a UNESCO-listed guild square and the city’s famous small statue, ending at a towering courthouse with sweeping views.

title: Brussels’ Noble Beginnings: An Upper Town Walking Tour
place: Belgian Federal Parliament (Palace of the Nation)
creator: Shawn Basey
desc: A history walk through Brussels’ aristocratic Upper Town, from royal parkland to grand museums. Starting outside a national parliament, it passes a former royal hunting park and a Baroque church with a curious legend, ending at a towering courthouse.

title: Brussels and Bureaucracy: A Guide to the EU District and its Architecture
creator: Shawn Basey
desc: An architecture walk through Brussels’ EU quarter, tracing its bureaucratic and imperial roots. Starting at a grand triumphal-arch park, it passes the European Commission’s headquarters and a museum on European history, ending at the European Parliament.

title: Hidden Brussels: A Local’s Guide to Secret Places and Untold Stories
creator: Derek Blyth
desc: A local-secrets history walk through Brussels’ old town. Starting outside a grand former stock exchange, it passes a baroque central square, a hidden stretch of old city wall, and the city’s most famous small statue, ending at a garden with sweeping views.

title: Latin Quarter Tour: The Panthéon, Rue Mouffetard and the Best of the Left Bank
creator: Annie Sargent
desc: A history walk through Paris’s intellectual quarter. From Shakespeare and Company, it passes the Panthéon, burial place of Marie Curie, Voltaire, and Victor Hugo, and Rue Mouffetard, ending at the Roman-era Arènes de Lutèce.

title: Montmartre: More than Meets the Eye
creator: Annie Sargent
desc: A history-and-art walk through the bohemian hilltop neighborhood. From Abbesses Metro, it passes the Bateau-Lavoir, where Picasso developed cubism, and the ‘Wall of Love,’ ending at Sacré-Cœur Basilica.

title: Paris’ Iron Lady: A Walking Tour from Trocadéro Gardens to the Eiffel Tower
creator: Annie Sargent
desc: A history-and-architecture walk to Paris’s most recognizable monument. From Trocadéro, it passes the Palais de Chaillot and Pont de Bir-Hakeim, ending at Champ de Mars in front of the Eiffel Tower.

title: The Left Bank’s Most Elegant Park: Exploring the Luxembourg Garden
creator: Gary Kraut
desc: A park walk through 400 years of royal and civic history. From the northeast entrance by Odéon, it passes the Medici Fountain and a bronze Statue of Liberty replica paired with a 9/11 memorial oak, ending at the Luxembourg Museum.

title: The French Revolution in Paris: A Walking Tour with Context
creator: Context Travel
desc: A history walk tracing the Revolution’s Marais-area roots. From Place de la Bastille, it passes the Hôtel de Sully and Musée Carnavalet, ending at the Palais de Justice.

title: The Tuileries Garden: The Royal Walk from the Louvre to the Champs-Élysées
creator: Gary Kraut
desc: A royal-history garden walk. From the Louvre’s equestrian statue, it passes the Arc de Triomphe du Carrousel and the Musée de l’Orangerie, ending at Place de la Concorde.

title: The Champs-Élysées: From Place de la Concorde to the Arc de Triomphe
creator: Gary Kraut
desc: A walk up Paris’s grand avenue. From Place de la Concorde, it passes Pont Alexandre III and the Petit and Grand Palais, ending at the Arc de Triomphe.

title: Finding the Lost Generation in Montparnasse
creator: Philippa Campsie
desc: A literary-history walk through 1920s expatriate Montparnasse. From Port Royal RER, it passes cafés like La Closerie des Lilas and La Coupole, haunts of Hemingway, Fitzgerald, Gertrude Stein, and Man Ray, ending near the Théâtre de l’Odéon.

title: Savoring Paris: A Food Lover’s Walk around Les Halles
creator: Annie Sargent
desc: A food walk through the historic market district. From La Samaritaine, it passes Stohrer, Paris’s oldest patisserie (since 1730), and the Fontaine des Innocents, ending at Boulangerie Eric Kayser on Rue Montorgueil.

title: A Walking Tour through Napoleon’s Paris
creator: FrancoAmericana
desc: A history walk tracing Napoleon’s imperial legacy. From the Arc de Triomphe du Carrousel, it passes the Colonne Vendôme, cast from 180 captured cannons, and the Palais Bourbon, ending at Napoleon’s tomb in Hôtel des Invalides.

title: Art Nouveau and Modernist Architecture: A Guide to Paris’ 16th Arrondissement
creator: Catherine Anne
desc: An architecture walk through three design movements. From Pont de Grenelle, it covers Guimard’s Castel Béranger (birthplace of Parisian Art Nouveau), Le Corbusier’s Maison La Roche, and Rue Mallet-Stevens, ending on Rue de l’Assomption.

title: Between Two Revolutions: A Guide to Marquis de La Fayette’s Paris
creator: Rochambeau Chapter DAR
desc: A Revolutionary-era history walk. From the Bourse de Commerce, it passes the Palais Royal and the Hôtel de Coislin, where the treaty recognizing American independence was signed, ending near Lafayette’s final apartment.

title: Highlights Around Parc Montsouris: From Hidden Water to Secret Villages
place: Pavillon de la Porte d’Arcueil, Parc Montsouris
creator: Comte de Saint-Germain
desc: A walk through hidden southern Paris. From Pavillon de la Porte d’Arcueil, it explores Art Nouveau mosaic streets, the underground Montsouris reservoir (‘cathedral of water’), and Cité Universitaire, ending near Square des Mimosas.

title: Paris through the Ages: A Walking Tour from Notre Dame to Pont de la Concorde
creator: Peter Groark
desc: A sweeping history walk from medieval to revolutionary Paris. From Notre-Dame’s Point Zéro, it passes Sainte-Chapelle, Pont Neuf, and the Arc de Triomphe du Carrousel, ending at Pont de la Concorde.

title: Paris of Dreams and Nightmares: The Dark Side of the City of Light
creator: Gary Kraut
desc: A dark-history walk through central Paris. From Pont au Change, it covers the Conciergerie’s torture towers, the guillotine’s execution site, and the Mémorial de la Shoah, ending on Quai de la Mégisserie.

title: Paris’ Right Bank with Context: A Tour from the Louvre to the Arc de Triomphe
creator: Context Travel
desc: A royal-and-imperial history walk. From the Louvre’s Cour Carrée, it passes Palais Royal, the Tuileries, and Place de la Concorde, ending at the Arc de Triomphe.

title: Marais Through the Centuries: A Tour of Paris’ Historical District with Context
creator: Context Travel
desc: A history walk tracing the Marais from wetlands to aristocratic quarter to Jewish district to bohemian enclave. It passes Hôtel de Sens, Village Saint-Paul, Place des Vosges, and Musée Carnavalet, ending at Square du Temple.

title: Coco Chanel’s Paris: A Walking Tour
place: Rue de Rivoli at the Tuileries Garden
creator: Philippa Campsie
desc: A fashion-history walk tracing Chanel’s Paris. From Rue de Rivoli near the Tuileries, it passes the Ritz (her home for decades), her fashion house at 31 Rue Cambon, and Place Vendôme, ending at Café de la Paix.

title: Paris’ Left Bank Tour with Context: From Notre Dame to the Latin Quarter
place: Cité Métro station, Île de la Cité
creator: Context Travel
desc: An art-and-history walk. From near Île de la Cité, it passes Sainte-Chapelle, Shakespeare and Company, and Saint-Germain-des-Prés, ending at Pont des Arts.

title: Gourmet and Kid-Friendly Walk in the Marais
creator: Claire Mora
desc: A family-friendly food-and-history walk. From Place de l’Hôtel de Ville, it stops at bakeries (Berko, Pralus, Huré), the Picasso Museum, and Place des Vosges, ending at a hidden garden on Rue des Rosiers.

title: Lessons in History: A Guide to Thomas Jefferson’s Time in Paris
place: Thomas Jefferson statue, Quai Anatole France
creator: Rochambeau Chapter DAR
desc: A history walk through Jefferson’s pre-revolutionary Paris. From his statue near Musée d’Orsay, it passes Le Procope café and the Hôtel de Salm (which inspired Monticello), ending near the former home of an early abolitionist.

title: Hemingway’s Paris: A Tour of His Life and Work with Context
place: 74 Rue du Cardinal Lemoine (Hemingway’s first apartment)
creator: Context Travel
desc: A literary biography walk retracing a young American novelist’s 1920s years in the Left Bank student quarter. From outside his first apartment, it passes a hilltop church and a domed mausoleum, ending at a famous English-language bookshop.

title: Benjamin Franklin’s Paris: A Guide to the Revolutionary’s Life in the City
creator: Rochambeau Chapter DAR
desc: A Revolutionary-era history walk on the Americans who won France’s help for independence. From a square with a statue of two allied generals shaking hands, it crosses palace gardens with Eiffel Tower views to the envoys’ former estate.

title: Midnight in Montparnasse
creator: Julia Kuzmina
desc: A cultural-history walk through the artists’ quarter in its 1910s–30s heyday. From a metro exit near the district’s tall black tower, it passes a square honoring an American-born dancer, ending at a famous writers’ café.

title: Above the Catacombs in Lupin’s footsteps: A Paris Walking Tour
place: Port-Royal maternity hospital, Boulevard de Port-Royal
creator: Comte de Saint-Germain
desc: A crime-and-TV walk tracing street-level filming spots from a Netflix heist series above the city’s bone-filled tunnels. From a maternity hospital, it passes a high-walled prison and an observatory garden, ending back on the boulevard.

title: Renovation, Restoration and Rebirth: A Notre-Dame Tour with Context
creator: Context Travel
desc: An indoor architectural walk through Notre-Dame’s 900-year history and 2019–2024 fire restoration. From the cathedral square, it covers the nave, rose windows, and Crown of Thorns reliquary, ending at the Grand Organ.

desc: A royal-history walk following the first leg of Bohemia’s coronation route through the Old Town. From outside a grand Art Nouveau civic hall, it runs down a medieval thoroughfare to the old main square, ending at the plaza by the famous stone bridge.

creator: Jo Eckardt

creator: Rory MacLean
desc: A history walk through Berlin’s tumultuous 20th century, from Kaiser to Cold War. Starting outside a subway station by the parliament building, it passes a triumphal gate and a field of memorial slabs, ending near former government ministry gardens.

title: Ku’damm: Haute Couture and Currywurst

desc: An architecture walk through Berlin’s post-reunification government buildings. Starting at a bridge over the river near the parliament, it follows striking modern buildings along the riverside, ending near the national chancellery.

creator: Coffee Coos of Dean Village

title: Lisbon’s Iconic Tiles: A Walking Tour with Context

title: Gateway to the Americas: A Walking Tour Through Seville’s Golden Age
place: General Archive of the Indies (Archivo de Indias)
creator: Ben Barclay
desc: A deep dive into Seville’s golden age as the port for Spain’s empire. From the colonial archive, it follows the old shipyards and mint down to the river and its golden watchtower, then returns through the cathedral and Jewish quarter.

title: Essential Seville Walking Tour
creator: Alba TourGuide
desc: A local guide’s overview of the Andalusian capital’s must-see landmarks. From a central square, it takes in the vast Gothic cathedral and its Moorish bell tower, the old Jewish quarter, and a former tobacco factory, ending at a grand tiled plaza.

title: Flamenco on the Guadalquivir: Industry and Artistry in Seville’s Triana
creator: Ben Barclay
desc: A walk through the working-class quarter across the river, home to flamenco and ceramics. From the old iron bridge, it winds past tiled churches, a former Inquisition castle turned market, and potters’ streets, ending with a skyline view.

title: Seville Revealed: The Architecture of Santa Cruz and Plaza de España
place: General Archive of the Indies (Archivo de Indias)
creator: WALKITECT
desc: An architect’s deep read of the city’s built fabric, from medieval alleys to a 1929 expo showpiece. From the colonial archive, it winds through the old Jewish quarter and a grand park to the tiled plaza, ending at the Gothic cathedral.

title: Seville’s Plaza de España: A Window into the Rich History of Spain
place: Aníbal González statue, Plaza de España
creator: Ben Barclay
desc: A focused tour of Seville’s grandest square, built for the 1929 expo. From its architect’s statue, it circles the tiled semicircle bench by bench, reading the ceramic panels that tell the history of each Spanish province.

title: Palaces and Piazzas: The Highlights of Florence
creator: Elisabetta Marchi
desc: A history walk through Florence’s monuments and the Medici’s rise from bankers to rulers. From the cathedral square, it passes a guild church built as a grain market and a secret elevated walkway, ending at a centuries-old wine palace.

title: Inside the Uffizi Galleries: An Art History Guide
creator: Alexandra Korey
desc: An in-museum walk through the Uffizi’s Renaissance masterpieces, led by a PhD art historian. From the ticket entrance, it moves chronologically past an unfinished Leonardo and a sculptor’s only surviving panel, ending on a dramatic late-Renaissance canvas.

title: Fantastic Florence Sights: Michelangelo Terrace and San Miniato Basilica
creator: Fabio Strufaldi
desc: A scenic walk through Florence’s green hillside quarters, from the river to a panoramic overlook. From a bridge over the Arno, it passes a rose garden of unusual public art and a hillside cemetery, ending at a marble-faced medieval basilica.

title: Three Hundred Years of Art, Power, and Politics: A Tour of Medici Florence
creator: Julie Thomas
desc: A walk tracing the Medici dynasty across three centuries and three palaces. From the family’s mausoleum church, it passes a palace built to avoid ostentation and the square where a coup turned deadly, ending at the family’s final grand residence.

title: Monumental Moments in History: A Florence Walking Tour
creator: Julie Thomas
desc: A history walk tracing 2,000 years of Florence through its central squares. From the cathedral square, it passes a 600-year-old bell tower and a boar-shaped fountain said to bring good luck, ending at the ancient Roman forum’s site.

title: Where Tradition Meets History: A Walking Tour of Florence’s Oltrarno District
creator: Julie Thomas
desc: A neighborhood walk through Florence’s authentic, less-touristed Oltrarno district. From Ponte Vecchio’s southern foot, it passes a secret Medici prayer corridor overlooking a church and a hidden square popular with locals, ending near a medieval tower.

title: Uffizi Gallery: A Tour of Renaissance Masterpieces
creator: Julie Thomas
desc: An in-museum walk through the Uffizi’s Renaissance masterpieces, from Gothic painting to the High Renaissance. From the entrance, it passes Botticelli’s mythologies and an unfinished Leonardo, ending in the Michelangelo and Raphael room.

title: Politics and Power: An Introduction to Florence with Context
creator: Context Travel
desc: A history walk looping through Florence’s historic core, tracing the power behind the Renaissance. Starting and ending at a Roman-era square, it passes a secret elevated corridor built for a ruling family and a fountain said to bring good luck.

title: Classic Florence: From Piazza di Santa Maria Novella to Ponte Vecchio
creator: Francesca
desc: An introductory history walk from the station square to Florence’s oldest bridge. From a Gothic basilica near the station, it passes a self-supporting dome and a bustling indoor food market, ending at the city’s oldest bridge.

title: Fine Food in Florence: A Walking Tour with Context
creator: Context Travel
desc: A food-and-wine walk tracing Tuscan culinary traditions through Florence’s center, with tastings. From a central political square, it passes a centuries-old wine bar with an underground cellar and a tripe-sandwich cart, ending at a bohemian market square.

title: Bridging Florence’s History: An Arno River Walking Tour with Context
place: Piazza dei Mozzi, by Ponte alle Grazie
creator: Context Travel
desc: A history walk tracing how the Arno shaped Florence’s economy and disasters. From a riverside square near a historic bridge, it passes flood markers on facades and a Renaissance palace with a rooftop porch, ending at a medieval city gate.

title: AudioZoom into Florence: An Introduction to the Historical City Center
creator: eArs
desc: An introductory history walk through Florence’s Renaissance landmarks, in a light, accessible style. From the Medici mausoleum church, it passes the house of a legendary medieval poet and a lucky boar fountain, ending at a Roman-era square.

title: A Culinary Tour of El Born
creator: Foodie in Barcelona
desc: A food-blogger’s tasting walk through a medieval trading district: from a bulk wholesaler where locals queue for grains and nuts, pass a 160-year-old almond roastery and a beloved counter-service seafood bar, ending at a pastry shop dating to 1849.

title: Barceloneta Unfiltered: A Walking Tour of the Soul Behind the Sand
creator: Christoph
desc: A ten-year resident’s walk through a working-class beach barrio: starting at the metro station, pass tiny apartments, a wood-fired bakery, and a memorial sculpture for demolished beach shacks, ending at a beachside community kiosk.

title: Barcelona’s Architecture: A Guide to Art Nouveau and Gaudí with Context
creator: Context Travel
desc: An architecture historian’s walk through the city’s Modernist golden age: from the main central square, trace an elegant boulevard past ornamented merchant houses and one of the architect’s three masterpieces, ending outside his unfinished basilica.

title: Barcelona Walking Tour: Landmarks and Legends of El Born and Ciutadella Park
creator: Spain Walking Tours
desc: A history walk through a medieval trading district and its park: starting at a grand 19th-century train station, pass a crowdfunded Gothic basilica and the city’s shortest street, ending near a park built on the ruins of a former citadel.

title: La Sagrada Familia: An Audio Guide with Context
creator: Context Travel
desc: An architecture expert’s indoor decode of the city’s unfinished basilica: from the security entrance, walk through tree-like columns and three biblically-narrated façades, ending in the museum workshops that hold the architect’s original plaster models.

title: Park Güell Tour: A Fun and Cultural Look into Gaudí’s World
creator: Les Bons Plans de Barcelone
desc: A local guide’s circular tour of a UNESCO-listed hillside park: starting at a mosaic-covered entrance, wind past an ergonomic curved bench and a colorful salamander sculpture, climbing to the park’s highest point for panoramic city views.

title: Catalan Culture with Context: A Guide to Barcelona’s Gràcia District
place: Jardinets de Gràcia, by Hotel Casa Fuster
creator: Context Travel
desc: A cultural historian’s tapas-and-history walk through a once-independent village: starting at a garden near a Modernist hotel, trace how industrialization forged a distinct regional identity, ending at a square marking a 19th-century uprising.

title: Jewish Barcelona: A History Tour with Context
creator: Context Travel
desc: A historian’s trace of 700 years of Jewish life: from a gate where medieval merchants once entered the city, pass a preserved ritual bath and a former synagogue site now home to Catalonia’s government, ending at the city’s Gothic cathedral.

title: Barcelona Walking Tour: El Raval and the Gothic Quarter’s Landmarks
creator: Spain Walking Tours
desc: A local-legends tour of the old city: from a fountain said to guarantee your return to Barcelona, weave from La Rambla’s red-light past through the Gothic Quarter’s Roman foundations, ending near a cursed bridge skull said to hold the city together.

title: Multicultural Madrid Walking Tour: From Plaza Mayor to Lavapiés
creator: Melissa Dura
desc: A social-history walk of Madrid’s Jewish, Muslim, and Christian past into Lavapiés, home to 82 nationalities. From Plaza Mayor, it passes cave taverns once haunted by a bandit and Spain’s last ‘República Española’ fountain, ending at Plaza Antón Martín.

title: Medieval Madrid: A Guide to the City’s Muslim Past
creator: Felicity Hughes
desc: A history walk tracing Madrid’s origins as Mayrit, the only European capital founded by a Muslim ruler. From Plaza de Oriente, it passes the underground Tower of Bones and flint walls said to spark when struck, ending in the old Morería quarter.

title: Malasaña Backstreets: Rebellious Suburb to Hipster Haven
creator: Felicity Hughes
desc: A history walk through Malasaña’s turn from pious suburb to post-Franco creative hub. From Plaza de la Luna, it passes the Convent of San Plácido, site of a 1630s scandal, and the bars where Almodóvar and the Movida launched, ending at the History Museum.

title: El Retiro Park’s Rise, Ruin and Redemption: A Tour of the Former Royal Retreat
place: Goya Monument, beside the Prado Museum
creator: Felicity Hughes
desc: A history walk through the UNESCO royal park, from royal retreat to public park. From the Monument to Goya, it passes the House of Beasts, where lions once fought, and the lake where the royal elephant bathed, ending at the Fallen Angel fountain.

title: Madrid’s Literary District: A Barrio de las Letras Tour
creator: Felicity Hughes
desc: A literary-history walk through the Golden Age quarter of Cervantes and Lope de Vega. From Plaza de Santa Ana, it passes the convent holding Cervantes’s bones and Hemingway’s Civil War-era bars, ending at a garden said to be haunted by dead writers.

title: Beauty, Scandals, and Masterpieces: A Prado Museum Audio Guide
creator: Yohanna Lerman
desc: An in-museum audio guide through the Prado’s essential works. From the Jerónimos hall, it covers Bosch’s Garden of Earthly Delights, the mirror trick in Velázquez’s Las Meninas, and Goya’s Naked Maja, ending with Sorolla’s sunlit beaches.

title: History with a Side of Tapas: A Local’s Madrid
creator: Native Spanish Tapas
desc: A history-and-food walk pairing Madrid’s Moorish-to-modern past with family-run tapas bars. From Plaza Isabel II, it visits Casa Labra, serving cod croquettes since 1860, and Casa Botín, the world’s oldest restaurant, ending over Madrid-style paella.

title: Tales of the Old Town: A Madrid Walking Tour with Context
place: Isabel II statue, Plaza de Isabel II
creator: Context Travel
desc: A royal-history walk through the Habsburg and Bourbon eras. From the Isabel II statue by Teatro Real, it covers the Royal Palace’s rebuild after an 18th-century fire and the 1492 expulsion of Spain’s Jews, ending at the old Chocolatería San Ginés.

title: Madrid’s Golden Age: 500 Years of History along the Manzanares River
creator: Clare Starkie
desc: A history walk along the northern Manzanares bank, tracing 500 years from the Spanish Golden Age to today. From Segovia Bridge, it passes the Vargas Palace, where Napoleon’s brother hid from an angry mob, ending near Puente del Rey and the Royal Palace.

title: Elegant Salamanca and Chueca: A Guide to Madrid’s Posh Districts with Context
creator: Context Travel
desc: An architecture-and-history walk through Madrid’s 19th-century expansion districts. From Palacio de Cibeles, it traces José de Salamanca’s rags-to-riches-to-rags development of Calle Serrano and Chueca’s rise as an LGBTQ+ hub, ending near Calle Alcalá.

title: Madrid Walking Tour: Manzanares River’s Story from Prehistory to Popular Park
creator: Clare Starkie
desc: A history walk along the Manzanares, tracing 300,000 years to the modern Madrid Río park. From the Matadero, a converted slaughterhouse, it passes the much-relocated Obelisco de la Castellana, built for a deposed queen, ending at the Toledo Bridge.

title: The Roman Jewish Ghetto
creator: Giancarlo Buonomo
desc: A Jewish-history walk through Europe’s oldest such community, tracing 2,000 years from papal persecution to wartime deportation. From the old gateway on a main street, it passes the great synagogue and kosher kitchens, ending at the riverbank.

title: Rome and the Renaissance: A Tour from the Vatican City to Piazza di Spagna
creator: A History of Italy Podcast
desc: A Renaissance art-and-history walk from the Vatican to the famous steps. From the great colonnaded square before the basilica, it passes a riverside papal fortress, an emperor’s tomb, and a landmark oval piazza, ending by the elegant stairway.

title: Rome’s Medieval Village: A Trastevere Walking Tour
creator: Tiffany Parks
desc: A neighbourhood walk through the medieval quarter across the river, all ivy-draped alleys and artisan food shops. From a lively riverside piazza, it takes in a mosaic-fronted basilica and tiny old churches, ending at a busy tram square.

title: Roman Forum in Focus: An Audio Guide to Ancient Rome’s Heart
place: Temple of Antoninus and Faustina, Roman Forum
creator: Michael Anderson
desc: An ancient-history walk through the ruined heart of the empire, needing a site ticket. From a columned temple portico, it threads past the senate house, the sacred flame’s temple, and Caesar’s funeral site, ending at a triumphal arch.

title: Rome’s Colosseum with Context: Its Games, Architecture, and History
creator: Context Travel
desc: An in-depth guide to the great arena, from its bloody games and logistics to its architecture. From a slope facing the amphitheatre, it takes you inside to imagine the gladiators, animal hunts, and roaring crowds, ending among the ruins within.

title: From Aqueducts to Baroque: Rome’s Fountains and Squares Walking Tour
creator: GeoBeat Audio Tour
desc: A fountains-and-squares walk reading Rome through its water and stone. From the great baroque coin-tossing fountain, it takes in an ancient domed temple, a sunken ruins square, and a market piazza, ending at a stately Renaissance square.

title: Spanish Steps to Piazza Navona: A Meander through Baroque Rome
creator: Stephanie Bull
desc: A baroque-heart stroll through Rome’s showpiece squares and fountains. From a boat-shaped fountain below the famous stairway, it winds past the great coin-tossing fountain and the domed ancient temple, ending at an oval piazza on a chariot stadium.

title: The History of Power in Modern Rome: An Ancient City Walking Tour
creator: A History of Italy Podcast
desc: A political-history walk tracing power from ancient Rome to the modern republic. From the triumphal arch outside the amphitheatre, it passes the seats of Italian government, a president’s palace, and the coin-tossing fountain, ending at a piazza.

title: The Jewel of the Roman Renaissance: A St Peter’s Basilica Audio Guide
creator: A History of Italy Podcast
desc: An in-depth guide to the great Renaissance basilica, its art and its symbols. From the colonnaded square, it moves inside past Michelangelo’s Pietà, ornate chapels, and Bernini’s bronze canopy, ending at the towering altar beneath the dome.

title: The Pantheon: The Mysteries and Secrets of the World’s Largest Dome
creator: Tiffany Parks
desc: An in-depth guide to the ancient temple with the world’s largest unreinforced dome. From the square before its columned porch, it moves inside to read the coffered dome, the open oculus, and Raphael’s tomb, ending by a famous coffee bar.

title: Castel Sant’Angelo with Context: An Audio Guide of Hadrian’s Mausoleum
creator: Context Travel
desc: An in-depth guide to the riverside castle that began as an emperor’s tomb, later a papal fortress and prison. From the statue-lined bridge, it moves through burial chambers, papal apartments, and cells, ending on the rooftop terrace with city views.

title: From Egypt to Papal Rome: St Peter’s Square, Martyrdom and Power
creator: GeoBeat Audio Tour
desc: A deep read of the Vatican’s great piazza, from ancient Egypt to papal power. From the central obelisk where a ceremonial avenue opens out, it takes in the sweeping colonnade and the basilica facade, ending at the sealed Holy Door.

title: The Vatican Museums Audio Tour with Context: A Guide to the Treasures Within
creator: Context Travel
desc: An expert-led, five-guide walk through the Vatican’s vast art collection. From outside the museum entrance, it moves through painting galleries, Egyptian and Etruscan rooms, tapestry and map halls, and the Raphael Rooms, ending in the Sistine Chapel.

title: Rome for Readers: A Literary Tour of the Eternal City
creator: Tiffany Parks
desc: A literary walk following the writers who fell for Rome — Keats, Byron, Goethe, Dickens, and more. From a panoramic hilltop terrace, it descends past a landmark oval piazza, an old literary café, and the poets’ stairway, ending at a fountain square.

title: Borghese Gallery and Museum: An Audio Tour with Context
creator: Context Travel
desc: An expert-led walk through one cardinal’s dazzling art collection. From outside the villa museum in its park, it moves room to room past Bernini’s marble myths, Caravaggio’s realism, and Renaissance masterworks, ending among neoclassical sculpture.

title: The Roman Forum and the Palatine Hill with Context: An Audio Tour
place: Palatine Hill entrance, Via di San Gregorio
creator: Context Travel
desc: An archaeologist-led walk through the heart of ancient Rome. From a gate near the Colosseum, it climbs the founding hill past emperors’ palaces and a view terrace, then drops into the Forum’s temples and arches, ending at a triumphal arch.

title: Pizzas, Pastas and Piazzas: A Guide to Rome’s Culinary Culture with Context
creator: Context Travel
desc: An expert-led food walk through Rome’s culinary traditions. From a Renaissance river bridge, it winds through market squares and old bakeries, pastry bars, and salumerie, unpacking pizza, pasta, and aperitivo, ending in a historic riverside quarter.

title: Ostia Antica: An Audio Guide with Context
creator: Context Travel
desc: An archaeologist-led walk through Rome’s ancient port city on the coast. From the site’s ticket office, it follows cart-rutted streets past a necropolis, mosaic baths, apartment blocks, and a huge theatre, ending among grand civic ruins.

title: Nero’s Rome: A Guide to the Infamous Emperor with Context
creator: Context Travel
desc: An archaeologist-led walk tracing a notorious emperor’s vanished golden palace. From a café on a ruin-filled hill, it crosses a park past imperial baths and a buried cistern, skirts the Colosseum, and ends at an ancient chariot-racing field.

title: Hidden Gems of Ancient Rome with Context
creator: Context Travel
desc: An archaeologist-led walk past the overlooked corners beside Rome’s famous sights. From Michelangelo’s hilltop square, it threads the old center past talking statues and obelisks, ending at a museum built around an ancient altar.

title: The World’s Largest Church: A St Peter’s Basilica Audio Tour with Context
creator: Context Travel
desc: An art-historian-led walk inside the world’s largest church, with an optional dome climb. From the great colonnaded square, it moves through the basilica past Michelangelo’s Pietà, papal tombs, and Bernini’s Baroque interior, then up to the cupola.

title: Ancient Stadium, Baroque Fountains: A Piazza Navona Audio Tour
place: Fountain of the Moor, Piazza Navona
creator: GeoBeat Audio Tour
desc: A deep read of Rome’s most theatrical square, built over a buried Roman stadium. From its curved southern end by a triton fountain, it takes in a papal palace, a baroque church, and Bernini’s four-rivers fountain, ending at a Neptune fountain.

title: Londinium’s Footprint: Roman Wall Walk
creator: Amy McMahon
desc: A history walk tracing the path of London’s Roman wall, from 1st-century origins to rediscovery after WWII bombing. From the Tower of London, it passes wall the Normans built on and a segment hidden in a parking garage, ending near the Barbican.

title: Spectacle, Sin and Uproar: A Hidden History of Covent Garden
creator: Jack Chesher
desc: A history walk through Covent Garden’s rowdier past, from piazza to red-light district and back. It passes a theatre where audiences rioted 62 days over ticket prices and a pub nicknamed ‘Bucket of Blood’ for bare-knuckle boxing, ending on a backstreet.

title: Stephen Fry’s Quite Interesting Tour of the City and Bankside
creator: QI
desc: A walk through the City of London and Bankside, narrated by Stephen Fry with the BBC QI team. From St Paul’s, it passes Shakespeare’s Globe, where Fry once performed, and a play so ‘cursed’ it went unperformed for 400 years, ending near the London Stone.

title: From Friars to Fellmongers: A Historic Bermondsey Walking Tour
creator: Steve Matthews
desc: A history walk tracing Bermondsey’s shift from monastic settlement to leather district. From London Bridge, it passes an 11th-century abbey where monks drained the marshes and streets where tanners once worked, ending near the old Leather Market.

title: London’s Alternative History Tour: Uncovering the City’s Secrets
creator: Joey Leskin
desc: A quirky, off-beat history walk through Covent Garden and the Strand, led by a London-born travel writer. It passes London’s grandest hidden courtyard and a street so oddly angled it still confuses taxi drivers, ending at a historic riverside pub.

title: Hyde Park and Kensington Gardens: Royalty, Relaxation and Rebellion
creator: Gio
desc: A scenic walk through two of London’s grandest Royal Parks, led by a 15-year local guide. From Marble Arch, it passes the site of London’s most famous open-air free-speech venue and a 900-year-old oak said to hide fairies, ending near Kensington Palace.

title: The South Bank: 400 Years of Entertainment from London Bridge to the Tate Modern
place: Monument to the Great Fire of London
creator: Brian Cookson
desc: A history walk tracing Southwark as London’s entertainment district, from Chaucer’s pilgrims to Shakespeare’s playhouses. Near Monument, it passes Britain’s oldest theatre, now a museum, and steps that inspired Oliver Twist, ending at Tate Modern.

title: Theatreland Tour with Ian McKellen
creator: Official London Theatre
desc: A walk through London’s West End theatre district, narrated by Ian McKellen with tales from his stage career. From a Leicester Square booth, it passes a monument with a missing sundial and a theatre once a public toilet, ending near Trafalgar Square.

title: Stephen Fry’s Quite Interesting Tour of Westminster
creator: QI
desc: A walk through Westminster full of royal and political trivia, narrated by Stephen Fry with the BBC QI team. From Westminster Pier, it passes 10 Downing Street, whose last private resident was known only as ‘Mr. Chicken,’ ending near Cleopatra’s Needle.

title: The Ealing Beaver Project Tour: A Pioneering Urban Rewilding Story
creator: The Ealing Beaver Project
desc: A nature walk through Britain’s only public urban beaver reintroduction site, led by the project’s license holder. From a sunken wetland once farmland and golf course, it passes beaver-built dams and a pond crossing, ending at the 2023 release lagoon.

title: Canons Park: The Life and Times of the Duke of Chandos
creator: Aaron Graham
desc: A history walk through a once-grand estate, developed with an Oxford research centre, tracing the Duke of Chandos’s rise and fall. It passes a mile-long avenue he landscaped and a temple exposing ties to empire and slavery, ending in parkland.

title: For Your Ears Only: James Bond’s London
creator: Talk the Walk
desc: A film-history walk tracking real London locations from the James Bond films. From Piccadilly, it passes the hotel bar that inspired ‘shaken, not stirred’ and buildings used as MI6 and the MoD on screen, ending in Covent Garden.

title: Westminster - Heart of the Nation
creator: Brian Cookson
desc: A history walk through the ceremonial core of British government, from Whitehall to the Archbishop of Canterbury’s home. From Embankment, it passes Banqueting House, where Rubens’s ceiling hangs above where Charles I died, ending at Lambeth Palace.

title: Classic Sights and Hidden Histories
creator: Steven Russell
desc: A ‘greatest hits’ history walk through Royal London and the stories behind its facades. From Green Park, it passes the Cabinet War Rooms — Churchill’s whisky-fueled war HQ — and Parliament built over a plague pit, ending at Trafalgar Square.

title: The Killing of a King: Royal London during the reign of King Charles I
creator: Talk the Walk
desc: A history walk retracing Charles I’s final steps from palace to execution block. Near the Ritz, it passes the hall where he was tried and a widow who kept her husband’s severed head for 20 years, ending at Banqueting House, where he died in 1649.

title: Wicked Whitechapel: Where Now’s Jack the Ripper Audio Tour
creator: Where Now Audio
desc: A true-crime history walk tracing the 1888 Jack the Ripper murders through the East End, via dramatized scenes with voice actors. From Whitechapel station, it passes Brick Lane and a pub where a victim was last seen, ending opposite the Ten Bells pub.

title: Historical Pubs of London: A Tipply Trundle Through Liquid History
creator: Liquid History Tours
desc: A pub-crawl history walk down Fleet Street’s ‘street of shame,’ led by the author of an award-winning London pub guide. From Blackfriars, it passes London’s oldest tailor and a haunted backstreet boozer dating to 1549, ending on the edge of Covent Garden.

title: Charles Dickens from Furnival’s Inn to Doughty Street
creator: Lucinda Hawksley
desc: A literary-biography walk through Dickens’s early London, led by his own descendant. From Chancery Lane, it passes Staple Inn, a half-timbered building he saw daily as a young journalist, and streets that inspired Bleak House, ending at the Dickens Museum.

title: Tower of London to St Paul’s: An Ancient Square Mile Walking Tour
creator: Martin Hughes
desc: A history walk tracing 2,000 years of the City of London, from Roman ruins to Georgian finance. From the Tower of London, it passes a bombed-out Wren church now a garden and London’s first coffee-house site, birthplace of Lloyd’s, ending near St Paul’s.

title: Exploring Mayfair: London’s Most Luxurious Neighbourhood
creator: Gio
desc: A neighborhood walk through London’s wealthiest district, tracing 300 years from Shepherd Market to Savile Row. Near Hyde Park Corner, it passes an old execution route the Grosvenors turned into boutiques and a century-old barbershop, ending at Piccadilly.

title: Fairer than Florence: A Stroll Through Thomas Cubitt’s Pimlico
creator: Steve Matthews
desc: A history walk through Pimlico, tracing the builder who turned farmland into stucco squares. From St George’s Drive, it passes Churchill’s old home in Eccleston Square and Dolphin Square, a 1930s block favored by spies, ending near Bessborough Street.

title: Bohemian Bloomsbury: A Guide to Literary London
creator: Brian Cookson
desc: A literary-history walk through the Bloomsbury Group’s haunts — Woolf, Eliot, and their circle — across Georgian squares. From Warren Street, it passes the pub where Dylan Thomas met his wife and Orwell’s Ministry of Truth model, ending at Yeats’s home.

title: Walking Wandsworth: A Riverside Stroll between Putney and Battersea
creator: Steve Matthews
desc: A history walk along the southwest Thames, tracing 2,000 years of riverside change. From St Mary’s Church Putney, it passes the grave of Benedict Arnold and a former gasworks once central to hot-air ballooning, ending at Battersea Park’s Peace Pagoda.

title: Notting Hill far beyond the film
creator: Rafa Maciel
desc: A social-history walk through Notting Hill’s shift from Victorian slum to carnival capital. From Holland Park, it passes a park once a Victorian waste dump and the site of the 1958 race riots that birthed Notting Hill Carnival, ending on Portobello Road.

title: The Britpop Camden Tour
creator: Miranda Diboll
desc: A first-person music-history walk through Camden’s mid-90s Britpop scene, narrated by someone who was there. From Caffe 43, it passes the Good Mixer pub where the Blur-vs-Oasis rivalry began and Dingwalls, ending at the Dublin Castle.

title: The Rise and Fall of Roman London with Tristan Hughes
creator: History Hit
desc: A Roman-history walk tracing Londinium from its founding to its abandonment in 410 AD. From London Bridge’s south side, it crosses the ‘burn layer’ left by Boudica’s rebellion and passes the London Mithraeum, ending at Roman wall in the Barbican.

title: Finding Fitzrovia: The Neighbourhood on the Fringe of Soho
creator: Steve Matthews
desc: A history walk through a neighborhood so obscure it had no official name until the 1970s. From Goodge Street, it passes the Fitzroy Tavern — haunt of Dylan Thomas and George Orwell — and a Hard Day’s Night filming spot, ending on Grafton Way.

title: The Ted Lasso Way: A Richmond Walking Tour
creator: Timeless Walking Tours
desc: A TV-tourism walk through Richmond, tracing filming locations from the Emmy-winning series Ted Lasso. From Richmond Station, it passes the 700-year-old Richmond Green seen in many scenes and Ted’s flat, ending at the pub that became the Crown & Anchor.

title: Symbols of the City: Decoding Two Thousand Years of London
creator: Jack Chesher
desc: A history walk through the City of London’s overlooked symbols and details. From St Paul’s tube, it passes Postman’s Park’s memorial to Londoners who died saving others and the first coffeehouse site, birthplace of Lloyd’s, ending at Leadenhall Market.

title: Diamonds, Bishops and a Daring Heist: Hatton Garden Walking Tour
creator: Steve Matthews
desc: A history walk through London’s jewellery quarter, from a bishop’s palace to a diamond heist. From Farringdon, it passes St Etheldreda’s Church and its medieval roof and the 2015 Hatton Garden heist site, ending at a royal banknote engravers’ home.

title: A Walk Around the Tower of London from the Monument to Traitors Gate
place: Monument to the Great Fire of London
creator: J. P. Holdstock
desc: A history walk through the Tower’s darker legends, from executed queens to a bear named Martin. From Monument, it crosses London Bridge and the South Bank before circling back over Tower Bridge, ending at Traitors Gate.

title: The Great Fire of London with Dan Snow
creator: History Hit
desc: A history walk tracing the 1666 fire’s four-day path of destruction. From Pudding Lane, where it began, it crosses London Bridge as Pepys described it and passes St Paul’s, ending at the Golden Boy of Pye Corner, where the fire stopped.

title: London’s Royal Parks: Primrose Hill and Regent’s Park
creator: Gio
desc: A parks-and-architecture walk from Primrose Hill’s panoramic viewpoint down through Regent’s Park to Baker Street. From Chalk Farm, it passes London Zoo and the Sherlock Holmes Museum, ending at 221b Baker Street.

title: Stockholm’s Old Town: A Scenic Island Walk
creator: Irina Kåvik
desc: A guide’s scenic walk across the Old Town’s quiet islands, heavy on architecture and legend. From a lakeside embankment, it explores Riddarholmen’s crooked buildings and royal burial church, then the palace and cathedral, ending at the opera house.

title: Vienna and the Holocaust: From Tragedy to Justice
creator: Raymond and Krista White
desc: A substantive walk through Jewish Vienna and the city’s role in the Holocaust. From the old Jewish quarter across the canal, it visits a former Gestapo site, a synagogue, and the central victims’ memorial, following a famous Nazi hunter’s work.

title: The World That No Longer Exists: Krakow’s Kazimierz District
creator: Wiktor Marcinkowski
desc: A walk through Krakow’s old Jewish and Christian quarter, tracing centuries of coexistence that ended in tragedy. It passes the birthplace of a cosmetics pioneer and a 16th-century synagogue and cemetery still in use, ending at a Moorish-style synagogue.

title: Composing Dublin: Photography on a Walking Tour
creator: Nuala Redmond
desc: A photography walk through Dublin’s docklands and Georgian squares, pairing smartphone technique with local history. From a triumphal arch near the custom house, it passes a replica famine ship and a harp-shaped bridge, ending at a literary garden square.

title: Robert Louis Stevenson’s Edinburgh Trail: The University Years
creator: Martin White
desc: A literary-biography walk tracing Robert Louis Stevenson’s university years and the Gothic Old Town behind his darkest writing. From a close opposite a medieval cathedral, it passes a university quad and a grave-robbing graveyard, ending at a poets’ kirk.

title: Art Nouveau’s Sublime Capital: A Brussels Walking Tour
creator: Derek Blyth
desc: An architecture walk through a quiet residential district’s Art Nouveau treasures. Starting outside a modern glass tower, it passes the world’s first Art Nouveau house and a restored mural-covered townhouse, ending at a grand Art Nouveau mansion.

title: A Tasty Stroll Around The Cool Spots of the Pijp
creator: Susam
desc: A local’s food-and-hangouts walk through a trendy southern neighborhood: starting at a former cinema turned café, pass a famous street market and a leafy park, ending at a cozy wine bar.

title: The Whistlers (La Gomera)
creator: Corneliu Porumboiu
desc: Porumboiu’s sunlit noir: a crooked Bucharest cop learns a Canary Islands whistling language to spring a launderer and abscond with the cash. Half the film flies south. The corrupt Bucharest of surveilled flats and dirty money the plot begins in.

title: 4 Months, 3 Weeks and 2 Days (4 luni, 3 săptămâni și 2 zile)
creator: Cristian Mungiu
desc: Mungiu’s Palme d’Or masterpiece: two students arrange an illegal abortion in 1987 Bucharest, a single grim day under Ceaușescu’s total control. A communist-era hotel and the student dorms, the grey city where the terrible transaction unfolds.

title: The Way I Spent the End of the World (Cum mi-am petrecut sfârșitul lumii)
creator: Cătălin Mitulescu
desc: Two siblings in a Bucharest apartment block live the last year of the dictatorship in 1989, from playground to revolution. Tender and sly. The identical concrete blocks of the outer city, the regimented world the regime built to house everyone.

title: The Death of Mr. Lazarescu (Moartea domnului Lăzărescu)
creator: Cristi Puiu
desc: The film that lit the Romanian New Wave: a sick old man is shuttled by ambulance between Bucharest hospitals all night as doctors pass him along. Blackly funny. The central hospitals, the indifferent system the dying man is ferried through.

title: La French (The Connection)
creator: Cédric Jimenez
desc: The true 1970s duel between a crusading magistrate and the mob boss behind the ‘French Connection’ heroin pipeline out of Marseille. Jean Dujardin. The port city of labs and hitmen where the world’s heroin was refined and shipped.

title: Taxi
creator: Gérard Pirès
desc: A Besson-scripted action-comedy: a speed-demon Marseille cabbie and a hapless cop chase a gang through the city in a souped-up Peugeot. The streets of Marseille, the tunnels and seafront corniche its runaway car races along at full throttle.

title: Girl Picture (Tytöt tytöt tytöt)
creator: Alli Haapasalo
desc: Three Helsinki teenagers — two best friends and a figure skater — chase desire and identity across three Fridays. Warm, frank and Sundance-winning. The malls, rinks and bus stops of the ordinary city where their weekends happen.

title: Dogs Don’t Wear Pants (Koirat eivät käytä housuja)
creator: J-P Valkeapää
desc: A strange, tender Finnish oddity: a widowed heart surgeon numb with grief finds feeling again through a Helsinki dominatrix. Not for everyone. The anonymous modern city of clinics and basement clubs where his double life unfolds.

title: Bye (Adiós)
place: Las Tres Mil Viviendas, Polígono Sur (area)
creator: Paco Cabezas
desc: A prisoner on day release comes home for his daughter’s first communion, and her death that night opens up police corruption and the drug trade. A hard, sun-bleached Seville thriller. Las Tres Mil Viviendas, the estate where it begins.

title: Hobson’s Choice
creator: David Lean
desc: A tyrannical bootmaker’s eldest daughter marries his shy assistant and sets up a rival shop. David Lean shot the streets on location, and it shows 1880s Salford with real wit. Chapel Street, the Salford high road where Hobson’s shop stands.

title: The Class of ’92
creator: Ben Turner and Gabe Turner
desc: Documentary about six Manchester United youth players, Beckham, Giggs, Scholes, Butt and the Neville brothers, who grew up together and won the 1999 Treble. A good way into the city’s football culture. Old Trafford, United’s stadium.

title: A Taste of Honey
creator: Tony Richardson
desc: A British New Wave landmark: a Salford teenager, pregnant by a Black sailor, sets up home with a gay friend as her mother drifts off. Tender and radical for 1961. Salford, the canals, gasworks and back-to-back streets of the postwar northern city.

title: East Is East
creator: Damien O’Donnell
desc: A Pakistani chip-shop owner in 1971 Salford tries to force arranged marriages on his half-English sons, and the family revolts. Very funny, then dark. The Salford terraces, the mixed working-class streets where two cultures collide at home.

title: Hell Is a City
creator: Val Guest
desc: A hard-boiled Hammer thriller shot on the real streets: a Manchester detective hunts an escaped robber across rooftops, pubs and the moors. The city centre, whose 1960 warehouses and alleys the film captures before the slum clearances erased them.

title: 24 Hour Party People
place: Site of the Haçienda club, Whitworth Street West
creator: Michael Winterbottom
desc: Steve Coogan as Tony Wilson in a gleeful, unreliable telling of Factory Records — Joy Division, New Order, Happy Mondays and the Haçienda’s rise and ruin. The Haçienda site on Whitworth Street West, the club that bankrupted Factory.

title: Control
creator: Anton Corbijn
desc: Anton Corbijn’s stark black-and-white portrait of Joy Division’s Ian Curtis — marriage, epilepsy, fame, and his suicide at 23. Devastating. Macclesfield, the satellite town south of Manchester where Curtis lived and died, not the city itself.

title: Looking for Eric
creator: Ken Loach
desc: Ken Loach’s warm comedy: a broken Manchester postman is counselled by a hallucinated Eric Cantona, and his mates rally against a gangster. Old Trafford, the United ground whose god-king steps out of the poster to sort his life out.

title: Peterloo
creator: Mike Leigh
desc: Mike Leigh’s sprawling recreation of the 1819 Peterloo Massacre, when cavalry charged 60,000 peaceful reform demonstrators in central Manchester. St Peter’s Field, now St Peter’s Square, where the sabres came down on the crowd.

title: England Is Mine
creator: Mark Gill
desc: A quiet portrait of the young Morrissey in 1970s Manchester — a clerk with a typewriter, crushing boredom and enormous ambition — before the Smiths existed. Stretford, the suburb of the bedroom where he wrote and waited for a way out.

title: Oasis: Supersonic
creator: Mat Whitecross
desc: An exhilarating archive documentary of Oasis’s rocket from a Burnage council house to Knebworth in five years, told by the warring Gallaghers. Burnage, the south Manchester suburb the brothers grew up fighting in and never stopped fighting about.

title: Inheritance
creator: James Moll
desc: The daughter of camp commandant Amon Göth meets Helen Jonas, who was forced to work as a maid in his villa. It is a film about inheritance and reckoning. They meet at Płaszów, the former camp site in southern Kraków.

title: Needle Park Baby (Platzspitzbaby)
creator: Pierre Monnard
desc: Based on Michelle Halbheer’s memoir of growing up with a heroin-addicted mother. The most-watched Swiss film of 2020. It opens in 1995 as police clear the Letten, the riverside rail area where Zurich’s drug scene moved after Platzspitz.

title: Bad Luck Banging or Loony Porn (Babardeală cu bocluc)
creator: Radu Jude
desc: Radu Jude’s Golden Bear provocation: a teacher’s leaked sex tape drags her before outraged parents, split by a montage-tour of the pandemic city. Central Bucharest, whose ad-choked, monument-strewn streets the film walks as an essay in itself.

title: Tom of Finland
creator: Dome Karukoski
desc: The true story of Touko Laaksonen, war hero turned creator of the world’s most famous homoerotic art, in a postwar Helsinki that criminalised him. Central Helsinki, the parks and back rooms of the closeted gay city he drew his way out of.

title: Marius
creator: Alexander Korda
desc: The first of Pagnol’s beloved Marseille Trilogy: a young man torn between the sea’s call and the girl he loves, in his father’s bar on the old harbour. The Vieux-Port, the quayside of César’s café and the sailors’ Marseille it made immortal.

title: Transit
creator: Christian Petzold
desc: Petzold’s haunting adaptation of Anna Seghers: a refugee waits in Marseille for papers to escape a fascist Europe, in a story set eerily in the present. The port and its consulates, the desperate waiting-room city of exiles hoping for a ship.

title: 22 Bullets (L’Immortel)
creator: Richard Berry
desc: Jean Reno as a retired Marseille godfather who survives 22 bullets from a childhood friend and hunts down everyone behind the hit. The Old Port and the hills above it, the gangster’s Marseille of villas, cafés and long-nursed vendettas.

title: Marius et Jeannette
creator: Robert Guédiguian
desc: Guédiguian’s tender L’Estaque romance: a cashier and a watchman with battered pasts find each other among a warm, struggling working-class community. L’Estaque, the seaside industrial neighbourhood the director has filmed his whole career.

title: Bye Bye
creator: Karim Dridi
desc: Two French-Tunisian brothers land in Marseille’s Panier after a family tragedy, one drifting toward a dangerous dealer. A landmark of the immigrant city. Le Panier, the steep old quarter of newcomers, temptation and belonging above the port.

title: Comme un aimant (The Magnet)
creator: Kamel Saleh & Akhenaton
desc: A group of young men drift through petty crime and dead-end days in Le Panier, made by Marseille’s own rap royalty from IAM. Le Panier, the labyrinth of stairs and squares whose street life and slang the film breathes.

title: Borsalino
creator: Jacques Deray
desc: Delon and Belmondo as rival dandies turned partners carving up the 1930s Marseille rackets — based on the real gangsters Carbone and Spirito. The old central quarters around the Opéra, the interwar underworld of protection and vice they conquer.

title: Shéhérazade
creator: Jean-Bernard Marlin
desc: A raw, tender debut: a teenage ex-con adrift in Marseille falls for a young sex worker among the estates and back streets. Kenza Fortas, electric. The Belsunce and Noailles quarters, the hard central Marseille the lovers survive in.

title: Nightwatching
creator: Peter Greenaway
desc: Greenaway’s argument is that Rembrandt hid an accusation of murder inside The Night Watch, and was ruined for it. Strange, painterly, and slow. The painting hangs in the Rijksmuseum, in a room built for it.

title: Loving Vincent
creator: Dorota Kobiela & Hugh Welchman
desc: Every frame is an oil painting, made by over a hundred artists, and it investigates how Van Gogh actually died. Unlike anything else. The story happens in France, but the Van Gogh Museum on Museumplein holds most of the paintings it imitates.

title: Anne Frank Remembered
creator: Jon Blair
desc: The Oscar-winning documentary, filmed in the real places. Interviews with the friends who survived, with Miep Gies who hid them, and seven seconds of home-movie footage of Anne on a balcony, the only film of her that exists.

title: Riphagen
place: Former SD headquarters, Gerrit van der Veenstraat
creator: Pieter Kuijpers
desc: The other side of occupied Amsterdam: a Dutch criminal who promised Jews safety for money, then handed them to the Germans anyway. He was never punished. The Nazi security HQ was on what is now Gerrit van der Veenstraat, in the south.

title: Süskind
creator: Rudolf van den Berg
desc: A German Jew works for the Nazis at the theatre where Amsterdam’s Jews are being held, and smuggles around 600 children out the back. Walter Süskind was real. He did not survive. The Hollandsche Schouwburg is now a memorial.

title: Turkish Delight
creator: Paul Verhoeven
desc: The most-watched Dutch film ever made: a sculptor and the woman he loves, wildly, and then she gets ill. Explicit, tender, and now over fifty years old. Jan Wolkers wrote the novel about his own marriage.

title: Amsterdamned
creator: Dick Maas
desc: A diver murders people and escapes through the canals, and there is a genuinely great speedboat chase along them. It’s a silly thriller, and the city is just a set, but it’s the cult Amsterdam film.

title: Meet the Fokkens
creator: Rob Schröder & Gabriëlle Provaas
desc: Twin sisters in their late sixties who worked the windows of the Red Light District for fifty years, and are still at it. Funny, matter-of-fact, and sadder than it looks. Filmed on the Wallen, where they had their rooms.

title: The Resistance Banker
creator: Joram Lürsen
desc: A banker and his brother quietly stole the equivalent of half a billion euros from the Dutch central bank and used it to fund the resistance. It’s true, and it’s the largest bank fraud in Dutch history. Van Hall was executed in 1945.

title: The Wounds (Rane)
creator: Srđan Dragojević
desc: Two boys in a New Belgrade tower block grow up through the 1990s wars into celebrity gangsters. Brutal, sardonic, the definitive film of Serbia’s lost decade. Not gentle. The concrete blocks of Novi Beograd, the estates the gangsters came from.

title: Love Affair, or The Case of the Missing Switchboard Operator (Ljubavni slučaj)
creator: Dušan Makavejev
desc: A Black Wave landmark, banned for years: a switchboard operator’s affair with a rat-catcher is intercut with lectures on sexology and criminology. Playful, erotic, subversive. Dorćol, the old riverside quarter of tenement rooms where the lovers meet.

title: Tito and Me (Tito i ja)
creator: Goran Marković
desc: A dreamy ten-year-old in a crowded 1954 Belgrade flat adores Marshal Tito and wins a march to his birthplace. A warm, sly comedy about a personality cult seen from a child’s height. The House of Flowers, Tito’s Belgrade residence and now his tomb.

title: Who’s Singin’ Over There? (Ko to tamo peva)
creator: Slobodan Šijan
desc: A ramshackle bus carries squabbling passengers toward Belgrade on 5 April 1941, the day before the bombs fall. Voted the best Serbian film of its half-century, and very funny until it isn’t. Terazije, the central boulevard the bus is trying to reach.

title: Cabaret Balkan (Bure baruta)
creator: Goran Paskaljević
desc: One night in late-1990s Belgrade, strangers collide in a chain of grudges and violence that keeps escalating. A furious portrait of a city with nothing left to lose. Slavija, the traffic-choked central roundabout the film’s night keeps circling.

title: The Trap (Klopka)
creator: Srdan Golubović
desc: A father in post-Milošević Belgrade cannot afford his son’s heart surgery, and a stranger offers him money to kill a man. A cold, superb thriller about a city where everything has a price. The Gazela Bridge, between the old city and the new.

title: Balkan Spy (Balkanski špijun)
creator: Dušan Kovačević & Božidar Nikolić
desc: A former political prisoner becomes convinced his new lodger is a foreign agent, and turns his household into a one-man secret police. A comedy about the paranoia a police state leaves behind. Voždovac, the low suburban streets of the family house.

title: Underground
creator: Emir Kusturica
desc: Kusturica’s Palme d’Or epic: a cellar full of Belgraders is kept believing the war never ended, for fifty years. Wild, drunken, furious, hugely argued-over. The Belgrade Zoo below Kalemegdan fortress, bombed open in 1941 as the animals flee.

title: The Load (Teret)
creator: Ognjen Glavonić
desc: During the 1999 NATO bombing, a driver hauls a sealed truck from Kosovo to Belgrade, told not to look inside. Quiet, austere, and about a real war crime the country still argues over. Batajnica, the airbase outskirts where mass graves were found.

title: The Happiest Day in the Life of Olli Mäki
creator: Juho Kuosmanen
desc: A wry, tender true story: a Finnish boxer is hyped into a 1962 world title fight while quietly realising he cares far more about the woman he loves. The Olympic Stadium, where the whole country watched him lose the bout and win his life.

title: Concrete Night (Betoniyö)
creator: Pirjo Honkasalo
desc: A black-and-white drama about a 14-year-old boy’s last night with his older brother before the brother goes to prison. It shows a hard Helsinki far from the harbour. The concrete housing estates of the eastern suburbs, where it was shot.

title: Tove
creator: Zaida Bergroth
desc: A biopic of Tove Jansson in the years after the Second World War, painting, partying and inventing the Moomins. It shows the bohemian Helsinki that shaped her. Ullanlinna, the seaside district where she kept her tower studio for decades.

title: Helsinki, Forever (Helsinki, ikuisesti)
creator: Peter von Bagh
desc: Peter von Bagh’s essay-documentary assembles a century of Finnish film, newsreel, painting and song into a portrait of Helsinki itself — its wars, its poverty, its light. Senate Square, the neoclassical heart the city keeps returning to on screen.

title: The Man Without a Past (Mies vailla menneisyyttä)
creator: Aki Kaurismäki
desc: Aki Kaurismäki’s Cannes-winning masterpiece: a man beaten senseless in Helsinki loses his memory and rebuilds a life among the container-dwellers by the harbour. Deadpan and deeply kind. The Verkkosaari harbour, home to his shipping-crate community.

title: The Paper Will Be Blue (Hârtia va fi albastră)
creator: Radu Muntean
desc: A tense real-time night of the December 1989 revolution: a militia conscript deserts to join the uprising, and his unit hunts him through the chaos. The Romanian TV station, the epicentre from which the televised revolution convulsed the city.

title: The Autobiography of Nicolae Ceaușescu (Autobiografia lui Nicolae Ceaușescu)
creator: Andrei Ujică
desc: Andrei Ujică’s three-hour montage of state-archive footage, letting Ceaușescu’s own propaganda tell his 25-year reign — rallies, palaces, adulation — with no narration. The Palace of the Parliament, the colossal folly his megalomania built.

title: Child’s Pose (Poziția copilului)
creator: Călin Peter Netzer
desc: A Golden Bear drama of class and control: an imperious, wealthy Bucharest mother pulls every string to shield her adult son after he kills a boy in a car crash. The affluent north of the city, the villas and connections her money can still buy.

title: Filantropica (Philanthropy)
creator: Nae Caranfil
desc: A wry landmark comedy of Bucharest hustle: a broke teacher falls in with a beggar-mafia boss who runs the city’s guilt for profit. The fancy restaurants of central Bucharest, where staged sob-stories are performed for the diners’ small change.

title: Pororoca
creator: Constantin Popescu
desc: A harrowing slow-burn: a Bucharest father loses sight of his small daughter for a moment in a park, and his life collapses into obsession. An ordinary city park, the sunny green space where a single instant tears a family apart.

title: Collective (Colectiv)
creator: Alexander Nanau
desc: An Oscar-nominated documentary following reporters who, after the 2015 Colectiv nightclub fire, expose the hospital corruption that killed the burn victims. Astonishing, true. The Colectiv club site, the sealed factory where 64 young people died.

title: Tintoretto: A Rebel in Venice
creator: Giuseppe Domingo Romano, Pepsy Romanoff
desc: Documentary on Jacopo Tintoretto, a Venetian painter who rarely left the city and fought rivals for work. Its centre is the Scuola Grande di San Rocco, a confraternity hall he filled with canvases between 1564 and 1587.

title: Dangerous Beauty
creator: Marshall Herskovitz
desc: Glossy drama on Veronica Franco, a 16th-century courtesan and published poet who faced the Inquisition and was acquitted. A 1565 register of courtesans lists her in the parish of Santa Maria Formosa, a church and campo in Castello.

title: The Merchant of Venice
place: Jewish Ghetto, Campo del Ghetto Nuovo
creator: Michael Radford
desc: Al Pacino plays Shylock in this Shakespeare adaptation shot in Venice. It opens by showing how the city confined its Jews, which the play leaves offstage. The Ghetto, a walled Cannaregio quarter, was created by decree in 1516.

title: Casanova
creator: Lasse Hallström
desc: Light romantic comedy with Heath Ledger, shot on location and loose with the facts. The real Casanova was jailed in the Piombi, cells under the lead roof of the Doge’s Palace, and escaped across that roof in 1756.

title: The Wings of the Dove
place: Palazzo Barbaro on the Grand Canal
creator: Iain Softley
desc: Henry James adaptation moved to 1910: two lovers scheme over a dying American heiress. James stayed at Palazzo Barbaro, a Grand Canal palace, and put its ballroom in the novel. The film shot there.

title: Death in Venice
creator: Luchino Visconti
desc: Visconti’s slow, lush take on Thomas Mann’s novella, with Dirk Bogarde as a composer fixated on a boy. Mann stayed at the Grand Hotel des Bains, a belle époque hotel on the Lido, in 1911. Visconti filmed there. It is now closed.

title: Peggy Guggenheim: Art Addict
place: Peggy Guggenheim Collection, Palazzo Venier dei Leoni
creator: Lisa Immordino Vreeland
desc: Documentary on the American collector who backed Pollock and Ernst. In 1949 she bought Palazzo Venier dei Leoni, an unfinished palace on the Grand Canal, and lived there with her art. It is now the Peggy Guggenheim Collection museum.

title: Summertime
creator: David Lean
desc: David Lean’s romance with Katharine Hepburn as a lonely American tourist, shot on location in 1950s Venice. In Campo San Barnaba, a square in Dorsoduro, she steps back for a photo and falls into the canal.

title: Don’t Look Now
creator: Nicolas Roeg
desc: Nicolas Roeg’s thriller about grieving parents in off-season Venice, all damp alleys and wrong turns. Donald Sutherland restores San Nicolò dei Mendicoli, a small church in western Dorsoduro. Has a frank sex scene.

title: Bread and Tulips
place: Campiello dei Miracoli, by Santa Maria dei Miracoli church
creator: Silvio Soldini
desc: Warm Italian comedy (Pane e tulipani): a Pescara housewife misses her tour bus and stays on in Venice. She works in a flower shop in Campiello dei Miracoli, a small square by the Miracoli church. The shop was a fake facade.

title: The Venice Syndrome
creator: Andreas Pichler
desc: Documentary (Das Venedig Prinzip) on a city emptying out: residents priced out to the mainland, porters and hotel staff serving the crowds. St Mark’s Square, the main piazza, is where the visitor numbers are plainest.

title: Ludwig
creator: Luchino Visconti
desc: Visconti’s portrait of Bavaria’s “fairy-tale king” Ludwig II, from coronation to his death in 1886. Long and slow, at four hours. Its Munich scenes were shot in the rococo Cuvilliés Theatre in the Residenz palace and at Nymphenburg.

title: Munich: The Edge of War
creator: Christian Schwochow
desc: Spy drama around the 1938 Munich Agreement, from Robert Harris’s novel. The characters are invented; the conference is not. Hitler and Chamberlain signed in the Führerbau, now the city’s music university building.

title: 13 Minutes
place: Site of the Bürgerbräukeller beer hall, Gasteig
creator: Oliver Hirschbiegel
desc: Original title Elser. Carpenter Georg Elser built a bomb into a pillar of the Bürgerbräukeller beer hall in 1939. Hitler left 13 minutes early. A plaque in the pavement by the GEMA building marks the pillar. Elser was killed at Dachau in 1945.

title: Sophie Scholl – The Final Days
creator: Marc Rothemund
desc: The White Rose student’s arrest, interrogation and trial, built from Gestapo transcripts. She was caught throwing leaflets into the atrium of the university’s main building in February 1943. She was executed four days later.

title: Go for It, Baby
creator: May Spils
desc: Zur Sache, Schätzchen: a lazy Schwabing songwriter drifts through one day and into trouble with the police. A huge 1968 hit and the defining picture of the old bohemian quarter. His flat is on Türkenstraße, a street of bars near the university.

title: Visions of Eight
creator: Miloš Forman, Kon Ichikawa, Claude Lelouch, Yuri Ozerov, Arthur Penn, Michael Pfleghar, John Schlesinger, Mai Zetterling
desc: The official film of the 1972 Games, made by eight directors who each took one subject: sprinters, weightlifters, the decathlon, the marathon. Shot largely in the Olympic Stadium, under its tent-like acrylic roof.

title: One Day in September
creator: Kevin Macdonald
