desc: Oscar-winning account of the 1972 hostage-taking of Israeli athletes. Eleven Israelis and a German police officer died. It began in the team’s apartments on Connollystraße in the athletes’ village. A memorial tablet stands at number 31.

title: September 5
place: Olympic Park, near the TV tower
creator: Tim Fehlbaum
desc: The 1972 hostage crisis as seen from the ABC Sports control room, which suddenly had to cover a live terror attack. Tense and tightly made. The studio sat in the Olympic Park, across from the athletes’ village. Shot in and around Munich.

title: Ali: Fear Eats the Soul
creator: Rainer Werner Fassbinder
desc: An older German cleaner marries a Moroccan guest worker, and Munich turns cold on them. Fassbinder’s plainest film about racism. On their wedding day they eat at the Osteria Italiana restaurant, once Hitler’s favourite.

title: Love to Love You, Donna Summer
creator: Roger Ross Williams, Brooklyn Sudano
desc: Portrait of the disco singer, co-directed by her daughter, from home movies and archive. Summer came to Munich for the musical Hair and stayed years. In the basement studio of the Arabellahaus tower she and Giorgio Moroder made “I Feel Love.”

title: Der blinde Fleck
place: Oktoberfest bombing memorial, Theresienwiese main entrance
creator: Daniel Harrich
desc: The Blind Spot: a journalist digs into the 1980 Oktoberfest bombing, closed as one man’s act. Thirteen people died at the fairground’s main entrance on the Theresienwiese. The case was reopened in 2014 and ruled far-right terror in 2020.

title: Rossini
creator: Helmut Dietl
desc: Satire of Munich’s film and media crowd, who eat, scheme and sleep with one another at one Italian restaurant. The Rossini was modelled on Romagna Antica, a real Schwabing restaurant on Elisabethstraße where that crowd did gather.

title: Munich: Secrets of a City
creator: Dominik Graf, Michael Althen
desc: München – Geheimnisse einer Stadt: an essay film mixing documentary and staged scenes about the city’s buried history and daily life, tied together by the 1999 solar eclipse. The rare feature that is about Munich itself. Hard to find with subtitles.

title: Welcome to Germany
creator: Simon Verhoeven
desc: Willkommen bei den Hartmanns: a well-off Munich family takes in a Nigerian refugee. Broad comedy, but rooted in 2015, when thousands of refugees arrived at the central station and residents met them with food and clothes.

title: Gnarr
creator: Gaukur Úlfarsson
desc: Documentary on Jón Gnarr, a punk comedian who founded a joke party after the financial crash and was elected mayor of Reykjavík. His office was City Hall, which stands at the edge of the Tjörnin pond.

title: 101 Reykjavík
creator: Baltasar Kormákur
desc: Baltasar Kormákur’s deadpan debut. A slacker who still lives with his mum sleeps with her girlfriend, a flamenco teacher, through downtown Reykjavík’s long winter nights. Kaffibarinn, a bar on Bergstaðastræti, is at the centre of the 101 scene.

title: The Innocents (De uskyldige)
creator: Eskil Vogt
desc: Eskil Vogt’s horror fable. Over a long, empty summer, children on an Oslo housing estate discover telekinetic powers and turn cruel. They run unwatched among the tower blocks of Romsås, an estate set against the forest. Disturbing in places.

title: Sick of Myself (Syk pike)
creator: Kristoffer Borgli
desc: Satire. A woman in Oslo’s art crowd disfigures herself with a banned drug to win back the attention her sculptor boyfriend gets. Her world is the galleries and cafés of Grünerløkka, a neighbourhood whose vanity the film mocks.

title: Easy Money (Snabba Cash)
creator: Daniel Espinosa
desc: A poor business student passes as rich in Stockholm’s smart set while sliding into the cocaine trade. About class, migration and money. Stureplan, the square at the centre of the city’s upmarket nightlife, is the world JW wants to buy into.

title: Summer with Monika (Sommaren med Monika)
creator: Ingmar Bergman
desc: Early Bergman. Two working-class Stockholm teenagers run off to the archipelago for a summer together, then come back to hard city life. Harriet Andersson’s breakout role. The couple’s story begins and ends in Södermalm, then a working-class district.

title: Northwest (Nordvest)
creator: Michael Noer
desc: A teenager works his way up Copenhagen’s immigrant underworld, burgling for one crime boss and then another, and drags his brother in. Shot in Nordvest, the hard northwest district of the city it is named after.

title: Reconstruction
creator: Christoffer Boe
desc: A man leaves his girlfriend for a stranger and wakes in a Copenhagen where no one knows him and the streets rearrange themselves. The city is the puzzle. Copenhagen Central Station, the main railway station, is the hub of its shifting map.

title: Intermission
creator: John Crowley
desc: Interlocking Dublin ensemble with Colin Farrell and Cillian Murphy: a bungled bank raid, a bus crash, a lovelorn cop. The city at street level, with a lot of swearing. It is set on the northside, in places like Fairview, a suburb of cafés and estates.

title: The Snapper
creator: Stephen Frears
desc: Roddy Doyle comedy. A young northside woman gets pregnant, won’t name the father, and her family closes ranks. Colm Meaney plays her flustered da. Kilbarrack, a northside suburb, is the real place behind Doyle’s fictional Barrytown.

title: Michael Collins
creator: Neil Jordan
desc: Neil Jordan’s epic about the man who ran the guerrilla war for Irish independence, from the 1916 Rising to the civil war that killed him. Liam Neeson stars. The rebels seized and held the General Post Office on O’Connell Street in 1916.

title: Istanbul Beneath My Wings (İstanbul Kanatlarımın Altında)
creator: Mustafa Altıoklar
desc: Period drama set in 17th-century Ottoman Istanbul, under a paranoid sultan, about the polymath Hezârfen, who tries to fly across the Bosphorus. Bawdy in places. Legend says he launched his glide from the Galata Tower, the stone tower above the Golden Horn.

title: Dikkenek
creator: Olivier Van Hoofstadt
desc: A crude comedy of ‘belgitude’. A Brussels loudmouth meddles in his shy friend’s love life. Marion Cotillard appears before she was famous. The Marolles, an old working-class quarter, supplies the dialect and swagger the film runs on.

title: Jeanne Dielman, 23 quai du Commerce, 1080 Bruxelles
creator: Chantal Akerman
desc: Chantal Akerman’s real-time study of a Brussels widow’s routine of cooking, cleaning and discreet prostitution, until it cracks. Voted the greatest film ever made. The title is her address, 23 Quai du Commerce, on the canal. Slow, at over three hours.

title: Caché (Hidden)
place: Rue des Iris (the film’s townhouse street)
creator: Michael Haneke
desc: Michael Haneke’s thriller. A comfortable Paris couple receive anonymous surveillance tapes that dig up a buried colonial guilt, the 1961 massacre of Algerians. Their townhouse, the one being watched, is on Rue des Iris, a quiet street in the 13th.

title: Breathless (À bout de souffle)
creator: Jean-Luc Godard
desc: Godard’s jump-cut landmark of the New Wave. A petty thief who has killed a policeman and an American girl selling newspapers improvise love and betrayal. She walks the Champs-Élysées, the city’s grand avenue, selling the Herald Tribune.

title: Children of Paradise (Les Enfants du paradis)
creator: Marcel Carné
desc: Marcel Carné’s epic of 1830s Paris theatreland: a courtesan and the mime, actor, count and thief who love her. Shot in secret under the Occupation. It recreates the playhouses of the Boulevard du Temple, then known as the ‘Boulevard of Crime’.

title: Joanna
creator: Feliks Falk
desc: Drama inspired by true events. In occupied Kraków, a lonely woman hides a small Jewish girl and pays a terrible price. She shelters the child from the Gestapo and her neighbours in the Old Town, among its courtyards and churches.

title: Man of Marble (Człowiek z marmuru)
creator: Andrzej Wajda
desc: Andrzej Wajda’s landmark. A film student digs up the buried story of a 1950s Stakhanovite bricklayer, a hero and then a non-person in Stalinist Poland. Plac Centralny is the main square of Nowa Huta, the steel town built beside Kraków to remake it.

title: Kontroll
creator: Nimród Antal
desc: Thriller with black humour, shot entirely in the real Budapest metro: ticket inspectors, a killer, and a man who won’t go above ground. Deák Ferenc tér, the central station where the lines cross, is the hub of its underground world.

title: Anthropoid
place: Church of Sts Cyril and Methodius, Resslova
creator: Sean Ellis
desc: The true story of the Czech parachutists who killed Nazi ruler Heydrich in 1942, and their last stand, shot in Prague at the real sites. They made that stand in the crypt of the Church of Sts Cyril and Methodius on Resslova Street.

title: Loners (Samotáři)
creator: David Ondříček
desc: Ensemble film about seven lonely young Praguers around the millennium, their aimless lives colliding by chance. Post-communist twenty-somethings. They drift through the bars and flats of Vinohrady and Žižkov, neighbouring districts east of the centre.

title: The Emperor and the Golem (Císařův pekař – Pekařův císař)
creator: Martin Frič
desc: A much-loved 1951 comedy set in Rudolf II’s Prague: an emperor obsessed with alchemy, a baker who is his double, and a clay Golem coming to life. Jan Werich plays both roles. Prague Castle was the emperor’s court of astronomers and charlatans.

title: Revanche
creator: Götz Spielmann
desc: An ex-con working in a Vienna brothel plans a bank robbery in the country to free the Ukrainian sex worker he loves. It goes fatally wrong. Tense, then rural. Alex and Tamara’s life together begins on the Gürtel, the ring road and nightlife strip.

title: Woman in Gold
creator: Simon Curtis
desc: The true story of refugee Maria Altmann’s fight to recover Klimt’s golden portrait of her aunt, looted by the Nazis in 1938. Helen Mirren stars. The painting hung for decades in the Upper Belvedere, a palace museum, before it was returned.

title: The Tunnel (Der Tunnel)
creator: Roland Suso Richter
desc: Based on a real 1961 escape: a former swimmer digs under the new Wall to get his sister out of the East. Tense, and largely true. On Bernauer Straße the Wall split houses; the Berlin Wall Memorial there now stands over the tunnel routes.

title: One, Two, Three
creator: Billy Wilder
desc: Billy Wilder’s fast Cold War farce. A Coca-Cola boss in West Berlin panics when his boss’s daughter marries a communist. The Wall went up mid-shoot. His characters keep crossing the sector line at the Brandenburg Gate.

title: Cabaret
creator: Bob Fosse
desc: Liza Minnelli sings in a seedy club as the Nazis rise outside, from Isherwood’s Weimar Berlin. The dread is in the songs. Filmed on sets. Nollendorfplatz, a square in Schöneberg, was the heart of the gay and cabaret scene Isherwood lived in.

title: Burke & Hare
creator: John Landis
desc: John Landis’s dark comedy about the real 1828 killers who smothered victims and sold the bodies to Edinburgh’s anatomy schools. Simon Pegg and Andy Serkis. The pair worked the closes of the Grassmarket and West Port, in the Old Town.

title: Filth
creator: Jon S. Baird
desc: James McAvoy as a corrupt Edinburgh detective falling apart, scheming for promotion through a haze of drugs and cruelty. Irvine Welsh, unfiltered. Between crime scenes and pubs he prowls the wintry, festive Old Town. Bleak and crude.

title: The Prime of Miss Jean Brodie
creator: Ronald Neame
desc: Maggie Smith’s Oscar-winning role as a magnetic, dangerous 1930s Edinburgh teacher who moulds her favourite girls and admires the fascists. From Muriel Spark. The Meadows, a park on the south side, sits in the world of the city’s proper girls’ schools.

title: Plato’s Academy (Akadimia Platonos)
creator: Filippos Tsitos
desc: A xenophobic Athens shopkeeper is thrown when his mother recognizes an Albanian labourer as her son. A sly comedy about Greek identity. It unfolds in Akadimia Platonos, a working-class district named after Plato’s ancient school.

title: The Hand of God (È stata la mano di Dio)
creator: Paolo Sorrentino
desc: Paolo Sorrentino’s autobiographical film. A Naples teenager, obsessed with football in the Maradona years, is orphaned by a tragedy and drawn toward cinema. The Stadio Maradona in Fuorigrotta is where Maradona played after his 1984 arrival.

title: Gomorrah (Gomorra)
creator: Matteo Garrone
desc: Matteo Garrone’s film of the Camorra in pieces: waste dumping, couture sweatshops, teenage foot soldiers. No glamour and no escape. From Saviano’s book. The Vele di Scampia, crumbling sail-shaped housing blocks, became the clans’ fortress.

title: The Four Days of Naples (Le quattro giornate di Napoli)
creator: Nanni Loy
desc: A recreation of four real days in September 1943, when Neapolitans, street children included, rose up and drove the Germans out. The uprising was fought house to house through the barricaded alleys of the historic centre.

title: Fados
creator: Carlos Saura
desc: Carlos Saura’s staged concert film of fado, Lisbon’s music of longing, or saudade, from Amália to Mariza, with Cape Verdean and Brazilian threads. Mouraria, a poor old quarter, is where fado and its first legend, Maria Severa, were born.

title: Os Verdes Anos (The Green Years)
creator: Paulo Rocha
desc: The founding film of Portuguese New Cinema. A country boy comes to early-1960s Lisbon to work as a cobbler and falls for a maid, as the modern city sours his hopes. Alvalade, a planned district of new apartment blocks, stands for the growing capital.

title: Blancanieves
creator: Pablo Berger
desc: A silent, black-and-white Snow White reset in 1920s Andalusia, where the heroine becomes a bullfighter. Strange and beautiful. The Maestranza, Seville’s grand bullring, is the stage of Carmen’s triumph and downfall.

title: Flamenco
creator: Carlos Saura
desc: Carlos Saura’s showcase of flamenco: thirteen forms, sung, played and danced by its leading artists on a bare stage. He filmed it inside the old Plaza de Armas station in Seville, then an empty railway terminus.

title: Take the Ball, Pass the Ball
creator: Duncan McMath
desc: Documentary on how Guardiola’s 2008–2012 Barcelona side became perhaps the best football team ever, told by the players. A break from the heavier films. Camp Nou, the club’s stadium, is where they perfected tiki-taka before crowds near 100,000.

title: Salvador (Puig Antich)
creator: Manuel Huerga
desc: Daniel Brühl plays Salvador Puig Antich, a real young Barcelona anarchist executed by garrotte in 1974, the last such execution in Spain. La Model, the panopticon prison where he was held and killed, is now open as a memorial.

title: Florence and the Uffizi Gallery
creator: Luca Viotto
desc: A 4K tour of Renaissance Florence and its greatest gallery, narrated as Lorenzo de’ Medici, from Botticelli to Brunelleschi’s dome. The Uffizi was built as the Medici’s offices and became the world’s first modern museum.

title: Amici miei (My Friends)
creator: Mario Monicelli
desc: Mario Monicelli’s classic. Four middle-aged Florentine men stave off despair with elaborate pranks, in thick local dialect. Funny and cruel. At Santa Maria Novella, the main railway station, they slap passengers leaning out of departing trains.

title: May God Save Us (Que Dios nos perdone)
creator: Rodrigo Sorogoyen
desc: Two mismatched detectives hunt a killer of elderly women across Madrid in 2011, during the crisis, the 15-M protests and a papal visit. Tense and sweaty. The Puerta del Sol is the central square the indignados occupied that summer.

title: What Have I Done to Deserve This? (¿Qué he hecho yo para merecer esto!)
creator: Pedro Almodóvar
desc: Pedro Almodóvar’s breakthrough. An exhausted cleaner, hooked on pills, cracks up amid a grotesque family in a cramped flat by the motorway. They live in the ‘Colmena’ tower blocks of La Concepción, a working-class area beside the M-30 ring road.

title: Romanzo Criminale
creator: Michele Placido
desc: The rise and fall of the real Banda della Magliana, the gang that ran Rome’s underworld from the 1970s into the ’80s, tangled up with terrorism and the state. The crew took its name from Magliana, a district in the south of the city.

title: Bend It Like Beckham
creator: Gurinder Chadha
desc: A Sikh teenager in West London defies her parents to play football. A warm crowd-pleaser about growing up between two cultures. Her family home is in Hounslow, a suburb under the Heathrow flight path.

title: Naked
creator: Mike Leigh
desc: Mike Leigh’s bleak night walk: a clever, cruel drifter from Manchester rants his way across a cold London after dark. David Thewlis in the lead. Hard going. He crashes and roams the small hours in Dalston, in the East End.

title: The King’s Speech
creator: Tom Hooper
desc: The true story of the stammering George VI and the unorthodox Australian who coached him through a wartime broadcast. Colin Firth and Geoffrey Rush. Lionel Logue’s real speech-therapy rooms were at 33 Portland Place, a street in Marylebone.

title: Sid and Nancy
creator: Alex Cox
desc: Alex Cox’s raw account of Sex Pistols bassist Sid Vicious and Nancy Spungen, from London squalor to a New York overdose. Grim. The 100 Club, a basement venue on Oxford Street, is where London punk was born.

title: Virgin Mountain (Fúsi)
creator: Dagur Kári
desc: Dagur Kári’s film about Fúsi, a large, shy middle-aged man who still lives with his mother in suburban Reykjavík and slowly reaches toward a first connection. His small life is set in outer housing estates like Breiðholt.

title: Edvard Munch
creator: Peter Watkins
desc: Peter Watkins’s docudrama about the young Munch in 1880s Kristiania, making ‘The Scream’ out of illness, grief and a disapproving bourgeois city. He grew up in Grünerløkka, a working-class quarter, among the deaths that recur in his art.

title: The Man on the Roof (Mannen på taket)
creator: Bo Widerberg
desc: Police procedural. After a sadistic cop is murdered, Martin Beck hunts a sniper across Stockholm, ending in a helicopter shootout. A national hit. The rooftop gunman turns Odenplan, a square in Vasastan, into a battlefield.

title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo (Män som hatar kvinnor)
creator: Niels Arden Oplev
desc: The original Swedish film of Stieg Larsson’s thriller. A journalist and the hacker Lisbeth Salander dig into a decades-old disappearance. Blomkvist’s flat is at Bellmansgatan 1, a Gothic-looking building on Södermalm that fans still visit.

title: Stockholm Bloodbath
creator: Mikael Håfström
desc: A gory revenge adventure set around the 1520 massacre, when the Danish king executed scores of Swedish nobles. Rough history, rougher film. The killings happened in Stortorget, the main square of Gamla Stan, the Old Town.

title: Pusher
creator: Nicolas Winding Refn
desc: Refn’s debut follows a Copenhagen drug dealer over one week as his debts close in. Handheld and shot on real streets. In the 1990s Istedgade, a street in Vesterbro, was the red-light and heroin strip the film moves through.

title: The Bombardment (Skyggen i mit øje)
place: Site of the Institut Jeanne d’Arc school, Frederiksberg Allé
creator: Ole Bornedal
desc: In 1945 the RAF bombed the Gestapo’s Copenhagen headquarters and, by mistake, a school full of children. A true story, and hard to watch. The school was the Institut Jeanne d’Arc, a French school on Frederiksberg Allé. The site is now apartments.

title: Rosie
creator: Paddy Breathnach
desc: Written by Roddy Doyle. A Dublin mother and her four kids live in their car after their landlord sells up, phoning B&Bs for a bed. The housing crisis, up close. Gardiner Street, on the northside, is a strip of emergency lodgings.

title: The General
place: Oxford Road and Charleston Road junction, Ranelagh
creator: John Boorman
desc: Brendan Gleeson plays Martin Cahill, the Dublin crime boss who robbed and taunted the state until the IRA shot him in 1994. True, and morally slippery. He was killed at the junction of Oxford Road and Charleston Road in Ranelagh.

title: The Commitments
creator: Alan Parker
desc: Northside Dublin kids form a soul band because ‘the Irish are the blacks of Europe.’ Alan Parker’s film of Roddy Doyle’s novel, loud and broke. The band comes out of the north inner city, the working-class streets north of the Liffey.

title: Paper Lives (Kağıttan Hayatlar)
creator: Can Ulkay
desc: A homeless, ailing waste-paper collector takes in a lost boy from the streets of poor Istanbul. Sentimental, but rooted in the city’s margins. The collectors scrape a living in Kasımpaşa, a hard hillside district above the Golden Horn.

title: Somersault in a Coffin (Tabutta Rövaşata)
creator: Derviş Zaim
desc: Derviş Zaim’s debut. A homeless man on the Bosphorus shore steals a car each night to keep warm and returns it by dawn. Based on a real drifter. He sleeps rough by Rumeli Hisarı, the 15th-century fortress on the water.

title: Crossing the Bridge (The Sound of Istanbul)
creator: Fatih Akın
desc: Fatih Akın’s music documentary goes around Istanbul looking for its sound: fasıl and rock, Roma clarinet, rap and the last great voices. It keeps coming back to the Galata Bridge over the Golden Horn, with its fishermen and street players.

title: Oslo, August 31st (Oslo, 31. august)
creator: Joachim Trier
desc: Joachim Trier’s film about a single day. A recovering addict on leave from rehab drifts through Oslo, deciding whether to keep living. Anders revisits the cafés, parks and old friends’ flats of central Oslo.

title: Les Misérables
creator: Ladj Ly
desc: Ladj Ly’s debut feature. A day with a police anti-crime unit in a banlieue east of Paris tips toward disaster. It takes Hugo’s title and updates his anger. Ly grew up on the Bosquets estate in Montfermeil and filmed it there.

title: Le Samouraï
creator: Jean-Pierre Melville
desc: Jean-Pierre Melville’s cold noir. Alain Delon is a lone hitman in trench coat and fedora, hunted through Paris after a job goes wrong. Widely imitated. The long cat-and-mouse chase runs through Châtelet, the big métro interchange.

title: The 400 Blows (Les Quatre Cents Coups)
creator: François Truffaut
desc: Truffaut’s semi-autobiographical film about a neglected Paris boy drifting toward reform school. It launched the New Wave. Young Antoine Doinel skips school and roams Pigalle, the streets between Clichy and Montmartre.

title: The Lovers on the Bridge (Les Amants du Pont-Neuf)
creator: Leos Carax
desc: Two homeless drifters make the Pont-Neuf their home while it is closed for repairs during the 1989 bicentennial. Leos Carax’s big, feverish romance. They sleep, drink and dance on Paris’s oldest bridge, over the Seine.

title: Grounding: The Last Days of Swissair
creator: Michael Steiner & Tobias Fueter
desc: Drama about the 2001 collapse of Swissair, the ‘flying bank’ and a symbol of Swiss reliability, when its fleet was literally grounded. A national trauma. The stranded planes sat at Zurich Airport in Kloten.

title: Schindler’s List
creator: Steven Spielberg
desc: Spielberg’s account of Oskar Schindler, who saved 1,100 Jews from the Kraków ghetto and the Płaszów camp. The ghetto was liquidated from Plac Bohaterów Getta, a square in Podgórze. It is now a memorial of empty chairs.

title: The Double Life of Veronique (La Double vie de Véronique)
creator: Krzysztof Kieślowski
desc: Kieślowski’s mystery about a Kraków choir soprano and her French double, who share an unspoken bond across Europe. Half the film is Polish. In Rynek Główny, the city’s main market square, Weronika glimpses her other self.

title: The Witness (A tanú)
creator: Péter Bacsó
desc: A bumbling dyke-keeper is pushed through the absurd show-trial politics of 1950s Hungary. Banned for a decade, now the country’s favorite satire of communism. Very funny. The Parliament building on the Danube stands for the regime it mocks.

title: The Piano Teacher (La Pianiste)
creator: Michael Haneke
desc: Michael Haneke’s film with Isabelle Huppert as a repressed piano professor, ruled by her mother, who falls into a cruel affair with a student. Cold and unsparing. Its world is Vienna’s classical music scene, centred on the Musikverein concert hall.

title: Christiane F. (Wir Kinder vom Bahnhof Zoo)
creator: Uli Edel
desc: The true account of a 13-year-old sliding into heroin in 1970s West Berlin, with a David Bowie score. Hard to watch. Bahnhof Zoo, the big train station by the zoo, is where she and other kids bought drugs and sold themselves.

title: The Lives of Others (Das Leben der Anderen)
creator: Florian Henckel von Donnersmarck
desc: A Stasi officer bugs a playwright’s flat in 1984 East Berlin and slowly changes sides. Fiction, but the surveillance was real and everywhere. The Stasi Museum in Lichtenberg is the secret police’s own headquarters, left as it was.

title: Downfall (Der Untergang)
creator: Oliver Hirschbiegel
desc: Bruno Ganz plays Hitler’s last ten days in the bunker as the Red Army closes in, drawn from his secretary’s memoir. Airless and exact. The Führerbunker site on Gertrud-Kolmar-Straße is now a car park with one plain information board.

title: The Illusionist (L’Illusionniste)
creator: Sylvain Chomet
desc: Sylvain Chomet’s wordless animated film: a fading French magician and a girl who believes in him, in a hand-drawn 1950s Edinburgh. He wanders the Royal Mile, the Old Town’s main street, drawn in close detail.

title: Hallam Foe
creator: David Mackenzie
desc: Coming-of-age story. A grieving boy runs away to Edinburgh, spies on the city from its rooftops and follows a woman who looks like his mother. He makes his hideout in the clock tower of the Balmoral Hotel, above Princes Street.

title: Trainspotting
creator: Danny Boyle
desc: Danny Boyle’s adaptation of Irvine Welsh. Renton and his mates chase heroin and waste their youth in early-1990s Edinburgh. Leith, the docks district, is their world; the opening chase runs down Princes Street.

title: Never on Sunday (Pote tin Kyriaki)
creator: Jules Dassin
desc: Melina Mercouri plays a Piraeus prostitute who puts straight an earnest American who wants to ‘improve’ her. It made her a star, and its song won an Oscar. Ilya’s world is the port of Piraeus, its dockside tavernas and its free Sundays.

title: Passione
creator: John Turturro
desc: John Turturro’s documentary on Neapolitan song and its Arab, African and Spanish roots, sung around the city by living performers. The Lungomare at Santa Lucia is the seafront that gave its name to the best-known Neapolitan serenade.

title: Il resto di niente
creator: Antonietta De Lillo
desc: The short-lived Parthenopean Republic of 1799, told through Eleonora Pimentel Fonseca, the noblewoman hanged when the Bourbons crushed Naples’s brief democracy. Its leaders were executed in Piazza del Mercato, the old market square.

title: The Gold of Naples (L’oro di Napoli)
creator: Vittorio De Sica
desc: Vittorio De Sica’s six stories of Naples: Sophia Loren as a pizza seller, Totò bullied by a squatter, a count who gambles. The street life spills across Spaccanapoli, the straight street that cuts through the old town.

title: Night Train to Lisbon
creator: Bille August
desc: A Swiss teacher follows the author of a strange book to Lisbon and uncovers a resistance cell from the Salazar years. In English and seen through a tourist’s eyes, but sincere. The red 25 de Abril Bridge over the Tagus was once named after Salazar himself.

title: Grupo 7 (Unit 7)
creator: Alberto Rodríguez
desc: Crime drama based on real events. Four brutal undercover cops ‘clean up’ Seville’s drugs and prostitution in the years before the 1992 Expo changed the city. They work over the Alameda de Hércules, a long square that was then seedy.

title: Alatriste
creator: Agustín Díaz Yanes
desc: Viggo Mortensen as a tired swordsman for hire as Spain’s Golden Age empire declines. Long and sprawling. Seville appears as the port for the Indies. The treasure fleets left for the Americas from the docks by the Torre del Oro, a tower on the Guadalquivir.

title: Biutiful
creator: Alejandro González Iñárritu
desc: Iñárritu’s Barcelona is not the postcard one. Javier Bardem plays a dying fixer among undocumented street sellers and sweatshops. Fiction, but the migrant city is the real subject. Santa Coloma de Gramenet is an immigrant suburb on the city’s edge.

title: La ciutat cremada (The Burnt City)
creator: Antoni Ribas
desc: The first Catalan-language film after Franco. A bourgeois family is caught up in the 1909 Tragic Week, when workers burned convents and the army fired back. Much of the revolt burned in El Raval, a district of the old town.

title: Hannibal
creator: Ridley Scott
desc: Ridley Scott’s sequel finds Lecter in Florence as a museum curator, stalked by a local detective. A thriller, shot in the real city. Lecter haunts the Palazzo Vecchio, the town hall, and the detective’s killing is staged from it.

title: Light in the Piazza
creator: Guy Green
desc: An American mother tours 1950s Florence with her beautiful daughter, who has a brain injury, and the girl falls for a local man. The mother has to decide what to reveal. They spend their days around Piazza del Duomo, under Brunelleschi’s dome.

title: Mid-August Lunch (Pranzo di Ferragosto)
creator: Gianni Di Gregorio
desc: A small, gentle comedy. A broke middle-aged Roman ends up looking after four elderly ladies over the empty Ferragosto holiday. His cramped flat and the market where he shops for the meal are in Trastevere, the old quarter by the river.

title: Barrio
creator: Fernando León de Aranoa
desc: Three broke teenagers get through a hot summer on the poor edge of Madrid while everyone with money leaves town. Clear-eyed. Their small lives are stuck in Orcasitas, a district of housing estates in the south of the city.

title: Tesis (Thesis)
creator: Alejandro Amenábar
desc: Amenábar’s debut thriller. A film student researching snuff videos finds the trail leads into her own Madrid university. She hunts a killer among the faculty at the Complutense, on the Ciudad Universitaria campus, where it was filmed.

title: Death of a Cyclist (Muerte de un ciclista)
creator: Juan Antonio Bardem
desc: A wealthy professor and his married lover run down a worker and drive off, and guilt eats into their comfortable world. A sly 1955 jab at Franco’s bourgeoisie. That class lives in the Salamanca district, Madrid’s moneyed grid of streets.

title: Non essere cattivo (Don’t Be Bad)
creator: Claudio Caligari
desc: Two friends chase highs and quick money through the drugs and wreckage of Ostia in 1995. Claudio Caligari’s last film, made as he was dying. Lido di Ostia is Rome’s rough seaside suburb, where the pair burn out.

title: Il Sorpasso (The Easy Life)
creator: Dino Risi
desc: A brash charmer pulls a shy student out of a deserted August Rome on a reckless road trip. A high point of Italian-style comedy, with a hard ending. The ride starts on Via Veneto, an avenue emptied for Ferragosto.

title: Bicycle Thieves (Ladri di biciclette)
creator: Vittorio De Sica
desc: De Sica’s neorealist film. A man who hangs posters and his young son search postwar Rome for the stolen bike his job depends on. Sad and plain. They look for it at Porta Portese, the Sunday flea market where stolen bikes were broken up for parts.

title: Attack the Block
creator: Joe Cornish
desc: A teenage gang in South London defends its council estate from alien invaders on Bonfire Night. John Boyega’s debut. The estate is the real star, and the tower-block London the film turns into a battlefield is Kennington.

title: London
creator: Patrick Keiller
desc: Patrick Keiller’s essay film. A narrator and his unseen friend walk through London in 1992, thinking about its history and decline while the camera studies its streets. The South Bank of the Thames is one stop on their wandering.

title: The Long Good Friday
creator: John Mackenzie
desc: Bob Hoskins plays a London gangster whose empire comes apart over one Easter weekend, just as he bets everything on redeveloping the derelict docks. St Katharine Docks, the marina by Tower Bridge, is the waterfront he hopes to cash in.

title: The Elephant Man
creator: David Lynch
desc: David Lynch’s black-and-white film about Joseph Merrick, the gentle, badly deformed man a Victorian surgeon took from a freak show. A true story. He was given a home at the Royal London Hospital in Whitechapel, where his skeleton is still kept.

title: Life in a Fishbowl (Vonarstræti)
creator: Baldvin Zophoníasson
desc: Three Reykjavík lives cross in 2006, the year before the crash: a banker, a teacher and single mother who turns to sex work, and a drunk writer. The title is Vonarstræti, ‘Hope Street’, a street by the city pond.

title: Reykjavík-Rotterdam
creator: Óskar Jónasson
desc: Smuggling thriller. A broke Reykjavík security guard agrees to one more run of contraband booze by sea. Later remade in Hollywood as ‘Contraband’. The ships, and the temptation, come in at the Old Harbour, Reykjavík’s working port.

title: 22 July
creator: Paul Greengrass
desc: Paul Greengrass’s sober account of the 2011 far-right attacks in Norway: a bombing, a massacre, a trial. True, and hard to watch. Breivik’s car bomb went off in the Government Quarter, the ministry buildings in central Oslo.

title: Stockholm
creator: Robert Budreau
desc: Ethan Hawke plays the bungling robber in the 1973 bank hold-up whose hostages took his side, the case that named ‘Stockholm syndrome’. True story. The six-day siege at Kreditbanken on Norrmalmstorg, a square in central Stockholm, gripped Sweden.

title: Italian for Beginners (Italiensk for begyndere)
creator: Lone Scherfig
desc: Dogme comedy about grieving, lonely Copenhageners who find each other at a night-school Italian class. Plain and quietly hopeful. The characters live in Hvidovre, a modest suburb southwest of the city.

title: A Royal Affair (En kongelig affære)
creator: Nikolaj Arcel
desc: True 1770s scandal. A British-born queen and the royal physician Struensee take power behind a mad king and push through Enlightenment reforms, until the court strikes back. With Mads Mikkelsen. That court sat at Christiansborg Palace.

title: Once
creator: John Carney
desc: A Dublin busker and a Czech immigrant make music together over one week and almost fall in love. Tiny budget; its song won an Oscar. He plays for coins on Grafton Street, the pedestrian shopping street in the city centre.

title: The Dead
creator: John Huston
desc: John Huston’s last film, from Joyce’s story. At a 1904 Twelfth Night dinner, small talk gives way to a wife’s buried grief. Quiet and sad. Joyce set it at 15 Usher’s Island, a quayside house where his aunts lived, now a Joyce landmark.

title: Distant (Uzak)
creator: Nuri Bilge Ceylan
desc: Ceylan’s Cannes winner. A jaded Istanbul photographer resents the cousin from the country sleeping on his couch, in a near-silent, snowbound city. Slow. His apartment is in Cihangir, a hillside neighbourhood in Beyoğlu above the frozen Bosphorus.

title: Eşkıya (The Bandit)
creator: Yavuz Turgul
desc: The film credited with reviving Turkish cinema. A bandit freed after 35 years comes to 1990s Istanbul to find the man who betrayed him. Şener Şen stars. He ends up lost in Tarlabaşı, a run-down backstreet district in Beyoğlu.

title: Topkapi
creator: Jules Dassin
desc: Jules Dassin’s heist comedy: a gang plots to steal an emerald dagger from the sultan’s treasury, filmed at the real monuments. At Topkapı Palace, the Ottoman sultans’ seat, the thieves lower a man into the jewel room from the roof.

title: Les Barons (The Barons)
creator: Nabil Ben Yadir
desc: Comedy about young Moroccan-Belgian men in Brussels who believe life is a fixed ration of steps, so the less you move, the longer you live. The idle ‘barons’ hold court in Molenbeek and Saint-Josse, Brussels’ North African neighbourhoods.

title: La Haine
place: Cité de la Noé estate, Chanteloup-les-Vignes
creator: Mathieu Kassovitz
desc: The day after a riot, three friends, Arab, African and Jewish, kill time on a bleak housing estate and then in a hostile central Paris. The defining film of the banlieue. It was shot at the Cité de la Noé, an estate in Chanteloup-les-Vignes.

title: Cléo from 5 to 7 (Cléo de 5 à 7)
creator: Agnès Varda
desc: Agnès Varda follows a pop singer in near real time as she wanders Paris, waiting for a cancer test result and slowly starting to see the city. Her two hours pass in the Left Bank streets and cafés of Montparnasse, around Rue Daguerre.

title: Paris 1900
creator: Nicole Védrès
desc: Documentary assembled from archive film of Belle Époque Paris, 1900 to 1914: the Exposition, the boulevards, the last years before the war. The Eiffel Tower, built for the 1889 exhibition, stands over the city it shows.

title: 33 Scenes from Life (33 sceny z życia)
creator: Małgorzata Szumowska
desc: Szumowska’s autobiographical drama. A Kraków artist watches both her parents die within months as her marriage frays. Unsentimental and hard. Julia’s comfortable life comes apart in Kazimierz, the old Jewish district now favoured by artists.

title: Gloomy Sunday (Ein Lied von Liebe und Tod)
creator: Rolf Schübel
desc: A doomed love triangle in a 1930s Budapest restaurant, built around ‘Gloomy Sunday’, Rezső Seress’s real song linked to suicides. Seress played it at Kispipa, an actual restaurant on Akácfa utca in the old Jewish Quarter.

title: Fateless (Sorstalanság)
creator: Lajos Koltai
desc: From Imre Kertész’s novel. A 14-year-old is deported from Budapest to the camps and comes back unable to explain it. Mostly set in Auschwitz and Buchenwald, not the city. The real deportations left from Józsefváros Station, a Budapest railway station.

title: Kolya (Kolja)
creator: Jan Svěrák
desc: Oscar winner. A womanizing Prague cellist ends up looking after a small Russian boy in 1988, shortly before the Velvet Revolution. The two make a home in Malá Strana, the Lesser Town quarter below Prague Castle.

title: Pelíšky (Cosy Dens)
creator: Jan Hřebejk
desc: Tragicomedy of two feuding families, one communist and one not, sharing a Prague apartment block through the 1968 Prague Spring and the tanks that ended it. Much loved at home. The block is an apartment house in Vinohrady, a residential district.

title: Museum Hours
creator: Jem Cohen
desc: A guard at the Kunsthistorisches Museum befriends a Canadian visitor, and the film moves between Bruegel’s paintings and Vienna’s winter streets. Quiet and slow. The two meet in the museum, the imperial art palace on the Ringstrasse.

title: Before Sunrise
creator: Richard Linklater
desc: Linklater’s romance: two strangers get off a train and walk and talk through one Vienna night until dawn parts them. Shot all over the city. One stop on their walk is the Kleines Café, a small café on Franziskanerplatz.

title: A Dangerous Method
creator: David Cronenberg
desc: Cronenberg on the birth of psychoanalysis: Freud, Jung and the patient between them, in the buttoned-up Vienna of 1900. Talky and cool. Freud saw patients at Berggasse 19, his real consulting rooms, now the Sigmund Freud Museum.

title: Good Bye, Lenin!
creator: Wolfgang Becker
desc: Around 1989, a son pretends East Germany still exists inside his mother’s bedroom so the news won’t kill her. Funny and sad. The world he tries to preserve is Karl-Marx-Allee, the monumental GDR boulevard in Friedrichshain.

title: B-Movie: Lust & Sound in West-Berlin
creator: Jörg A. Hoppe, Klaus Maeck & Heiko Lange
desc: Archive documentary on West Berlin’s underground from 1979 to 1989: Bowie, Nick Cave, punk, squats, told by scene fixer Mark Reeder. Lighter than most on this list. SO36, a club in Kreuzberg, was at the center of it and still is.

title: Race
creator: Stephen Hopkins
desc: True story of Jesse Owens winning four gold medals at the 1936 Berlin Olympics as Hitler watched, a Black athlete puncturing a propaganda show. He ran in the Olympiastadion, the Nazi-built stadium still in use today.

title: Aimée & Jaguar
creator: Max Färberböck
desc: The true love story between a Nazi officer’s wife and a Jewish woman hiding in wartime Berlin. Felice Schragenheim was real; she died in the camps. The film is set around Bayerischer Platz, a square at the heart of Schöneberg’s Jewish quarter.

title: Greyfriars Bobby
creator: Don Chaffey
desc: Disney’s version of Edinburgh’s most sentimental legend: a Skye terrier who guarded his master’s grave for 14 years in the 1860s. Bobby kept his vigil in Greyfriars Kirkyard, a churchyard in the Old Town; his small statue stands by the gate.

title: Festival
creator: Annie Griffin
desc: Black comedy set at the Edinburgh Fringe: comedians, luvvies and a nervous playwright collide during the world’s biggest arts festival. Filmed from inside the August crush of flyers and street acts on the Royal Mile, the Old Town’s main street.

title: The Ogre of Athens (O Drakos)
creator: Nikos Koundouros
desc: A meek bank clerk is mistaken for a wanted gangster in this 1950s Greek noir, expressionist and fatalist, nearly banned on release. The anonymous, fearful city that swallows him is downtown Athens around Omonia Square.

title: Naples Millionaire (Napoli milionaria)
creator: Eduardo De Filippo
desc: Eduardo De Filippo, the master of Neapolitan theatre, films his own play: a family’s café gets through the war on the black market and can’t survive the peace. They live in the Quartieri Spagnoli, a tight grid of poor alleys in central Naples.

title: Così parlò Bellavista
creator: Luciano De Crescenzo
desc: Gentle comedy. A retired Neapolitan professor lectures a manager transferred from the north on how to actually live. Pure 1970s Naples wit. Bellavista holds court on the Vomero, a hill district of middle-class apartment blocks.

title: Lisbon Story
creator: Wim Wenders
desc: Wim Wenders sends a sound man to record Lisbon for a friend’s unfinished film. The result is a love letter to the city, with fado-tinged music by Madredeus. He chases sounds up the stairways of Alfama, the old quarter crossed by trams.

title: Recordações da Casa Amarela (Recollections of the Yellow House)
creator: João César Monteiro
desc: Monteiro’s grubby, funny film about a broke, lecherous lodger scheming and decaying in a cheap boarding house. Deliberately vile; not for everyone. He prowls between flophouse and street in the Bairro Alto, a faded old quarter of Lisbon.

creator: Susana de Sousa Dias
desc: Documentary made only from mugshots of political prisoners and survivors’ voices recalling Salazar’s secret police. The title is the dictatorship’s 48 years. The Museu do Aljube, a former political prison in Lisbon, now remembers them.

title: Polígono Sur (Seville, Southside)
place: Las Tres Mil Viviendas, Polígono Sur (area)
creator: Dominique Abel
desc: Documentary on the flamenco of Las Tres Mil Viviendas, Seville’s poorest and most stigmatized estate and one of the genre’s living roots. In the Polígono Sur housing project, old Triana Gitano families and new fusions meet.

title: Solas
creator: Benito Zambrano
desc: Zambrano’s drama: a beaten-down Seville woman and her visiting elderly mother find some grace in a grim city apartment. Hard but kind. They live in a working-class barrio near the Macarena, far from the postcard center.

title: Antonio Gaudí
creator: Hiroshi Teshigahara
desc: Teshigahara’s near-wordless documentary looks at Gaudí’s Barcelona buildings with a sculptor’s eye, set to Takemitsu’s score. No lecture. His organic forms are easiest to walk through in Park Güell, a mosaic-tiled park on a hill.

title: Marathon
creator: Carlos Saura
desc: Carlos Saura’s official film of the 1992 Barcelona Olympics, built around the marathon, which finished with a climb up Montjuïc. A city remaking itself for the world. The Games opened and closed at the Estadi Olímpic Lluís Companys, on Montjuïc.

title: The Photographer of Mauthausen (El fotógrafo de Mauthausen)
creator: Mar Targarona
desc: Francesc Boix, a Barcelona communist held in a Nazi camp, smuggled out negatives; his photos later helped convict war criminals. A true story, set in Austria, not the city. Boix grew up in Poble-sec, a working-class district below Montjuïc.

title: A Room with a View
creator: James Ivory
desc: E.M. Forster’s Edwardian tourists lose their English reserve in Florence: a faint in a piazza, a stolen kiss, a room facing the Arno. Merchant Ivory cleared Piazza della Signoria, the city’s main square, to film the scene where Lucy faints.

title: Tea with Mussolini
creator: Franco Zeffirelli
desc: Zeffirelli’s boyhood memories: eccentric English and American women raise an orphan in 1930s Florence, then defy the Fascists to save its art. Their Florence centres on the basilica of Santa Croce; the fresco-rescue finale was filmed in San Gimignano.

title: The Great Beauty (La grande bellezza)
creator: Paolo Sorrentino
desc: Sorrentino’s Oscar winner, an heir to La Dolce Vita: a jaded writer drifts through the rooftop parties and ruins of present-day Rome. The film opens at the Fontana dell’Acqua Paola, a large fountain on the Gianicolo hill overlooking the city.

title: The Silence of Others (El silencio de otros)
creator: Almudena Carracedo & Robert Bahar
desc: Oscar-shortlisted documentary following victims of Franco’s dictatorship as they fight Spain’s official forgetting and sue for justice decades later. Many of those executed after the war lie in La Almudena, Madrid’s main cemetery.

title: The Day of the Beast (El día de la bestia)
creator: Álex de la Iglesia
desc: A priest, a metalhead and a TV psychic try to stop the birth of the Antichrist in Madrid at Christmas. Gory, funny and very local. The finale plays out on the KIO Towers, the pair of leaning office towers at Plaza de Castilla.

title: Surcos (Furrows)
creator: José Antonio Nieves Conde
desc: Neorealist drama: a peasant family moves to 1950s Madrid and is ground down by black-market hustlers and tenement poverty. Unusually honest for Franco’s Spain. Newcomers like them crowded into Lavapiés, an inner-city quarter.

title: Caro Diario (Dear Diary)
creator: Nanni Moretti
desc: In the first chapter of his film diary, Nanni Moretti rides his Vespa through a summer-empty Rome, admiring neighbourhoods tourists don’t see. He lingers over Garbatella, a garden suburb of low houses south of the centre.

title: La Dolce Vita
creator: Federico Fellini
desc: Fellini follows a gossip journalist through seven nights in 1960 Rome, and Anita Ekberg wades into a fountain. The film gave us the word ‘paparazzo’. That scene was shot in the Trevi Fountain, the large baroque fountain in central Rome.

title: Amy
creator: Asif Kapadia
desc: Asif Kapadia’s Oscar-winning documentary on Amy Winehouse, built from home footage, follows her from teenage talent to public destruction. She made Camden Town, the north London market-and-pub district, her own; her statue stands there now.

title: My Beautiful Laundrette
creator: Stephen Frears
desc: Thatcher’s London, seen through a British-Pakistani man and his white ex-punk lover, who open a glamorous launderette. A landmark for Stephen Frears and Hanif Kureishi. Their business and romance take root in Vauxhall, in South London.

title: Pride
creator: Matthew Warchus
desc: True story of London gay activists who raised money for striking miners in 1984, and the unlikely friendship that followed. Lesbians and Gays Support the Miners really met at Gay’s the Word, a bookshop in Bloomsbury.

title: Screaming Masterpiece (Gargandi snilld)
creator: Ari Alexander Ergis Magnússon
desc: Documentary on Iceland’s outsized music scene: Björk, Sigur Rós, the Sugarcubes, múm, and the small capital that keeps producing them. Much of it lives in the clubs and venues of 101 Reykjavík, the downtown district.

title: Max Manus (Man of War)
creator: Joachim Rønning & Espen Sandberg
desc: True story of Max Manus, Norway’s best-known WWII saboteur, and the Oslo Gang, who blew up German ships in the harbour during the occupation. They mined the docks below Akershus Fortress, where captured comrades were shot.

title: The Bothersome Man (Den brysomme mannen)
creator: Jens Lien
desc: Jens Lien’s deadpan satire of Scandinavian comfort. A man arrives in a bland, pleasant city where nothing satisfies and no one bleeds. The glassy new waterfront district of Bjørvika is the frictionless Oslo it mocks.

title: Waltz for Monica (Monica Z)
creator: Per Fly
desc: Biopic of jazz singer Monica Zetterlund, from a provincial town to New York and fame, fighting sexism and drink along the way. Partly rural, but the music is Stockholm’s. Its jazz golden age played at Nalen, a concert hall on Regeringsgatan.

title: The Square
creator: Ruben Östlund
desc: Ruben Östlund’s Palme d’Or satire about a Stockholm museum curator and the art world’s hollow virtue, told in one awkward scene after another. It moves through Kungsträdgården, the central park by the Royal Palace. Interiors were shot in Gothenburg.

title: Another Round (Druk)
creator: Thomas Vinterberg
desc: Four burnt-out Copenhagen teachers test the theory that a steady daytime buzz makes life better. Sad and funny, and it ends on a dance. They walk the city out along the Lakes, the chain of long lakes curving round the city centre.

title: The Human Scale
creator: Andreas Dalsgaard
desc: Documentary on architect Jan Gehl’s idea that cities should be built for people, not cars, with Copenhagen as the proof. It covers other cities too. Gehl helped make Strøget, the long shopping street through the old centre, car-free in 1962.

title: Flame & Citron (Flammen og Citronen)
creator: Ole Christian Madsen
desc: Two real Danish resistance fighters assassinate collaborators in occupied Copenhagen until they can no longer tell who deserves it. Morally grey and based on fact. Executed resistance fighters are buried at Mindelunden, a memorial park in Ryvangen.

title: Adam & Paul
creator: Lenny Abrahamson
desc: Two heroin addicts from Ballymun drift across Dublin over one grim, oddly funny day, chasing a fix. Close to Beckett. Their aimless loop through the city centre takes them over the Ha’penny Bridge, the old iron footbridge on the Liffey.

title: Veronica Guerin
place: Site of Veronica Guerin’s murder, Naas Road
creator: Joel Schumacher
desc: Cate Blanchett as the crime reporter murdered in 1996 for her stories on Dublin’s drug lords. A true story; her killing changed Irish law. A gunman shot her at a red light at a junction on the Naas Road, now a motorway.

title: My Left Foot
creator: Jim Sheridan
desc: Daniel Day-Lewis as Christy Brown, a working-class Dubliner born with cerebral palsy who learned to paint and write with one foot. A true story, told without sentiment. The Browns raised their large family in Crumlin, a southside housing estate.

title: Salkım Hanımın Taneleri (Mrs. Salkım’s Diamonds)
creator: Tomris Giritlioğlu
desc: Drama about the 1942 Wealth Tax, when Istanbul’s Greeks, Armenians and Jews were taxed into ruin and shipped to labour camps. True history, long taboo. It destroyed the minority merchants of Beyoğlu, the city’s cosmopolitan quarter.

title: Hababam Sınıfı (The Chaos Class)
creator: Ertem Eğilmez
desc: Turkey’s best-loved comedy, endlessly rerun. A class of hopeless students wages gentle war on their teachers at a private Istanbul school. The school is an old mansion in Çengelköy, a neighbourhood in the hills on the Asian shore of the Bosphorus.

title: Illegal (Illégal)
creator: Olivier Masset-Depasse
desc: An undocumented Russian mother is seized and held in a Belgian removal centre while she fights deportation. Hard to watch. The film shows from inside the closed detention centres near Steenokkerzeel, on the edge of Brussels.

title: Brussels by Night
creator: Marc Didden
desc: A landmark of Flemish cinema. A drifter roams a grey 1980s Brussels at night, running into strangers and their bottled-up frustrations. It wanders the bleak boulevards and bars of the city centre after dark.

title: JCVD
creator: Mabrouk El Mechri
desc: Jean-Claude Van Damme plays a washed-up version of himself, caught in a hostage siege at a post office in his native Brussels. More moving than you’d expect. The film takes him back to Schaerbeek, the commune where he grew up.

title: Amélie (Le Fabuleux Destin d’Amélie Poulain)
place: Café des Deux Moulins, Rue Lepic
creator: Jean-Pierre Jeunet
desc: Jean-Pierre Jeunet’s fairytale of a shy Montmartre waitress who secretly arranges small kindnesses for others. A deliberately storybook Paris. She works at the Café des Deux Moulins, a real café on Rue Lepic.

title: Sarah’s Key (Elle s’appelait Sarah)
place: Vél’ d’Hiv memorial, Quai de Grenelle
creator: Gilles Paquet-Brenner
desc: A journalist uncovers the story of a girl caught in the 1942 Vél’ d’Hiv roundup, when French police delivered 13,000 Jews to the Nazis. That part is history. A memorial on the Seine at Quai de Grenelle stands where the winter velodrome was.

title: French Cancan
creator: Jean Renoir
desc: Jean Renoir’s Technicolor romance about how the Moulin Rouge and its scandalous cancan began in 1890s Montmartre, a fond look at Belle Époque show business. The real Moulin Rouge, the windmill cabaret, still stands on Place Blanche.

title: Der Kreis (The Circle)
creator: Stefan Haupt
desc: Docudrama about Der Kreis, a pioneering postwar gay club and magazine in Zurich, through a 1958 love affair and the 1960s crackdown that broke it. Its discreet world was in the lanes of the Niederdorf, part of the old town.

title: Züri brännt (Zurich Is Burning)
creator: Videoladen Zürich
desc: Raw video record of the 1980 youth revolt. The city funded an opera renovation but not a youth centre, and Zurich filled with tear gas. The millions spent on the Opernhaus, the city’s opera house, set off the riots.

title: Vinci
creator: Juliusz Machulski
desc: Juliusz Machulski’s heist comedy: two thieves plan to swap Leonardo’s ‘Lady with an Ermine’ for a fake, straight off the museum wall. Fond of old Kraków. The real painting belongs to the Czartoryski Museum, which the caper targets.

title: White God (Fehér isten)
creator: Kornél Mundruczó
desc: A mongrel dog is dumped on the street and leads a citywide dog uprising through Budapest. A fable about who gets discarded, staged in the real city. The pack pours across Liberty Bridge, the green iron bridge over the Danube.

title: Diary for My Children (Napló gyermekeimnek)
creator: Márta Mészáros
desc: Márta Mészáros’s autobiographical film. An orphan returns to Stalinist Budapest and watches the terror that took her father close in on her. The House of Terror museum at Andrássy út 60 was the real secret-police HQ, Arrow Cross then communist.

title: Sunset (Napszállta)
creator: László Nemes
desc: László Nemes follows a young milliner through Budapest in 1913, the Habsburg city a year from catastrophe. Beautiful, menacing and disorienting. Its lost world parades past the State Opera, the opera house on Andrássy Avenue.

title: Citizen Havel (Občan Havel)
creator: Pavel Koutecký & Miroslav Janek
desc: Documentary shot over 13 years of Václav Havel’s presidency: the dissident playwright learning to run a country, camera always rolling. After 1989 the reluctant president moves into Prague Castle, the seat of power above the city.

title: Kafka
creator: Steven Soderbergh
desc: Steven Soderbergh’s black-and-white thriller: an insurance clerk named Kafka is drawn into a conspiracy in a shadowy 1919 Prague. Shot in the real city. The lanes of the Old Town, around Old Town Square, stand in for the writer’s oppressive Prague.

title: The Third Man
creator: Carol Reed
desc: Graham Greene and Carol Reed’s noir about racketeering in bombed Vienna under four-power occupation, with zither music and tilted camera angles. Harry Lime gives his ‘cuckoo clock’ speech on the Riesenrad, the giant Ferris wheel in the Prater park.

title: Sissi
creator: Ernst Marischka
desc: The 1955 fairytale of teenage Elisabeth becoming empress of Austria. Romy Schneider’s breakout, and comfort viewing across the German-speaking world. It was filmed at Schönbrunn Palace, the Habsburg residence where the real Sissi lived.

title: Wings of Desire (Der Himmel über Berlin)
creator: Wim Wenders
desc: Wim Wenders’ angels drift over a divided Berlin, listening to people’s lonely thoughts, and one wants to become human. The city and the Wall are the real subject. An angel perches on the Siegessäule, the Victory Column with its golden statue.

title: Bridge of Spies
creator: Steven Spielberg
desc: Steven Spielberg’s true Cold War story: an American lawyer negotiates the 1962 exchange of a Soviet spy for a downed US pilot. The handover took place on the Glienicke Bridge over the Havel, which the press called the Bridge of Spies.

title: Rosenstraße
creator: Margarethe von Trotta
desc: In 1943, German women stood in the street for days until the Gestapo released their Jewish husbands. The protest happened, though historians dispute the film’s telling. A sculpture, the Block der Frauen, marks the spot on Rosenstraße.

title: Berlin: Symphony of a Great City (Die Sinfonie der Großstadt)
creator: Walther Ruttmann
desc: Walther Ruttmann edits a single 1927 day, from factories and crowds to trams and nightfall, into rhythm with no plot. A record of a city the war later flattened. The camera keeps returning to Alexanderplatz, the busy central square.

title: Sunshine on Leith
creator: Dexter Fletcher
desc: Jukebox musical built on the Proclaimers’ songs. Two soldiers back from Afghanistan pick up their Edinburgh lives and loves, breaking into song. The romances and reunions play out on The Shore, the harbourside street in Leith.

title: Boy Eating the Bird’s Food
creator: Ektoras Lygizos
desc: A jobless young man goes hungry through three days of austerity Athens, sharing his last crumbs with his canary. Spare and raw, drawn from Hamsun’s ‘Hunger.’ He drifts among the dense apartment blocks of Kypseli, a crowded residential district.

title: Nostalgia
creator: Mario Martone
desc: Pierfrancesco Favino plays a man who returns after 40 years to his poor old Naples quarter and is drawn, fatally, toward a boyhood friend now a Camorra boss. Mario Martone’s mournful film. The quarter is the Rione Sanità, dense and devout.

title: Fortapàsc
creator: Marco Risi
desc: True story of Giancarlo Siani, a young reporter the Camorra shot dead in 1985 for his exposés. Naples as a war zone. He was gunned down in his car outside his home in the Vomero, a hillside district above the centre.

title: Hands over the City (Le mani sulla città)
place: Palazzo San Giacomo (city hall), Piazza Municipio
creator: Francesco Rosi
desc: Francesco Rosi’s angry political drama. After a tenement collapse kills residents, a developer (Rod Steiger) and his council allies carve up Naples for profit. The speculation is voted through at the city hall, Palazzo San Giacomo on Piazza Municipio.

title: Colossal Youth (Juventude em Marcha)
creator: Pedro Costa
desc: Pedro Costa’s slow, austere docufiction. Ventura, an ageing Cape Verdean labourer, moves between a condemned immigrant slum and a bleak new estate. Demanding. The estate is Casal da Boba, a rehousing project in Amadora on Lisbon’s edge.

title: Sangue do Meu Sangue (Blood of My Blood)
creator: João Canijo
desc: A single mother and her sister try to shield two kids from drugs and worse over one week on a Lisbon housing estate. Raw and operatic. It is set and shot in Bairro Padre Cruz, a large social-housing quarter in Carnide.

title: Capitães de Abril (April Captains)
creator: Maria de Medeiros
desc: Drama of the near-bloodless 1974 coup that ended Europe’s longest dictatorship, told from the young officers’ tanks. Real people, real day. The dictator surrendered at Largo do Carmo, a small central square, as crowds put carnations in gun barrels.

title: Carmen
creator: Vicente Aranda
desc: Vicente Aranda’s period version of Mérimée’s Carmen, a Seville cigarette-maker whose passion destroys the soldier who loves her. She rolls cigars at the Real Fábrica de Tabacos, the huge royal tobacco factory that now houses the university.

title: Nadie conoce a nadie (Nobody Knows Anybody)
creator: Mateo Gil
desc: A crossword setter is drawn into a deadly game during Seville’s Holy Week, and the mystery spills into the processions. A slick, atmospheric thriller. Paranoia and pageantry meet on the Semana Santa route around the Cathedral.

title: Spanish Affair 2 (Ocho apellidos catalanes)
creator: Emilio Martínez-Lázaro
desc: Hit comedy: a Basque man fakes Catalan roots for love, poking every stereotype about independence and identity. Silly, but the divisions are real. Plaça de Sant Jaume, a square in the Gothic Quarter, holds the Catalan government and city hall.

title: Land and Freedom
creator: Ken Loach
desc: Ken Loach follows a British volunteer into the Civil War militias, then into the 1937 street fighting between Republican factions. History arguing with itself. The May Days began at the Telefónica building on Plaça de Catalunya, the main square.

title: Paisà (Paisan)
creator: Roberto Rossellini
desc: Rossellini’s neorealist film of Italy’s 1944 liberation, in six episodes. In Florence, a nurse crosses the battle-torn city to find her partisan. She runs through the Vasari Corridor, the raised passage over the Ponte Vecchio, to cross the Arno.

title: Cronaca familiare (Family Diary)
creator: Valerio Zurlini
desc: Two Florentine brothers raised apart are reunited as one is dying. Valerio Zurlini’s quiet film, with Marcello Mastroianni, won the Golden Lion. It walks the Arno embankments around the Ponte Santa Trinita, a Renaissance bridge in the centre.

title: Sacro GRA
creator: Gianfranco Rosi
desc: Gianfranco Rosi’s Golden Lion-winning documentary circles the Grande Raccordo Anulare, Rome’s 68-km ring road, and the odd, quiet lives at its edges. The motorway loop frames a modern Rome most visitors never see.

title: Truman
creator: Cesc Gay
desc: An actor dying of cancer spends a few last days in Madrid with his visiting best friend and his dog, settling his affairs with grace and humour. Their unhurried winter goodbye plays out in Chamberí, a central residential district.

title: El verdugo (The Executioner)
creator: Luis García Berlanga
desc: Berlanga’s pitch-black comedy. A meek Madrid undertaker marries an executioner’s daughter and is trapped into taking over the job. A film against the death penalty. His ordinary life runs through the old city around the Plaza Mayor, the main square.

title: Goya’s Ghosts
creator: Miloš Forman
desc: Miloš Forman’s costume drama of Goya’s Madrid: the painter caught between the Inquisition, a wronged muse and Napoleon’s 1808 invasion. Uneven. The real Goyas the film draws on hang in the Prado, the city’s great art museum.

title: Mamma Roma
creator: Pier Paolo Pasolini
desc: Pasolini, with Anna Magnani as a former prostitute trying to reach respectability in the raw new estates on Rome’s edge, while her son slips away. The ancient aqueducts of the Parco degli Acquedotti loom over the borgata she moves to.

title: Roman Holiday
creator: William Wyler
desc: A runaway princess and an American reporter spend a day of stolen freedom touring Rome, in the film that made the city’s monuments romantic. Audrey Hepburn eats her gelato on the Spanish Steps, the long stairway above Piazza di Spagna.

title: The Agony and the Ecstasy
creator: Carol Reed
desc: Charlton Heston as Michelangelo fights Rex Harrison’s warrior pope over the Sistine Chapel ceiling, 1508–1512. Dated but handsome. Almost the whole film is spent on that four-year job, painting the chapel’s vault in the Vatican.

title: Shaun of the Dead
creator: Edgar Wright
desc: Edgar Wright’s zombie comedy. A slacker tries to win back his girlfriend and save his mum as the dead rise across suburban North London. Very funny, very English. He shuffles to the pub through Crouch End, a leafy North London neighbourhood.

title: Blow-Up
creator: Michelangelo Antonioni
desc: Michelangelo Antonioni’s puzzle set in 1966 Swinging London. A fashion photographer thinks his photos caught a murder in a quiet park. The park is Maryon Park in Charlton, south-east London, where he takes and later enlarges the fatal shot.

title: Suffragette
creator: Sarah Gavron
desc: A working laundress in the East End is drawn into the militant fight for women’s votes in 1912: arrests, hunger strikes, bombs. Grounded in real history. The campaign targeted the Houses of Parliament, and this was the first film ever shot inside them.

title: Twist and Shout (Tro, håb og kærlighed)
creator: Bille August
desc: Bille August’s coming-of-age film, set in 1963: two teenagers in Copenhagen’s suburbs, a Beatles-mad band, first love and a violent home. A big hit in Denmark. Brønshøj, where Bjarne Reuter, who wrote the novel, was born, stands in for that suburban world.

title: Tabu
creator: Miguel Gomes
desc: Miguel Gomes’ black-and-white film in two parts: a lonely woman in present-day Lisbon, then a doomed 1960s love affair in colonial Africa. Only the first half is in the city. In it, the neighbour Pilar joins a protest in the Rossio, Lisbon’s main square.

title: It Happened in Broad Daylight (Es geschah am hellichten Tag)
creator: Ladislao Vajda
desc: Thriller from a Dürrenmatt script: a Zurich police inspector keeps hunting a child-killer past his retirement. Later remade as ‘The Pledge’. Exteriors were shot outside the city. The Polizeikaserne was Zurich’s cantonal police headquarters, 1901–2022.

title: I Served the King of England (Obsluhoval jsem anglického krále)
creator: Jiří Menzel
desc: Jiří Menzel’s Hrabal adaptation. A small, ambitious waiter climbs through Prague’s grand hotels across the century’s upheavals, serving everyone and keeping nothing. He finds work at the Hotel Paříž, the Art Nouveau hotel by the Municipal House.

title: Variações (Variações: Guardian Angel)
creator: João Maia
desc: Biopic of António Variações, a barber turned genre-bending pop star in early-1980s Lisbon, who died of AIDS in 1984. Crowd-pleasing. In 1979 he opened his own barbershop, É Pró Menino e Prá Menina, on Rua de São José, off the Avenida da Liberdade.

title: Die Schweizermacher (The Swissmakers)
creator: Rolf Lyssy
desc: The most-watched Swiss film since records began in 1976. Two naturalization inspectors spy on foreigners who must prove they’re ‘Swiss enough’. A mild but sharp satire. No location is documented; the Stadthaus, seat of Zurich’s city government, stands in.

title: Palme
creator: Maud Nycander & Kristina Lindström
desc: Documentary on Olof Palme, the radical Swedish prime minister, loved and loathed, who was shot dead in 1986 while walking home from the cinema. He fell at the corner of Sveavägen and Tunnelgatan, a street corner in central Stockholm.

title: Rome, Open City (Roma città aperta)
creator: Roberto Rossellini
desc: Rossellini made this Resistance drama in Rome’s streets months after the Nazis left; a founding work of neorealism. Anna Magnani’s run after the truck and death was shot on Via Raimondo Montecuccoli, a residential street in the Prenestino district.

title: A Touch of Spice (Politiki Kouzina)
creator: Tassos Boulmetis
desc: A boy who grows up in Istanbul is expelled with his Greek family in 1964 and becomes an Athens astrophysicist who understands cooking better than living. Bittersweet. No Athens location is documented; Evripidou, the city’s spice-shop street, stands in.

title: Elling
creator: Petter Næss
desc: Oscar-nominated. Two men released from an institution learn to live together in a state-provided flat in Oslo, frightened of the world outside. No address for the flat is documented; Majorstuen, a residential district in central Oslo, stands in.

title: Gelin (The Bride)
creator: Lütfi Ö. Akad
desc: Lütfi Akad’s film about migration. An Anatolian family moves to Istanbul to make money in trade and lets the shop matter more than a dying child. Zeytinburnu, a gecekondu district on the city’s edge, is the kind of quarter newcomers poured into.

title: A Special Day (Una giornata particolare)
creator: Ettore Scola
desc: On the day in 1938 that Hitler visits Rome, a housewife and a gay broadcaster facing exile meet in their empty apartment block as the city parades. Loren and Mastroianni, against type. It never leaves Palazzo Federici, a real Fascist-era housing complex.

title: Ammore e malavita (Love and Bullets)
place: Basilica of Santa Maria della Sanità
creator: Manetti Bros
desc: The Manetti Bros’ Camorra musical. A hitman spares the woman he once loved, and the clan war breaks into song and dance. Deliberately trashy and very Neapolitan. It opens, and ends, with a boss’s funeral shot at the Basilica of Santa Maria della Sanità.

title: The Cremator (Spalovač mrtvol)
creator: Juraj Herz
desc: A mild crematorium keeper in late-1930s Prague, drawn in by Nazi ideology, drifts toward murdering his own family. Juraj Herz’s film is full of dread. The murders were shot in a working Prague crematorium; Strašnice is the city’s main one.

title: Sagrada: The Mystery of Creation
creator: Stefan Haupt
desc: Quiet documentary on Gaudí’s basilica, still being built well over a century on, and the craftsmen and doubters finishing another man’s design. The Sagrada Família is the most-visited monument in Spain.

title: Carmina o revienta (Carmina or Blow Up)
creator: Paco León
desc: A comedy shot like a documentary. Carmina, 58, runs a roadside venta in Seville; robbed again and refused by the insurers, she hatches a scheme to get the money back. Paco León’s own mother plays her. No specific Seville location is documented.

title: The Brand New Testament (Le Tout Nouveau Testament)
creator: Jaco Van Dormael
desc: Van Dormael’s fantasy: God is a spiteful bureaucrat in a grubby Brussels flat, until his young daughter leaks everyone’s date of death and runs off into the city. The story puts God’s flat in Molenbeek; it was actually shot on a set in Luxembourg.

title: Volcano (Eldfjall)
creator: Rúnar Rúnarsson
desc: Rúnarsson’s quiet study of a grumpy Reykjavík school janitor who retires, then must care for his wife at home after a stroke leaves her disabled. The couple left Heimaey after the 1973 eruption. Set in residential Reykjavík; no exact location is known.

title: Daisies (Sedmikrásky)
creator: Věra Chytilová
desc: Věra Chytilová’s anarchic New Wave film. Two girls, both named Marie, decide the world is spoiled, so they will be too, and wreck meals and men across Prague. It was banned. Their destruction runs through the restaurants and streets of central Prague.

title: Under the Tree (Undir trénu)
creator: Hafsteinn Gunnar Sigurðsson
desc: Dark comedy about a feud between neighbours in a Reykjavík suburb, which turns deadly over a tree that shades the next-door patio. Shot in 1960s architect-designed houses the director found scouting Reykjavík and nearby towns; the street is not named.

title: The Dreamers
creator: Bernardo Bertolucci
desc: Bertolucci’s 1968. Three film lovers shut themselves in a flat playing erotic film games while revolution breaks out outside. It opens with a restaging of the real protest at the Cinémathèque in the Palais de Chaillot, cut with 1968 newsreel. Explicit sex.

title: Man Bites Dog (C’est arrivé près de chez vous)
creator: Belvaux, Bonzel & Poelvoorde
desc: Black comedy in mockumentary form. A film crew follows a charming, talkative serial killer and slides into complicity. Very violent. It grew out of Rémy Belvaux’s student project at INSAS, the Brussels film school, and was partly shot in Namur.

title: Hope (Håp)
creator: Maria Sødahl
desc: Maria Sødahl’s semi-autobiographical drama. An Oslo theatre director gets a terminal diagnosis days before Christmas and has to look again at her long marriage. Their search for someone to talk to leads to the hospice at Lovisenberg.

title: Welcome in Vienna
creator: Axel Corti
desc: The last part of Axel Corti’s exile trilogy. Two émigrés return to Vienna in 1945 as US soldiers and find a broken, still antisemitic city. Their idealism sours. Stephansplatz is the central square, whose cathedral burned in the last days of the war.

title: Racer and the Jailbird (Le Fidèle)
creator: Michaël R. Roskam
desc: Michaël R. Roskam’s crime romance. A Brussels gangster (Matthias Schoenaerts) and a racing driver (Adèle Exarchopoulos) fall hard as his double life closes in. Shot in Brussels at no documented spot; Avenue Louise stands in for its moneyed world.

title: Headhunters (Hodejegerne)
creator: Morten Tyldum
desc: Jo Nesbø thriller. A corporate headhunter pays for his lifestyle by stealing art, until one of his marks turns on him. Shot around Oslo at no documented spot; the glassy Aker Brygge waterfront stands in for its world of money.

title: La Vie en Rose (La Môme)
creator: Olivier Dahan
desc: Marion Cotillard won an Oscar as Édith Piaf, from a childhood spent partly in a brothel to world fame and ruin. Legend says Piaf was born on the pavement of Rue de Belleville; a plaque at no. 72 marks it, on the working-class hill in northeast Paris.

title: Ecumenopolis (City Without Limits)
place: Ayazma, beside the Atatürk Olympic Stadium
creator: Imre Azem
desc: Angry documentary on Istanbul consuming itself: bulldozed neighbourhoods, evicted families, endless towers, a mega-city sprawling past any limit. Among its cases is Ayazma, a western neighbourhood cleared by force and handed to TOKİ for luxury housing.

title: Dog Days (Hundstage)
creator: Ulrich Seidl
desc: Ulrich Seidl’s unsparing mosaic of lonely, cruel lives during a heatwave in Vienna’s bland suburbs. Hard to watch. Seidl set it in Vösendorf and Wiener Neustadt rather than Vienna proper, and shot it in the flat country just south of the city.

title: The Ear (Ucho)
creator: Karel Kachyňa
desc: Banned for 20 years. A Party official and his wife come home from a dinner and slowly realize their Prague villa is bugged and he may be next in the purge. The evening’s reception was at Prague Castle, shown in ominous flashbacks.

title: Vitus
creator: Fredi M. Murer
desc: A Zurich piano prodigy fakes his way back to an ordinary boyhood, with Bruno Ganz as his grandfather. The closing sequence, Vitus playing Schumann’s piano concerto as soloist, was shot in the Tonhalle, during a real concert.

title: Woman at War (Kona fer í stríð)
creator: Benedikt Erlingsson
desc: Wry eco-thriller. A Reykjavík choir conductor secretly sabotages the power lines that feed the aluminium industry, then showers the city with leaflets. Austurvöllur, the protest square by parliament, stands for the politics she takes on.

title: Black
creator: Adil El Arbi & Bilall Fallah
desc: A Congolese girl and a Moroccan boy from rival Brussels street gangs fall in love. A brutal, doomed Romeo and Juliet by the directors later behind the Bad Boys films. Scenes were shot in Matongé’s Galerie d’Ixelles, the arcade with murals.

title: Germany Year Zero (Germania anno zero)
creator: Roberto Rossellini
desc: Rossellini shot a boy wandering the real rubble of Berlin in 1947, before it ends in one of cinema’s bleakest scenes. In the bombed-out shell of St. Matthäus-Kirche, Edmund stops to listen to organ music.

title: Hamam (Steam: The Turkish Bath)
creator: Ferzan Özpetek
desc: Ferzan Özpetek’s drama. An uptight Italian inherits a crumbling Istanbul bathhouse, and while restoring it he is changed by the city and a forbidden love. The film doesn’t name the district; Balat’s old back lanes are the kind it moves through.

title: Together (Tillsammans)
creator: Lukas Moodysson
desc: Moodysson’s comedy about a Stockholm commune in 1975, where misfits argue over politics, meat and marriage. Warm and funny. It was shot in western Sweden; the collective’s house stands for a Stockholm villa suburb like Bromma.

title: Dogtooth (Kynodontas)
creator: Yorgos Lanthimos
desc: Lanthimos’s breakout: parents keep their grown children behind a garden wall, with invented words and rules. Disturbing, with explicit scenes. It launched the Greek Weird Wave. The film never names its suburb; walled villas like those of Marousi fit.

title: Aloys
creator: Tobias Nölle
desc: A lonely private detective, adrift after his father’s death, is drawn into an imaginary world by a stranger’s phone game. Eerie. Its housing estate was shot in Bern, but a few scenes were filmed at Stettbach station, on Zurich’s eastern edge.

title: Restless Natives
creator: Michael Hoffman
desc: 1980s caper comedy: two bored lads from Wester Hailes in joke-shop masks hold up Highland tourist coaches from a motorbike and become folk heroes. Its motorbike chase was shot through the Old Town and ends on Princes Street.

title: Blue My Mind
creator: Lisa Brühlmann
desc: A 15-year-old who has just moved to Zurich goes through a violent, secret bodily transformation as her sense of self comes apart. A hard coming-of-age film. It was shot at real Zurich locations, among them the Glattzentrum mall.

title: Walking with the Enemy
place: Shoes on the Danube Bank memorial
creator: Mark Schmidt
desc: In 1944 Budapest a young Jew steals an Arrow Cross uniform to pull others off the deportation lists. Based on the real Pinchas Rosenbaum. The Shoes on the Danube Bank memorial marks where the fascist militia shot Jews into the river.

title: Sunshine (A napfény íze)
creator: István Szabó
desc: István Szabó’s saga of three generations of a Jewish family who change their name to survive empire, fascism and communism. Assimilation buys no safety. Ralph Fiennes plays three men. The Chain Bridge is at the heart of their Budapest.

title: Children of Glory (Szabadság, szerelem)
creator: Krisztina Goda
desc: The 1956 uprising, told through the water polo team that then met the Soviets in Melbourne’s ‘Blood in the Water’ match. True events, with a patriotic gloss. Corvin köz, a courtyard passage, is where teenage fighters held off tanks.

title: The Last Days
creator: James Moll
desc: Oscar-winning documentary from Spielberg’s Shoah Foundation. Five Hungarian Jews recall 1944, when the Nazis deported over 400,000 in a matter of weeks, near the war’s end. The Dohány Street Synagogue stands at the edge of the wartime ghetto.

title: Miracle in Milan
creator: Vittorio De Sica
desc: Original title Miracolo a Milano. Vittorio De Sica’s postwar fable, written with Cesare Zavattini: a kind orphan leads a shantytown against a greedy landowner. It ends with the poor flying on broomsticks over Piazza del Duomo, the cathedral square.

title: Maria by Callas
creator: Tom Volf
desc: Tom Volf’s documentary tells soprano Maria Callas’s life in her own words, from interviews, letters and home movies. La Scala, Milan’s opera house, was the centre of her career in the 1950s, when she and director Luchino Visconti staged operas there.

title: Rocco and His Brothers
creator: Luchino Visconti
desc: Luchino Visconti’s drama about a widow and her five sons who move from the poor south to Milan during the 1950s boom. It runs nearly three hours. Its darkest scene was shot on the shore of the Idroscalo, a rowing lake by Linate airport.

title: La Notte
creator: Michelangelo Antonioni
desc: Michelangelo Antonioni follows a novelist (Marcello Mastroianni) and his wife (Jeanne Moreau) through a day and night as their marriage runs down. It opens on the glass face of Gio Ponti’s new Pirelli Tower skyscraper. It is slow by design.

title: Teorema
creator: Pier Paolo Pasolini
desc: Pier Paolo Pasolini’s allegory: a mysterious young guest (Terence Stamp) upends each member of a rich Milan factory owner’s family. The owner hands his factory to the workers and ends up stripping naked in Milano Centrale, the main railway station.
