title: The Execution of Lady Jane Grey by Paul Delaroche
desc: Delaroche’s 1833 painting of the nine-day queen’s death in 1554 was thought destroyed in a 1928 flood until it turned up rolled in storage. It is in the National Gallery on Trafalgar Square.

title: The Vision after the Sermon by Paul Gauguin
desc: Gauguin painted this Breton scene in 1888 at Pont-Aven, with a flat red field and the women’s vision of Jacob wrestling an angel. The Scottish National Gallery on the Mound bought it in 1925; this conversation unpacks its break with Impressionism.

title: The Book of Kells, an illuminated gospel book
place: Book of Kells, Old Library, Trinity College
desc: An illuminated gospel book made around 800, probably begun on the island of Iona and finished at Kells. It is kept in the Old Library at Trinity College Dublin, where a few pages are shown at a time.

title: The Cross of Cong, a 12th-century reliquary cross
desc: Made around 1123 for Turlough O’Connor, High King of Ireland, and kept for centuries at Cong in County Mayo. It is in the National Museum of Ireland’s archaeology building on Kildare Street.

title: The Shrine of Saint Patrick’s Bell
desc: The iron bell is said to have belonged to Saint Patrick; its bronze and gold shrine was made around 1100. Both are in the National Museum of Ireland’s archaeology building on Kildare Street.

title: The Ardagh Chalice
desc: Found in 1868 by two boys digging potatoes in a ringfort in County Limerick, the eighth-century Ardagh Chalice combines silver, gold filigree and enamel. It sits in the National Museum of Ireland’s archaeology building on Kildare Street.

title: The Coggalbeg Hoard, a gold lunula and two discs
desc: Ireland had rich gold sources in the Bronze Age, and smiths beat it into crescent collars, discs and torcs. The best of them are in the National Museum of Ireland’s archaeology building on Kildare Street.

title: The Coronation Mantle of Roger II of Sicily
desc: Made in Norman Palermo around 1133 for Roger II of Sicily, with an Arabic inscription along its hem, the mantle was later used to crown Holy Roman Emperors. It is in the Imperial Treasury in Vienna’s Hofburg palace.

title: The Venus of Willendorf, a 30,000-year-old figure
desc: This 11 cm figure, about 30,000 years old, was found in 1908 near Willendorf in the Danube valley. It is in the Natural History Museum on Vienna’s Maria-Theresien-Platz, opposite the art history museum.

title: Death and Life by Gustav Klimt
desc: Klimt’s large allegory, begun in 1910 and later reworked, sets a dark figure of Death against a colourful tangle of bodies. It is in the Leopold Museum in Vienna’s MuseumsQuartier.

title: The Great Piece of Turf by Albrecht Dürer
desc: Dürer’s 1503 watercolour of dandelions, grasses and plantain, studied at ground level. It belongs to the Albertina, the Habsburg palace museum in Vienna with one of the world’s great collections of drawings and prints.

title: The Hermits by Egon Schiele
desc: Schiele’s 1912 double portrait shows him and his mentor Klimt as robed hermits, pressed close together. It is in the Leopold Museum, which holds the world’s largest Schiele collection in Vienna’s MuseumsQuartier.

title: The Kiss by Gustav Klimt
desc: Klimt’s 1907–08 painting of an embracing couple, made with oil paint and gold leaf, and bought by the Austrian state in 1908. It hangs in the Upper Belvedere, the Baroque palace museum in Vienna.

title: The Tower of Babel by Pieter Bruegel the Elder
desc: Bruegel’s 1563 painting of the biblical tower, modelled partly on the Roman Colosseum and set beside a busy Flemish harbour. It hangs in the Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna’s imperial picture gallery on the Ringstrasse.

title: The Crucifixion Triptych by Rogier van der Weyden
desc: A small triptych from around 1440 by the Netherlandish painter Rogier van der Weyden, its three panels joined by a single landscape. It is in the Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna’s imperial picture gallery on the Ringstrasse.

title: Jupiter and Io by Correggio
desc: Correggio’s 1530s painting of Jupiter, hidden in a dark cloud, holding the nymph Io; it was one of a series on the god’s loves. Two art historians look at it in the Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna’s imperial picture gallery.

title: The Three Philosophers by Giorgione
desc: Giorgione’s Venetian painting from around 1509, whose three figures have been read as magi, philosophers or the ages of man. It is in the Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna’s imperial picture gallery on the Ringstrasse.

title: The Art of Painting by Johannes Vermeer
desc: Vermeer kept this painting until his death; Hitler later bought it for his planned museum in Linz. It hangs in the Kunsthistorisches Museum on Maria-Theresien-Platz.

title: The Vienna Genesis, an illustrated sixth-century Bible
desc: A sixth-century Greek manuscript of Genesis on purple vellum, with silver text and painted scenes. It is held by the Austrian National Library at the Hofburg palace.

title: Self-Portrait in a Convex Mirror by Parmigianino
desc: Parmigianino painted this small self-portrait around 1524 on a convex wooden panel, his hand swelling in the foreground. It is in the Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna’s imperial picture gallery on the Ringstrasse.

title: Portrait of Wally by Egon Schiele
desc: Schiele painted his companion Wally Neuzil in 1912; seized at MoMA in 1998, it returned after a 2010 settlement with the heirs of its prewar owner. It is in the Leopold Museum in the MuseumsQuartier.

title: The Peasant Wedding by Pieter Bruegel the Elder
desc: Bruegel’s 1567 wedding scene: porridge carried on a door, bagpipers and a bride beneath a paper crown. It hangs in the Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna’s imperial picture gallery on the Ringstrasse.

title: Seated Male Nude (Self-Portrait) by Egon Schiele
desc: Egon Schiele was twenty when he painted this gaunt self-portrait in 1910, with no hands or feet. It belongs to the Leopold Museum in the MuseumsQuartier, which holds the world’s largest collection of his work.

title: The Last Judgment by Hieronymus Bosch
place: Academy of Fine Arts picture gallery, Schillerplatz
desc: Hieronymus Bosch’s Last Judgment triptych fills its central panel with demons, torture machines and sinners. It hangs in the picture gallery of the Academy of Fine Arts on Schillerplatz, an art school that also famously rejected the young Hitler.

title: The Beethoven Frieze by Gustav Klimt
desc: Made for a 1902 exhibition honouring Beethoven, the frieze traces humanity’s longing for happiness through monsters, nudes and a final embrace. It survives in the basement of the Secession, the white exhibition hall with a gilded laurel dome.

title: Saint Sebastian by Andrea Mantegna
desc: Andrea Mantegna’s small panel sets the martyr against crumbling classical architecture and signs it in Greek. It belongs to the Kunsthistorisches Museum, the imperial picture gallery built on the Ringstrasse in the 1880s.

title: The Hunters in the Snow by Pieter Bruegel the Elder
desc: Pieter Bruegel’s 1565 snowscape of weary hunters, skaters and a village below hangs in the Kunsthistorisches Museum, the Habsburg art museum on the Ring, which owns the largest group of his paintings anywhere.

title: Moon (And It Went Like)
creator: Kid Francescoli
desc: Dreamy, slow-building electronica with a teenage-summer ache, sung by Julia Minkin. Kid Francescoli is Mathieu Hocine’s Marseille project; the tiny Vallon des Auffes fishing cove stands in for its coastal reverie.

title: The Hooligan’s Return
creator: Norman Manea
desc: A Romanian-Jewish writer returns in 1997 to the Bucharest he fled — a childhood in the Transnistria camps, the communist years, exile — in a brilliant memoir of belonging. He walks the old streets of the centre, at once home and unhomely.

title: The History of the Jewish Ghetto in Florence: A Walking Tour with Context
creator: Context Travel
desc: A history walk tracing 500 years of Florentine Jewish life, from Renaissance banking to WWII persecution. From a tower near Ponte Vecchio, it passes camp-victim stones and a synagogue that survived the Nazis and a flood, ending at the Jewish museum.

title: Athens Below the Surface: A Walking Tour of the Podoniftis Stream
creator: Georges Xyftilis
desc: A hidden-waterways walk through the northern suburbs: trace a buried stream through overlooked neighborhoods, meeting a cave-dwelling priest along the way.

title: East of Eden: Tales from the Thames Riverbank
creator: Steve Matthews
desc: A history walk along the Limehouse and Wapping stretch of the Thames, tracing 450 years of dockside stories. From Westferry, it passes a pub where Raleigh set sail for the New World and a young Dickens sang on a table for pennies, ending near Tower Bridge.

title: From Righteous to Wretched: A Clerkenwell Tale
creator: Steve Matthews
desc: A history walk through a district that thrived as a lawless enclave, then sank into a poor slum. From Farringdon, it passes the Marx Memorial Library and a Victorian gas-lamp linked by telegraph to Scotland Yard, ending at Smithfield Market.

title: A Greenwich Tour: Where Time Begins
place: Island Gardens park, Isle of Dogs
creator: Brian Cookson
desc: A history walk through Greenwich, crossing under the Thames via a century-old foot tunnel to the Royal Observatory and Meridian Line. From Island Gardens, it passes where Raleigh laid his cloak over a puddle for Elizabeth I, ending near Greenwich Park.

title: The City through the Centuries
creator: Sam Brearley
desc: A history walk through the City of London tracing 2,000 years of Roman, medieval, and modern layers. It passes a civic hall over a Roman amphitheater, a hidden temple to an eastern god, and where the 1666 fire began, ending near the riverside fortress.

title: The Victorian City
creator: Judith Flanders
desc: Victorian London as an ordinary person met it: the traffic, the food sellers, the mud, the funerals. Flanders builds it street by street. Covent Garden was the great market, and it ran through the night.

title: Rise Up, Women!
creator: Diane Atkinson
desc: The suffragettes chained themselves to railings, smashed windows, burned buildings, and were force-fed in prison for it. Atkinson tells it through the women themselves. Millicent Fawcett’s statue stands in Parliament Square.

title: Charles Dickens: A Life
creator: Claire Tomalin
desc: The best life of Dickens: a boy sent to a blacking factory who never got over it, and a famous man who treated his wife appallingly. The Charles Dickens Museum on Doughty Street is the only one of his London houses left.

title: London: The Biography
creator: Peter Ackroyd
desc: London told as a living body rather than a timeline: its smells, riots, drunks, and fires, chapter by chapter. It is long and you can dip in. Ackroyd keeps returning to the City, the square mile where the Romans first built.

title: The Five
creator: Hallie Rubenhold
desc: Five women murdered in 1888, and this is a book about them rather than about him: who they were, how they ended up sleeping outside. It changed the story completely. Whitechapel is where they lived and died.

title: The Splendid and the Vile
creator: Erik Larson
desc: Churchill’s first year, told through the Blitz, his family, and the people around him. Larson makes documented history read like a novel. The Churchill War Rooms, underground off Whitehall, are exactly as they were left in 1945.

title: Empireland
creator: Sathnam Sanghera
desc: Britain built the largest empire in history and then mostly stopped talking about it. Sanghera looks at what’s left in the streets, the museums, and the arguments. The British Museum is where much of the loot ended up.

title: Black and British: A Forgotten History
creator: David Olusoga
desc: Black British history is not recent: it runs back to Roman soldiers, and through slavery, empire, and the Windrush. Olusoga is superb and hard to argue with. Windrush Square in Brixton is named for the 1948 ship.

title: The Ghost Map
creator: Steven Johnson
desc: In 1854 cholera killed hundreds around one Soho street in days. A doctor mapped the deaths and worked out it was the water, not the air. There’s a replica pump on Broadwick Street, and a pub named after him next to it.

title: Underground, Overground: A Passenger’s History of the Tube
creator: Andrew Martin
desc: How the Tube got built, by whom, and why the lines are such a mess. Funny, nerdy, and it improves every journey you take. Baker Street opened in 1863 and is the oldest underground station still running.

title: The Great Stink of London
creator: Stephen Halliday
desc: In 1858 the Thames stank so badly Parliament nearly fled, so an engineer built 1,300 miles of sewers under the city. They still work. The Victoria Embankment is Bazalgette’s; he built the road on top of the sewer he was hiding.

title: England’s Dreaming
creator: Jon Savage
desc: How punk happened: art school, boredom, unemployment, and a clothes shop on the King’s Road. The definitive book, written by someone who was there. 430 King’s Road was McLaren and Westwood’s shop, and it’s still a shop.

title: Show Me the Bodies: How We Let Grenfell Happen
creator: Peter Apps
desc: In 2017 a tower block caught fire and 72 people died, and the warnings had all been given. A housing journalist shows exactly how it was allowed to happen. Grenfell Tower still stands in North Kensington, wrapped and covered.

title: Down and Out in Paris and London
creator: George Orwell
desc: Orwell, broke on purpose, works as a dishwasher and sleeps in London’s doss houses, and reports back on what poverty actually costs. Short and clear. His London tramping was around the East End, out past Tower Hill.

title: Dr Johnson’s London
creator: Liza Picard
desc: Georgian London as it actually smelled: gin, sewage, wigs, and a man compiling a dictionary in an attic. Picard is fun and endlessly specific. Dr Johnson’s House on Gough Square is where he did it, and the attic is still there.

title: The Diary of Samuel Pepys
place: Monument to the Great Fire of London
creator: Samuel Pepys
desc: A naval bureaucrat writes down everything for nine years: the plague, the fire, his lechery, what he ate. Nobody has ever been this honest. He watched the Great Fire spread from Pudding Lane, where the Monument now stands.

title: Mrs Dalloway
creator: Virginia Woolf
desc: One June day in 1925, a woman walks across London to buy flowers and the whole city moves through her. Short, and the sentences are the point. Big Ben strikes through the book; she is heading from Westminster up to Bond Street.

title: Testaccio: The Hearth of Roman Food Tradition
creator: Luciana Squadrilli
desc: A neighbourhood food walk through a working-class Roman district. From under an ancient pyramid tomb, it winds past a covered market, a delicatessen, and trattorias famed for offal and cacio e pepe, ending on the main avenue toward the river.

title: History of the Jewish Ghetto in Rome: A Walking Tour with Context
creator: Context Travel
desc: An expert-led Jewish-history walk through the old ghetto and beyond. From a turtle fountain in a small square, it traces 300 years of confinement past the great synagogue, wartime memorials, and an ancient portico, crossing the river to Trastevere.

title: Death in Rome
creator: Robert Katz
desc: In 1944 partisans bombed an SS column, and the Germans shot 335 men and boys in a quarry in reprisal. Katz reconstructs both days, hour by hour. The Fosse Ardeatine is now a memorial on the site, and the caves are open.

title: Meditations
place: Column of Marcus Aurelius, Piazza Colonna
creator: Marcus Aurelius
desc: The private notebook of an emperor, telling himself to be calm, do his duty, and stop caring what people think. Short, and people still carry it around. His column stands in Piazza Colonna, carved with the wars he was fighting while writing it.

title: Rubicon
creator: Tom Holland
desc: How the Republic destroyed itself: Sulla, Pompey, Caesar, and a system that could not survive its own winners. It reads like a thriller. Caesar was stabbed at the Theatre of Pompey, now the sunken ruins at Largo di Torre Argentina.

title: SPQR
creator: Mary Beard
desc: A thousand years of Rome by the best-known Roman historian alive, who keeps asking how we know any of it. Sceptical, funny, and it never talks down. The Forum was the centre of everything: politics, law, gossip, and murder.

title: Rome: A History in Seven Sackings
creator: Matthew Kneale
desc: Rome told through the seven times it was sacked, from the Gauls to the Nazis. A brilliant structure, and each chapter rebuilds the city as it was that day. Porta San Sebastiano is a gate in the walls raised to keep the invaders out.

title: The Twelve Caesars
creator: Suetonius
desc: An imperial secretary’s dirt on the first twelve emperors: the poisonings, the perversions, the last words. Written in 121 AD, gossipy, and still enormous fun. The Palatine is the hill where they built their palaces.

title: Bernini: His Life and His Rome
creator: Franco Mormando
desc: Bernini made much of the Rome you photograph: the fountains, the colonnade, the sculpture. He also slashed his mistress’s face. Mormando refuses to tidy him up. His Four Rivers fountain stands in the middle of Piazza Navona.

title: Ancient Rome on Five Denarii a Day
creator: Philip Matyszak
desc: A guidebook to Rome in 200 AD: where to stay, what to eat, how to avoid being robbed, what the games are like. Silly, short, and it makes the ruins make sense. The Colosseum is where you’d have spent the afternoon.

title: Absolute Monarchs: A History of the Papacy
creator: John Julius Norwich
desc: Two thousand years of popes, most of them badly behaved. Norwich is a great storyteller and he does not pretend to be pious. St Peter’s is the seat of it all, built on what is said to be Peter’s grave.

title: Michelangelo and the Pope’s Ceiling
creator: Ross King
desc: Michelangelo was a sculptor who did not want the job, and he spent four years on his back arguing with a warrior pope. Short and gripping. The Sistine Chapel ceiling is what came out of it.

title: October 16, 1943
place: Jewish Ghetto, Via del Portico d’Ottavia
creator: Giacomo Debenedetti
desc: On 16 October 1943 the Germans emptied the Roman Ghetto in one morning. Debenedetti wrote this the following year, from the accounts of people who were there. It is about forty pages. The Portico d’Ottavia is the street it happened on.

title: Mussolini’s Rome
creator: Borden Painter
desc: Mussolini rebuilt Rome to look like an empire again, gutting old quarters to do it. The buildings are all still standing and mostly still in use. EUR is the district he built for a world’s fair that never happened.

title: Five Quarters: Recipes and Notes from a Kitchen in Rome
creator: Rachel Roddy
desc: An English writer cooks her way into a Roman neighbourhood: the pasta, the offal, the market ladies telling her she’s doing it wrong. Warm and useful. The Testaccio market is where she shops, and it’s still a real market.

title: The Italians
creator: Luigi Barzini
desc: An Italian explains the Italians to foreigners: the charm, the show, the deep distrust of the state, the reasons for all of it. Written in 1964 and still uncomfortably accurate. The Via Veneto was the street of the Dolce Vita.

title: Caravaggio: A Life Sacred and Profane
creator: Andrew Graham-Dixon
desc: Caravaggio painted the poor as saints, killed a man in a street fight, and died on the run at 38. The best art biography of recent years. Three of his masterpieces hang in San Luigi dei Francesi, exactly where he put them.

title: Royal Madrid: Scandal and Secrets from Puerta del Sol to the Palace
creator: Yohanna Lerman
desc: A history walk through royal scandal and hidden Madrid. From Puerta del Sol, it passes cloistered nuns who sell cookies through a hidden turnstile and the site of a 1906 anarchist attack on a royal wedding, via Plaza Mayor and the Royal Palace.

title: The Forging of a Rebel
creator: Arturo Barea
desc: A Madrid boy, poor, watches the old order rot and then blow up. His account of the city under siege in 1936 is the best thing written about it. Barea grew up around Lavapiés, the tight working-class streets south of the centre.

title: The Battle for Spain
creator: Antony Beevor
desc: The clearest account of the Spanish Civil War in English, and the least sentimental. Beevor is superb on the siege of Madrid. The front line ran through the Ciudad Universitaria, and students fought room to room in the faculty buildings.

title: Goya
place: San Antonio de la Florida Chapel
creator: Robert Hughes
desc: Goya went deaf, saw a war, and painted the worst things people do to each other. Hughes writes about him with fury and love. The Ermita de San Antonio de la Florida holds Goya’s own frescoes, and his body is buried under them.

title: The Vanishing Velázquez
creator: Laura Cumming
desc: A Victorian bookseller stakes everything on the claim that he has found a lost Velázquez. Around that, Cumming writes about looking at paintings better than almost anyone. The Prado has Las Meninas, and she is very good on it.

title: The Spanish Holocaust
creator: Paul Preston
desc: Franco’s side killed roughly 150,000 civilians away from the front, and Preston counts them. It is long and grim and unarguable. The eastern wall of La Almudena cemetery is where thousands of Madrileños were shot after the city fell.

title: Death in the Afternoon
creator: Ernest Hemingway
desc: Hemingway on bullfighting: what happens, why, and what he thinks it means. It is beautiful and it is also a defence of killing bulls, so read it knowing that. Las Ventas on Calle Alcalá is the biggest ring in Spain.

title: Spain: The Trials and Triumphs of a Modern European Country
creator: Michael Reid
desc: How Spain got from Franco’s death to now: the pact of silence, the boom, the crash, Catalonia. Clear and current. In 1981 armed officers stormed the Congreso de los Diputados; the bullet holes are still in the ceiling.

title: Madrid: A Cultural History
creator: Elizabeth Nash
desc: A short cultural history built around the places themselves: the palace, the taverns, the bullring, the Rastro market. Good for orientation. Puerta del Sol is Madrid’s centre, and the paving slab marking kilometre zero is right there.

title: Fear and Loathing in La Liga
creator: Sid Lowe
desc: Real Madrid against Barcelona, and why it is never only football. Franco, money, and a century of grudge, told by a very funny journalist. The Bernabéu is the stadium, and the club was Franco’s team whether it wanted to be or not.

title: Winter in Madrid
creator: C.J. Sansom
desc: Madrid in 1940: starving, defeated, full of spies, with Franco deciding whether to join Hitler. A thriller built on real history. The Gran Vía, the wide boulevard cut through the old city, is where his characters keep meeting.

title: Almodóvar on Almodóvar
creator: Frédéric Strauss
desc: Almodóvar talks through every film he has made, and the Madrid he came to as a broke provincial kid. Funny and unguarded. La Movida happened around Malasaña, in the bars just north of the centre.

title: A People’s History of Catalonia
creator: Michael Eaude
desc: A history of Catalonia from below: the factory workers, anarchists, and strikers, not the counts and architects. It’s the counterweight to the Gaudí postcard. Poble-sec is one of the old working-class districts under the Montjuïc hill.

title: The Struggle for Catalonia
creator: Raphael Minder
desc: A New York Times correspondent on why Catalonia keeps trying to leave Spain, written around the 2017 independence referendum. Even-handed and clear. Plaça de Sant Jaume holds both the Catalan government and the city hall, facing each other.

title: The Sagrada Família
creator: Gijs van Hensbergen
desc: A short book about one building. Started in 1882, still unfinished, funded by tickets and donations, hated by Picasso, loved by Dalí. It explains why the Sagrada Família looks like that, and why it has taken 140 years.

title: Ghosts of Spain
place: Fossar de la Pedrera, Montjuïc Cemetery
creator: Giles Tremlett
desc: Spain agreed to forget its civil war, and Tremlett goes looking for what got buried. Readable and unsettling. The Fossar de la Pedrera, a quarry in Montjuïc cemetery, holds mass graves and the tomb of Companys, the Catalan president Franco shot.

title: Fear and Loathing in La Liga
creator: Sid Lowe
desc: Barça versus Real Madrid, and why it is never only football. Franco, Catalan identity, and a century of grudge, told by a journalist who is very funny. The Camp Nou is the stadium in Les Corts, and under Franco it was where you could shout in Catalan.

title: Cathedral of the Sea
creator: Ildefonso Falcones
desc: Fourteenth-century Barcelona, told through the men who carried the stone. Massive bestseller in Spain, and the reason many visitors go to Santa Maria del Mar, the church in the old port quarter that ordinary labourers built themselves.

title: City of Marvels
creator: Eduardo Mendoza
desc: Barcelona builds itself between the two World’s Fairs, 1888 and 1929, and a poor boy claws his way up with it. A great comic novel about a city inventing itself. The 1888 fair was held in the Parc de la Ciutadella, which is what’s left of it.

title: The Shadow of the Wind
creator: Carlos Ruiz Zafón
desc: A boy is taken to a hidden library in the old city and picks one book, which someone is destroying every copy of. Set in the grey, frightened Barcelona after the Civil War. It sends thousands of readers to Carrer de l’Arc del Teatre in the Raval.

title: Barcelona
creator: Robert Hughes
desc: The big one: an art critic’s furious, funny history of the city, from Roman colony to Olympic makeover. It’s long, and worth it. He is at his best in the Barri Gòtic, the medieval quarter, where he shows you how much of it is a Victorian fake.

title: Homage to Catalonia
creator: George Orwell
desc: Orwell came to fight Franco and found a city run by its workers, waiters refusing tips. Then the revolution ate itself. During the 1937 street fighting he was posted on the roof of the Poliorama, a theatre on La Rambla, watching the Rambla below.

title: Homage to Barcelona
creator: Colm Tóibín
desc: The novelist arrived in 1975, two months before Franco died, and stayed. Part memoir, part history, part guide to Gaudí, Picasso, and Catalan stubbornness. He writes beautifully about Plaça Reial, the palm-lined square off the Rambla.

title: Catalan Cuisine
creator: Colman Andrews
desc: The book that told the English-speaking world Catalan food is not Spanish food: rabbit with snails, salt cod, romesco, sea and mountain on one plate. La Boqueria, the covered market off the Rambla, is where you see the whole larder at once.

title: The Rise and Fall of the House of Medici
creator: Christopher Hibbert
desc: Bankers who bought a city, then a papacy, then most of the art you came to see. Four hundred years of murder, patronage, and gout. Hibbert is a born storyteller. The Palazzo Medici Riccardi on Via Cavour was the family’s first house.

title: Death in Florence
creator: Paul Strathern
desc: A ranting friar took over Florence in 1494, burned the art, and was burned himself four years later in the same square. Strathern tells it as a duel between him and the Medici. Piazza della Signoria has a plaque where he was hanged and set alight.

title: The Stones of Florence
creator: Mary McCarthy
desc: An American writer looks hard at Florence and refuses to be charmed: a harsh, stony, quarrelsome city that happened to make beautiful things. Sharp and still true. She is very good on the Ponte Vecchio and the butchers who once worked it.

title: Galileo’s Daughter
creator: Dava Sobel
desc: Galileo’s daughter was a nun in a poor convent, and her letters to him survive; his to her do not. A warm, strange book about science and faith. The Museo Galileo, on the river, keeps his instruments and, oddly, one of his fingers.

title: Dante: A Life
creator: R.W.B. Lewis
desc: A short life of the poet who was thrown out of Florence, sentenced to burn if he returned, and wrote the greatest poem in Italian while in exile. The Casa di Dante is a museum near his family’s houses, though the building is a modern reconstruction.

title: Brunelleschi’s Dome
creator: Ross King
desc: Nobody knew how to build a dome that big, so the city ran a competition and a goldsmith with a temper won it. He never explained how. Short, gripping, and about engineering more than art. The Duomo is the thing he built, and you can climb inside it.

title: Dark Water: Flood and Redemption in the City of Masterpieces
creator: Robert Clark
desc: In November 1966 the Arno rose and drowned the city, killing people and thousands of artworks. Students came from everywhere to dig them out of the mud. Santa Croce was hit worst; a marker on the church wall shows how high the water came.

title: A Room with a View
creator: E.M. Forster
desc: An English girl in a Florence pensione is chaperoned, disapproved of, and kissed. Light, funny, and merciless about tourists who see nothing. Piazzale Michelangelo, up the hill, gives the postcard view she is supposed to admire.

title: The Agony and the Ecstasy
creator: Irving Stone
desc: A novel about Michelangelo, built on his letters and contracts. Enormous, and the reason many people first cared about him. He carved the David from a block other sculptors had abandoned; it stands in the Accademia, on Via Ricasoli.

title: Lives of the Artists
creator: Giorgio Vasari
desc: The first art history book, written in 1550 by a painter who knew many of them. Full of gossip, insults, and workshop detail. Vasari also designed the Uffizi, the long gallery on the Arno where much of the art he wrote about now hangs.

title: The Prince
creator: Niccolò Machiavelli
desc: A hundred pages, written by a sacked civil servant trying to get his job back, that changed how rulers think about power. It is short, cold, and still shocking. Machiavelli worked in the Palazzo Vecchio, the fortress-like town hall on the square.

title: Carmen
creator: Prosper Mérimée
desc: The novella behind the opera: a soldier ruined by a woman who will not be owned. Bizet added the tunes; Mérimée wrote the cruelty. Carmen rolls cigars at the Real Fábrica de Tabacos, the vast tobacco works that is now the University of Seville.

title: The Trickster of Seville and the Stone Guest
creator: Tirso de Molina
desc: The play that invented Don Juan: a Seville nobleman who seduces, lies, and is dragged to hell by a statue. Every later version starts here. The Hospital de la Caridad was founded by Miguel de Mañara, a real Seville rake long tied to the legend.

title: Over the Edge of the World
creator: Laurence Bergreen
desc: The first voyage around the earth, told as the ordeal it was — mutiny, scurvy, starvation, Magellan dead before the finish. Bergreen makes it vivid. The fleet fitted out and sailed from Seville in 1519, downriver past this tower on the Guadalquivir.

title: Duende: A Journey in Search of Flamenco
creator: Jason Webster
desc: An Englishman falls for flamenco, moves to Spain, and ends up living with a Gypsy family and playing guitar in the bars. Honest about how closed the world is. Its heart beats in Triana, the old Roma quarter where the form took shape.

title: Exemplary Stories
creator: Miguel de Cervantes
desc: Twelve short tales by the author of Don Quixote — sharp, funny, streetwise. Rinconete and Cortadillo drops two boy thieves into Seville’s world of fences and hard men. Cervantes knew it: he was jailed on Calle Sierpes, where the story unfolds.

title: The Spanish Inquisition: A Historical Revision
place: Castillo de San Jorge museum, Triana
creator: Henry Kamen
desc: Kamen dismantles the legend and leaves something stranger: a bureaucracy of fear, less all-powerful than you think, more insidious. Seville held the first auto-da-fé in 1481. Its tribunal ran from the Castillo de San Jorge, now a Triana museum.

title: Moorish Spain
creator: Richard Fletcher
desc: Eight centuries of Muslim Spain in one short, wry book — conquest, the caliphate, the long unravelling. Fletcher is brisk and never romantic. The Giralda began as the minaret of Seville’s great Almohad mosque; the cathedral just grew around it.

title: Spain: The Centre of the World 1519–1682
place: General Archive of the Indies (Archivo de Indias)
creator: Robert Goodwin
desc: For 150 years every ship to and from the Americas cleared through Seville, and the silver made it the richest city in Europe. Goodwin tells that Golden Age with gusto. It’s long. The trade was run from the exchange that is now the Archivo de Indias.

title: Ghosts of Spain
creator: Giles Tremlett
desc: A reporter who knows Spain digs into what it buried: the war graves, flamenco, the wild south, the pull between memory and forgetting. Warm and clear-eyed. He roams the whole country, but Andalusia and Seville’s late nights run right through it.

title: Death in the Afternoon
creator: Ernest Hemingway
desc: Hemingway’s book-length case for the bullfight as art, not sport — technical, obsessive, and a defence of killing as spectacle, so know that going in. The Maestranza, Spain’s grandest ring, is where the Seville season peaks each spring.

title: The Spanish Holocaust
creator: Paul Preston
desc: The definitive account of the terror behind Franco’s rise: the mass killings, the disappeared, the decades of silence. It is long and harrowing. In Seville, General Queipo took the city by fear in 1936; many victims lie in this cemetery’s ground.

title: From Posh Príncipe Real to Downtown Lisbon for a Ginjinha
creator: Rita Alves
desc: A neighborhood walk from upscale Príncipe Real into the historic center, ending with a local cherry liqueur. From a leafy square by a neo-Moorish palace, it passes a hilltop viewpoint and a station with horseshoe-arch doorways, ending at a ginjinha shot.

title: The Carnation Revolution
creator: Alex Fernandes
desc: On 25 April 1974 soldiers overthrew Europe’s longest dictatorship, and people put carnations in their gun barrels. Nobody was supposed to die, and almost nobody did. The bridge over the Tagus was renamed for the date within days.

title: Lisboeta
creator: Nuno Mendes
desc: A Lisbon-born chef’s book of the food he grew up on: bread stews, snails, tinned fish, custard tarts. Part memoir, part recipes, and it explains what you’re eating. The Mercado da Ribeira has been the city’s food market since 1892.

title: This Gulf of Fire
creator: Mark Molesky
desc: On All Saints’ Day 1755 the earthquake, then the fire, then the tsunami. Tens of thousands died and Europe argued about God afterward. The Carmo Convent was left roofless on purpose, and you can stand under its open Gothic arches.

title: The Portuguese: A Modern History
creator: Barry Hatton
desc: A reporter who has lived there for decades explains the Portuguese to themselves and to you: the empire, the dictatorship, the shrug. Affectionate and clear-eyed. Praça do Comércio is the great riverside square Pombal built after the earthquake.

title: Lisbon: War in the Shadows of the City of Light, 1939–1945
creator: Neill Lochery
desc: Neutral Lisbon in the war: refugees, spies, smuggled wolfram, and Salazar playing both sides for cash. It reads like a thriller and it’s all documented. Rossio, the old central square, was where the exiles sat and waited for a visa.

title: Pereira Maintains
creator: Antonio Tabucchi
desc: An ageing journalist in 1938 Lisbon minds his own business until he can’t. Short, quiet, and about the moment a coward decides. Bairro Alto is where the small newspapers and their cafés were.

title: The Year of the Death of Ricardo Reis
creator: José Saramago
desc: A doctor comes home to Lisbon in 1936 as fascism closes in, and is visited by the ghost of the dead poet Pessoa. Saramago won the Nobel. It’s a slow, rainy, extraordinary book. It circles the streets above Cais do Sodré, down by the river.

title: Conquerors: How Portugal Forged the First Global Empire
creator: Roger Crowley
desc: How a small poor country on the edge of Europe took the sea routes to India and built the first global empire, mostly by being ruthless. Fast and gripping. The Monument to the Discoveries in Belém celebrates it without much doubt.

title: The Book of Disquiet
creator: Fernando Pessoa
desc: A bookkeeper in Lisbon writes fragments about being nobody, and it turns out to be one of the strangest and best books of the century. Read it in pieces. Pessoa wrote in the cafés of Chiado; his bronze sits outside A Brasileira on Rua Garrett.

title: The Last Kabbalist of Lisbon
place: Largo de São Domingos (1506 massacre memorial)
creator: Richard Zimler
desc: A crime novel set during the real 1506 Lisbon massacre, when a mob killed thousands of converted Jews over three days. Zimler builds it on the surviving record. Largo de São Domingos, where much of it happened, has a memorial and an olive tree.

title: Street Fight in Naples
creator: Peter Robb
desc: Three thousand years of Naples told through its art and its revolts, by a writer who lived it. Gripping and personal. Piazza Mercato is where the fisherman Masaniello led the 1647 revolt against Spain — and where its rebels were later executed.

title: Naples ’44
creator: Norman Lewis
desc: The best book about occupied Naples: a British officer’s diary of a starving city surviving on wits, black market and miracle. Funny, humane, unforgettable. He walked Via Toledo, the spine of the old town, past all the war had thrown up.

title: The Day Before Happiness
creator: Erri De Luca
desc: A short, luminous novel of a Naples orphan raised by a building’s caretaker, who tells him how the city rose against the Nazis in 1943. De Luca is Neapolitan to the bone. The Quartieri Spagnoli’s tight lanes are its world.

title: Maradona: The Hand of God
creator: Jimmy Burns
desc: How a genius from the Buenos Aires slums became a god in Naples, winning the city’s only league titles before cocaine and the Camorra pulled him down. The stadium that now carries his name is where a poor southern city beat the rich north.

title: Caravaggio: A Life Sacred and Profane
creator: Andrew Graham-Dixon
desc: The painter as street-fighter: a murderer on the run who made the most violent, tender religious art of his age. Graham-Dixon tracks him to Naples. His huge Seven Works of Mercy still hangs over the altar at the Pio Monte della Misericordia.

title: My Brilliant Friend
creator: Elena Ferrante
desc: Two girls grow up clever and trapped in a poor postwar Naples neighbourhood, and their fierce sixty-year friendship carries all four novels. Naples is the real subject. The unnamed rione is Rione Luzzatti, the courtyard blocks east of the centre.

title: The Ancient Shore: Dispatches from Naples
creator: Shirley Hazzard
desc: Short, elegant essays by a novelist who loved Naples for decades — its light, its literature, its maddening beauty. A love letter with clear eyes. She knew the Chiaia seafront, the long bayside walk where the city faces its gulf.

title: Delizia!
creator: John Dickie
desc: How Italians invented their food, city by city — medieval banquets, pasta, and the rise of pizza from Naples street snack to global icon. Great fun. Pizzeria Brandi claims it baked the first Margherita here in 1889, for a visiting queen.

title: Gomorrah
creator: Roberto Saviano
desc: An insider’s report on the Camorra: the clans, the toxic-waste dumps, the teenage foot soldiers, the global reach. Saviano named names and has lived under guard since. The gang wars he describes were fought around the Vele, the towers of Scampia.

title: Italian Journey
creator: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
desc: The most famous Grand Tour diary. Goethe reaches Naples in 1787, calls it a paradise, and climbs Vesuvius three times to peer into the smoking crater. His delight is infectious. The volcano he scrambled up still looms over the whole bay.

title: The Skin
creator: Curzio Malaparte
desc: A savage, hallucinatory novel of the 1943 ‘liberation,’ when the Allies arrived and Naples sold everything, itself included, to survive. Grotesque on purpose, and not for everyone. It plays out under the walls of Castel dell’Ovo.

title: Pompeii: The Life of a Roman Town
creator: Mary Beard
desc: Not the disaster movie — the daily life. Beard reconstructs a working Roman town from its bakeries, brothels, graffiti and plumbing. Enter at the Porta Marina, the old sea gate, and the ruins read as a place people lived.

title: Those Who Are Loved
creator: Victoria Hislop
desc: A novel following one Athens woman from the occupation through the civil war to the colonels — she joins the communists and pays for it on the prison islands. History lightly worn. Exarcheia is the leftist quarter where a life like hers belonged.

title: Adults in the Room
creator: Yanis Varoufakis
desc: Greece’s finance minister on the 2015 debt showdown with Europe: five months of brinkmanship from inside the room. Gripping and thoroughly one-sided — he is the hero of it. Parliament on Syntagma Square is where the crisis played out in public.

title: The Hemlock Cup
creator: Bettany Hughes
desc: A life of Socrates set in the Athens he actually walked. Hughes rebuilds the streets, courts and gymnasia where he button-holed strangers. The Agora, the marketplace under the Acropolis, is where he did his talking — and where he was put on trial.

title: The Parthenon
creator: Mary Beard
desc: Not a temple tour — a biography of the building. Beard covers 2,500 years: church, mosque, the powder store that blew up in 1687, the marbles Elgin took. Short and funny. You look up at it afterward knowing exactly what you are seeing.

title: The Last Days of Socrates
creator: Plato
desc: Four short dialogues: Socrates on trial, refusing to flee, then drinking the hemlock. The Apology is the most readable thing the ancient world left us. His jury and his cell sat here, beside the Agora, in the heart of the ancient city.

title: Twice a Stranger
creator: Bruce Clark
desc: In 1923 Greece and Turkey swapped their minorities by treaty — 1.5 million people uprooted by religion, not language. Clark tracks the wreckage. Nea Smyrni is the Athens suburb the Anatolian refugees built and named for their lost city.

title: The Rise and Fall of Athens
creator: Plutarch
desc: Nine ancient biographies — Solon, Themistocles, Pericles, Alcibiades — that walk Athens from lawgiver to empire to ruin. Gossipy, quotable, the source later writers cribbed. The Pnyx is the bare hill where citizens voted the wars these men led.

title: The Colossus of Maroussi
creator: Henry Miller
desc: Miller’s 1939 trip to Greece, and the happiest thing he wrote — he arrives burnt-out and leaves lit up. Less a travel book than a man falling hard for a country. Maroussi, now a northern Athens suburb, is home to the giant talker of the title.

title: Road to Rembetika
creator: Gail Holst
desc: The blues of the Greek underworld: refugee players, hashish dens, the bouzouki, sung by people with nothing left. Holst explains the music and translates the songs. It grew in the tekes of Piraeus, the port where the boats from Asia Minor tied up.

title: Inside Hitler’s Greece
creator: Mark Mazower
desc: The clearest account of the Nazi occupation: the famine that killed tens of thousands in Athens, the resistance, the reprisals. Mazower writes history you can actually read. At the Kaisariani range the Germans shot 200 hostages in one day in 1944.

title: Deadline in Athens
creator: Petros Markaris
desc: A crime novel whose real subject is modern Athens: the traffic, the TV, the migrant smuggling, a sour cop grinding through all of it. Inspector Haritos works out of the police headquarters on Alexandras Avenue, the grey block this pin sits on.

title: History of the Peloponnesian War
creator: Thucydides
desc: An Athenian general’s account of the 27-year war that broke his own city. Cold, unsparing, the first history written like analysis. It’s long. Pericles gave his speech over the war dead at the Kerameikos, the public cemetery you can still walk through.

title: Unlocking Salford Quays: A Walking Tour from Lowry Theatre to Media City
creator: Richard Gasseling
desc: A story of industrial decline and rebirth: starting at a theatre named for a working-class painter, pass historic dockside warehouses and a football stadium, ending at a waterfront TV and media complex.

title: Trading Through Time: From Stockport Train Station to its medieval Market Hall
creator: Richard Gasseling
desc: A market-town history walk from Victorian village to industrial hub: starting at the train station, pass a hat-making museum and WWII air raid shelters, ending at a glass-fronted Victorian market hall.

title: The Haçienda: How Not to Run a Club
place: Site of the Haçienda club, Whitworth Street West
creator: Peter Hook
desc: New Order’s bassist bankrolled Britain’s most famous nightclub and watched it lose money every night for fifteen years. Hilarious, bitter and full of receipts. The Haçienda stood on Whitworth Street West; there are flats on the site now.

title: The Mighty Walzer
creator: Howard Jacobson
desc: A shy Jewish boy in 1950s Manchester becomes a table tennis champion, more or less. Very funny about ambition, mothers and losing. Jacobson grew up in this world. The Jewish Museum on Cheetham Hill Road is its surviving synagogue.

title: Peterloo: The Story of the Manchester Massacre
creator: Jacqueline Riding
desc: On 16 August 1819 cavalry charged a peaceful crowd of sixty thousand people demanding the vote. Eighteen died. Riding reconstructs the day and names the people in it. The memorial marks ground that is now a car park and a convention centre.

title: Manchester: A History
creator: Alan Kidd
desc: The clearest single-volume account of how a damp Lancashire town became the world’s first industrial city, then spent a century working out what came next. Chetham’s Library, founded in 1653, predates all of it.

title: Little Wilson and Big God
creator: Anthony Burgess
desc: Before A Clockwork Orange, Burgess was a Catholic boy loose in Manchester pubs, picture houses and back streets, and he recalls it in extraordinary detail. Boastful, filthy, very funny, unreliable in places. Moss Side is where he grew up.

title: Manchester, England: The Story of the Pop Cult City
creator: Dave Haslam
desc: A DJ and historian traces one line from Victorian music halls through northern soul to acid house, arguing the city’s noise came from its immigrants and its rain. The Free Trade Hall held the 1976 Sex Pistols gig everyone claims to have attended.

title: Mary Barton
creator: Elizabeth Gaskell
desc: A mill worker’s daughter, a strike, a murder, a father driven to it. Gaskell lived among the people she wrote about and let them speak in their own dialect, which scandalised London. Her house on Plymouth Grove is open and looks as she left it.

title: The Condition of the Working Class in England
creator: Friedrich Engels
desc: A 24-year-old German was sent to manage his father’s cotton mill and walked the slums instead, writing down exactly what he saw. Angry, precise, and the reason Marx became Marx. Ancoats was the world’s first industrial suburb; it is full of cafés now.

title: Alan Turing: The Enigma
creator: Andrew Hodges
desc: The definitive life: codebreaking at Bletchley, the birth of the computer in Manchester, and the prosecution that destroyed him. Hodges is a mathematician and does not skip the maths. Turing sits on a bench in Sackville Gardens.

title: My Own Story
creator: Emmeline Pankhurst
desc: The suffragette leader’s account of hunger strikes, force-feeding and prison, written while the fight was still going on. She is not modest and does not apologise. The Women’s Social and Political Union was founded in her parlour on Nelson Street.

title: The Anatomy Murders
creator: Lisa Rosner
desc: The true 1828 story of Burke and Hare, who smothered sixteen to sell fresh bodies to Edinburgh’s anatomy schools — and the eminent surgeon who asked no questions. Its dark end is the dissecting theatre at Surgeons’ Hall.

title: Knots and Crosses
creator: Ian Rankin
desc: The first Rebus: a hard-drinking detective hunts a child-killer through an Edinburgh of pubs, tenements and buried guilt the tourists never see. It launched a genre. Rebus drinks at the Oxford Bar, a real New Town howff with no frills.

title: 44 Scotland Street
creator: Alexander McCall Smith
desc: A warm, gently comic soap of a New Town stair — a hapless surveyor, a monstrous mother and her put-upon boy, an anthropologist and his dog. It all happens on Scotland Street, in the douce Georgian New Town.

title: Trainspotting
creator: Irvine Welsh
desc: Renton, Sick Boy, Begbie and Spud, spat out by Thatcher’s Britain into heroin, in furious Leith dialect that seizes you by the collar. Funny, filthy — not for the squeamish. It roars out of Leith, the old port at the foot of the Walk.

title: Capital of the Mind
place: David Hume’s tomb, Old Calton Burial Ground
creator: James Buchan
desc: How a cold, poor, half-medieval town became, for one dazzling half-century, the smartest place on earth — Hume, Adam Smith, the geologists and doctors who remade thought. Hume lies in this Robert Adam tomb on Calton Hill.

title: One Good Turn
creator: Kate Atkinson
desc: A road-rage attack during the crowded Festival tangles a crime writer, a retired detective and a Russian cleaner into one clever, funny plot. It plays out amid the August madness of the Fringe, thick around Bristo Square.

title: The Prime of Miss Jean Brodie
creator: Muriel Spark
desc: A charismatic 1930s schoolmistress shapes her chosen girls — ‘the crème de la crème’ — with beauty, fascism and betrayal. Spark’s diamond-hard masterpiece. Her school and the girls’ crocodile walks belong to Bruntsfield and the Links.

title: Edinburgh: A History of the City
creator: Michael Fry
desc: Fry tells his city’s whole turbulent story — sieges, plague, the Reformation, the Union, the Enlightenment blaze — with wit and strong opinions. It all looks up to the Castle on its black volcanic crag, where Edinburgh began.

title: The Heart of Midlothian
place: Heart of Midlothian mosaic (site of the Old Tolbooth)
creator: Walter Scott
desc: Scott’s Edinburgh novel: the 1736 Porteous riots, and a dairymaid who walks to London to beg her wrongly condemned sister’s life. It’s long, but it’s the one. The heart-shaped mosaic marks the Tolbooth jail at its centre.

title: Edinburgh: Picturesque Notes
creator: Robert Louis Stevenson
desc: Young Stevenson’s love-quarrel with his hometown: the wynds, the double city of grand New Town and rotting Old, and a climate he calls ‘one of the vilest under heaven.’ He grew up here at Heriot Row, in the New Town he half-fled.

title: The Private Memoirs and Confessions of a Justified Sinner
creator: James Hogg
desc: A young zealot decides God’s grace lets him murder freely, egged on by a stranger who may be the Devil or himself. Scotland’s great gothic novel of the divided soul, a century before Jekyll. A key scene unfolds in fog on Arthur’s Seat.

title: Witches, Riots and the Cold War: A Walk Through Wedding
creator: Marcel Krueger
desc: A neighborhood history walk through working-class Wedding, tracing social upheaval and a divided Cold War past. Starting outside a train station, it follows a small river past a Cold War ghost station, ending at a bathhouse turned library.

title: Silk, Sin and Stages: In and Out of Northern Friedrichstraße
creator: The Berlin Companion
desc: A cabaret-and-theater history walk through northern Friedrichstraße. Starting at a historic river-spanning railway station, it passes a WWII bunker turned art gallery and a theater tied to a famous playwright, looping back to the same station.

title: Old and New West Berlin: A Tour of Kurfürstendamm and Kantstrasse
creator: Jo Eckardt
desc: A 100-years-of-change walk through Charlottenburg, from Belle Époque glamour to Cold War division. Starting and ending at a bombed WWII memorial church, this loop follows a grand boulevard past a small Chinese quarter.

title: The East Side Gallery Self-Guided Tour: The Berlin Wall as a Canvas
creator: Roberta Schmoi
desc: A public-art history walk along the longest surviving stretch of the Berlin Wall. Starting outside a former East Berlin train station, it follows a riverside gallery of political murals, ending at a fairytale bridge that was once a border checkpoint.

title: Former East Berlin: A Walking Tour Through 400 Years of History
creator: Jo Eckardt
desc: An architecture walk through four centuries of former East Berlin. Starting at the famous Cold War border crossing, it follows a grand boulevard past a book-burning memorial and a historic opera house, ending at a river-island cluster of grand museums.

title: Memorials and Monuments: A Walking Tour from the Reichstag to Potsdam Square
creator: Jo Eckardt
desc: A memorials-and-monuments walk through political Berlin. Starting outside the German parliament building, it crosses a grand park past Cold War and wartime memorials and a somber Holocaust memorial, ending at a rebuilt modern square.

title: Der Klang der Familie: Berlin, Techno and the Fall of the Wall
creator: Felix Denk & Sven von Thülen
desc: An oral history of the years when the Wall came down and Berlin’s empty buildings filled with techno. Told entirely by the people who were there. Berghain, in an old power plant, is what that scene turned into.

title: Berlin: Imagine a City
creator: Rory MacLean
desc: Twenty-one Berliners across five centuries, each given a chapter: a Nazi filmmaker, a Cold War spy, a Wall victim, Bowie. Novelistic, and the best way in. Museum Island sits on the Spree, where the first settlement began.

title: Red Love: The Story of an East German Family
creator: Maxim Leo
desc: One family, three generations: a grandfather in the resistance, a father who hated the state, a son who left. The most human book on what East Germany was actually like. Leo grew up in Prenzlauer Berg, before it filled with cafés.

title: The Berlin Wall: A World Divided
creator: Frederick Taylor
desc: How a city got cut in half overnight in August 1961, and what it did to the people on both sides. Clear and gripping. Bernauer Straße is where the houses were on one side and the pavement on the other, and where people jumped.

title: The Ghosts of Berlin
creator: Brian Ladd
desc: What do you do with a city full of buildings you’d rather forget? Ladd walks through the arguments over the Wall, the bunker, the Palace of the Republic. The Topography of Terror sits on the Gestapo headquarters, deliberately left bare.

title: In the Garden of Beasts
creator: Erik Larson
desc: The American ambassador and his flirtatious daughter arrive in Berlin in 1933 and slowly work out what is happening. Reads like a thriller. Their world was the Tiergarten, the huge park where the diplomats lived and walked.

title: Aimée & Jaguar
creator: Erica Fischer
desc: A Jewish woman in hiding and the wife of a Nazi officer fall in love in wartime Berlin. It’s true; Lilly Wust survived, Felice Schragenheim did not. They lived in Schöneberg, and there’s a plaque on Friedrichshaller Straße.

title: Berlin: The Downfall 1945
creator: Antony Beevor
desc: The last months: the Red Army closing in, two million refugees, the city fighting street by street. Beevor is very readable and does not look away from the mass rapes. The Reichstag is the building the Soviets raised their flag on.

title: A Woman in Berlin
creator: Anonymous
desc: A Berlin woman’s diary, April to June 1945, written as the Red Army arrives. She is raped repeatedly and records it in dry, unsparing prose. Germany hated it in 1959. The Soviet memorial in Treptower Park honours the same army.

title: Goodbye to Berlin
creator: Christopher Isherwood
desc: A young Englishman teaches English, watches Weimar Berlin dance, and notices the Nazis arriving. Cabaret came from this. He lodged at Nollendorfstraße 17, off Nollendorfplatz; the plaque is on the wall.

title: Alone in Berlin
creator: Hans Fallada
desc: An ordinary Berlin couple lose their son and start leaving anti-Hitler postcards around the city. It’s based on a real case, and they were real. The Hampels lived off Amtsgerichtsplatz in Charlottenburg. It took the Gestapo two years.

title: Stasiland
creator: Anna Funder
desc: Funder goes looking for East Germans who resisted, and for the Stasi men who broke them. One of the great books of reportage, and very funny in places. The Stasi Museum on Normannenstraße is the old headquarters, left as it was.

title: The Vienna Food Walk
creator: Roland Pickl
desc: A food-and-drink walk through the old first district with five optional tasting stops. From a central metro station, it samples open sandwiches, sausages, and Viennese wine between the cathedral, coffee houses, and market squares. Eat like a local.

title: Becoming Freud
creator: Adam Phillips
desc: A short, elegant book about how Freud became Freud, by a working psychoanalyst. Better company than the theory itself. He saw patients at Berggasse 19 for 47 years, until the Nazis forced him out. The apartment is a museum, and nearly bare.

title: Beethoven: A Life in Nine Pieces
creator: Laura Tunbridge
desc: Nine pieces, nine chapters, one life. An Oxford scholar who writes for normal people. In 1802, in a house in the wine village of Heiligenstadt, Beethoven wrote a letter about killing himself and chose to keep working. It’s a museum now.

title: Mozart: A Life
creator: Paul Johnson
desc: A short, brisk life of Mozart, and a good antidote to the giggling genius of the movie. He was a working musician chasing commissions and running out of money. The flat on Domgasse, behind the cathedral, is his only surviving Vienna home.

title: The Hare with Amber Eyes
creator: Edmund de Waal
desc: A potter follows 264 tiny Japanese carvings through five generations of his family, the Ephrussi, Jewish bankers. In 1938 the Nazis emptied their palace on the Ringstrasse. It still stands at Universitätsring 14, with a supermarket on the ground floor.

title: The Lady in Gold
creator: Anne-Marie O’Connor
desc: The story of one painting: Klimt’s gold portrait of Adele Bloch-Bauer. The Nazis stole it. The Belvedere, a palace museum, showed it for decades as “the Woman in Gold.” Her niece sued Austria and won it back in 2006. It hangs in New York now.

title: Still Alive: A Holocaust Girlhood Remembered
creator: Ruth Klüger
desc: A Vienna girl, deported at eleven. She survived Theresienstadt and Auschwitz, and refuses to make any of it comforting, least of all for her own city. Judenplatz is a square in the old Jewish quarter. Its memorial is a sealed concrete library.

title: Hitler’s Vienna: A Dictator’s Apprenticeship
creator: Brigitte Hamann
desc: The other Vienna of 1900. Not Freud and Klimt, but cheap hostels, resentment, and everyday antisemitism. It’s where a failed painter picked up his ideas. Hitler spent three years in a men’s home on Meldemannstraße, a poor street. The building is gone.

title: Fin-de-Siècle Vienna: Politics and Culture
creator: Carl E. Schorske
desc: How one city invented modern art, psychoanalysis, and modern politics at once, while its politics fell apart. Schorske reads the Ringstrasse, the grand boulevard around the old town, as an argument: every building on it claims who Vienna belongs to.

title: The Third Man
creator: Graham Greene
desc: Greene walked around bombed, occupied Vienna to write this. A man sells watered-down penicillin to sick children and gets chased through the sewers. The racket was real. The Third Man Museum on Preßgasse keeps that city, and you can still tour the sewers.

title: Man’s Search for Meaning
creator: Viktor Frankl
desc: A Viennese psychiatrist lost his wife, parents, and brother in the camps. He came out believing a person can survive almost anything if they have a reason to. He wrote it in nine days. His museum on Mariannengasse is ten minutes from Freud’s.

title: A Nervous Splendor: Vienna 1888–1889
creator: Frederic Morton
desc: One winter in Vienna, told like a novel. Crown Prince Rudolf drifts toward killing himself while a young Freud, Mahler, and Klimt walk the same streets. Rudolf lies in the Kaisergruft, a crypt under a church, with 140 other Habsburgs.

title: The World of Yesterday
creator: Stefan Zweig
desc: Zweig’s goodbye to the Europe he grew up in: the coffeehouses, the safety, a world everyone assumed would last. He mailed the manuscript from exile in Brazil and killed himself days later. Café Central, a grand coffeehouse, is the room he means.

title: The Radetzky March
creator: Joseph Roth
desc: One family over three generations, rising and falling with the Habsburg empire until the war ends it. Roth watched the collapse happen. It’s the best book on what it feels like when your country stops existing. Heldenplatz is the imperial parade square.

title: Wittgenstein’s Nephew
place: Church of St Leopold (Kirche am Steinhof)
creator: Thomas Bernhard
desc: Two friends lie ill on the same hospital hill west of the city: Bernhard in the lung ward, his friend Paul in the asylum next door. Bernhard hated Austria and says so, furiously and hilariously. Otto Wagner’s gold-domed church crowns the grounds.

title: A Walk Through Post-Industrial Holešovice
creator: Christoph Amthor
desc: A post-industrial neighbourhood walk through a factory quarter reinventing itself. From a historic riverside market, it passes old storehouses, a contemporary art centre, and communist-era traces, ending at a nightclub built from salvaged machinery.

title: Tracing a 16th-Century Water Supply Tunnel
creator: Christoph Amthor
desc: An engineering-and-parks walk following a still-working Renaissance water tunnel from river to lake. From the riverbank below the giant metronome, it climbs a hill past hidden ventilation chimneys, ending at a lake in a former royal hunting park.

title: World Wars, Communism and Liberation: A Prague Walking Tour
creator: Jana Vesela
desc: A 20th-century-history walk through Nazi occupation, communism, and the 1989 revolution. From outside a grand Art Nouveau civic hall, it passes Holocaust memorial stones and a former secret-police street, ending below the national museum.

title: New Town: Art Nouveau and Elegant Cafés
creator: Jitka Simkova
desc: An architecture-and-café walk spanning a century of building styles and the 1989 revolution. From the top of the grand boulevard-square, it ducks through covered passageways to the avenue where the Velvet Revolution began, ending at the riverside.

title: A Prague Walking Tour: The Glory, Decline and Revival of Vysehrad Castle
creator: Jana Vesela
desc: A history-and-legend walk around a hilltop fortress above the river, away from the crowds. From an old fortress gate, it follows ramparts with sweeping views past an 11th-century round chapel, ending at a cemetery of famous composers.

title: Tales Behind the House Signs of Old Prague
creator: Jana Vesela
desc: An architecture-and-legend walk decoding the painted symbols that named houses before street numbers. From the foot of the grand boulevard-square, it winds through a medieval market quarter, ending at a small charming square.

title: The Mercurial Emperor
creator: Peter Marshall
desc: Around 1600 the emperor Rudolf II moved his court to Prague and filled it with astronomers, alchemists and painters chasing the philosopher’s stone. Marshall makes it vivid. It all happened at the Castle, where alchemists worked in Golden Lane.

title: Prague in Black and Gold
creator: Peter Demetz
desc: A Prague-born scholar tells his city’s whole life — Charles IV, the defenestrations, the Jewish town, the German-Czech tangle — with elegance and no nostalgia. The best single history. Old Town Square, with its clock and its ghosts, is its natural heart.

title: HHhH
place: Church of Sts Cyril and Methodius, Resslova
creator: Laurent Binet
desc: The true story of the parachutists who killed Heydrich, the SS chief ruling Prague — told by a novelist agonising over how to tell it. Gripping and honest. It ends in the crypt of this church on Resslova, where the assassins made their last stand.

title: The Magic Lantern
creator: Timothy Garton Ash
desc: An eyewitness to 1989: Garton Ash watches the Velvet Revolution from inside, as Havel and his circle plot the end of Communism. Thrilling, clear, first-hand. Civic Forum ran the revolt from the Laterna Magika, the theatre where this pin sits.

title: The Unbearable Lightness of Being
creator: Milan Kundera
desc: Kundera’s novel of love and weight, set as Soviet tanks crush the Prague Spring of 1968. Philosophy, sex, and a country losing its breath. The invasion filled Wenceslas Square, the long boulevard where Czechs gather to cheer and to grieve.

title: Utz
creator: Bruce Chatwin
desc: A slim, sly novel about a man who stays in communist Prague for love of his Meissen porcelain, hoarding beauty while the world greys. Chatwin at his most elegant. Utz’s windows look over the Old Jewish Cemetery, its stones tilting under the elders.

title: Under a Cruel Star
creator: Heda Margolius Kovály
desc: A luminous, terrible memoir: Kovály survives Auschwitz and a death march, comes home to Prague, then watches the Communists execute her husband in the 1950s show trials. He was hanged at Pankrác. Few books say more about the century in so few pages.

title: Too Loud a Solitude
creator: Bohumil Hrabal
desc: For 35 years Haňťa has crushed banned books in a wastepaper press, saving and reading what he can. Hrabal’s tender, drunk, heartbreaking little masterpiece. He wrote it in Libeň, the working-class district on the river he made his own.

title: The Good Soldier Švejk
creator: Jaroslav Hašek
desc: The great Czech comic novel: a cheerful idiot — or sly saboteur — bumbles through the Austrian war machine, deflating every authority. Bawdy and bottomless. Švejk sets off from U Kalicha, the beer hall where he arranges to meet after the war.

title: The Golem
creator: Gustav Meyrink
desc: A feverish dream-novel of the old Jewish ghetto: a jeweller, a legend, a clay man who walks every 33 years. Meyrink’s Prague is all fog and menace. The Old-New Synagogue, Europe’s oldest, is said to hold the golem of Rabbi Loew in its attic.

title: The Trial
creator: Franz Kafka
desc: Josef K. is arrested one morning for a crime no one will name, and destroyed by a court he can never reach. Kafka’s Prague of corridors and dread. He lies under a plain crystal stone in the New Jewish Cemetery, still visited daily.

title: Orbán: Europe’s New Strongman
creator: Paul Lendvai
desc: A veteran Hungarian journalist on how Viktor Orbán rebuilt the country: courts, media, universities, all of it. Sharp and unsparing. Parliament, on Kossuth tér by the river, is where the laws that did it were passed.

title: Budapest: Between East and West
creator: Victor Sebestyen
desc: A Budapest-born historian on the city that keeps getting pulled east and west: Romans, Ottomans, Habsburgs, Nazis, Soviets. Readable and personal. The Chain Bridge, opened in 1849, was the first permanent link between Buda and Pest.

title: Enemies of the People
creator: Kati Marton
desc: A journalist finds her own parents’ secret police file: 1,000 pages, and the informers were their friends. Both were arrested in Budapest in 1955. The House of Terror, at Andrássy út 60, was the building where it was all done.

title: Kasztner’s Train
place: Shoes on the Danube Bank memorial
creator: Anna Porter
desc: In 1944 a Hungarian Jewish lawyer bargained with Eichmann and got 1,600 people onto a train out. Then his own people called him a collaborator. Meanwhile the Arrow Cross shot Jews into the Danube; the Shoes memorial marks where they stood.

title: Journey to a Revolution
creator: Michael Korda
desc: In 1956 Hungarians rose against the Soviets and held them off for twelve days. Korda was a student who drove medical supplies in. He was there. Corvin köz, a cinema courtyard in Pest, was where the teenage fighters held out longest.

title: Ballad of the Whiskey Robber
creator: Julian Rubinstein
desc: A terrible ice hockey goalie robbed 29 Hungarian banks in the 1990s, handed flowers to the tellers, and became a folk hero. Hilarious, true, and the sharpest thing written on post-communist chaos. He tended goal for UTE, the Újpest club.

title: Budapest 1900
creator: John Lukacs
desc: One city at its peak: 1900, when Budapest was the fastest-growing capital in Europe, drunk on coffeehouses, poets, and money. Nobody writes about a golden age better. Heroes’ Square was built in 1896 to celebrate exactly that confidence.

title: Fatelessness
creator: Imre Kertész
desc: A fourteen-year-old Budapest boy is pulled off a bus and sent to Auschwitz, and describes it all without a shred of self-pity. Kertész lived it, and won the Nobel for writing it. The Dohány Street Synagogue stood at the edge of the ghetto.

title: Between the Woods and the Water
creator: Patrick Leigh Fermor
desc: A nineteen-year-old walks across Europe in 1934 and reaches Hungary just before the world ends. Beloved, and the prose is astonishing. He fell in with Budapest’s café society; Gerbeaud, on Vörösmarty tér, is the last grand one still open.

title: The Cuisine of Hungary
creator: George Lang
desc: The book that explained Hungarian food to the world: paprika, sour cream, goulash that is a soup, not a stew. Lang later rebuilt Gundel, the city’s famous restaurant. The Great Market Hall is where you see the paprika strings hanging.

title: Memoir of Hungary
creator: Sándor Márai
desc: Hungary’s great novelist came home to a wrecked city in 1945, watched the communists take it over, and left for good in 1948. A cold, clear-eyed record of a country changing hands. Castle Hill, where he walked, had been shelled to rubble.

title: The Trumpeter of Krakow
creator: Eric P. Kelly
desc: A children’s classic that conjures medieval Kraków: a refugee family, a guarded jewel, and the trumpeter who breaks off his hourly call mid-note. It’s for young readers, and wonderful. The broken hejnał still sounds from St Mary’s tower.

title: The Kraków Ghetto Pharmacy
place: Under the Eagle Pharmacy museum, Ghetto Heroes Square
creator: Tadeusz Pankiewicz
desc: The only non-Jew allowed to stay in the ghetto, a Polish pharmacist, wrote down what he saw from his counter: the round-ups, the courage, the killing. His pharmacy still stands on Plac Bohaterów Getta, now a museum among empty chairs.

title: The Captive Mind
creator: Czesław Miłosz
desc: The Nobel poet’s cold-eyed study of how clever people talk themselves into serving tyranny — written as Stalinism closed over Poland. A classic, though its subject is the nation, not the city. Miłosz is buried at Skałka, among Poland’s honored.

title: If This Is a Man
creator: Primo Levi
desc: Primo Levi’s account of surviving Auschwitz — cool, exact, morally bottomless, the essential book on the camps. Not about Kraków, but the camp an hour west is where so many of the city’s Jews were murdered, and where visitors go to grieve.

title: Schindler’s Ark
creator: Thomas Keneally
desc: The Booker-winning true story of Oskar Schindler, the profiteer who spent everything to save 1,200 Jewish workers. Spielberg filmed it; the book is deeper. His enamel factory in Zabłocie is now a gripping museum of occupied Kraków.

title: Another Beauty
creator: Adam Zagajewski
desc: A poet’s luminous memoir of coming of age in 1960s and 70s Kraków — café arguments, first poems, and the slow pressure of the regime. Quiet and wise. His Kraków turns around the Jagiellonian University and its old lecture halls.

title: The Crooked Mirror
creator: Louise Steinman
desc: An American Jew keeps returning to Poland and finds Poles trying to honour their vanished Jewish neighbours — grief, awkwardness and real repair. Hopeful, unsentimental. It moves through Kazimierz, the old Jewish quarter alive again.

title: A History of Kraków for Everyone
creator: Jan M. Małecki
desc: A Kraków historian walks you through a thousand years of his city — Piast dukes, the golden age, partition, war, communism — briskly and with affection. The best single history. It starts on the Rynek, Europe’s grandest medieval square.

title: The Wedding
creator: Stanisław Wyspiański
desc: The play every Pole knows: a real 1900 wedding where city poets meet peasant villagers, and the ghosts of Polish history crash the party. Young Poland’s masterpiece. It happened here at the Rydlówka, the Bronowice cottage now kept as a museum.

title: Map: Collected and Last Poems
creator: Wisława Szymborska
desc: The other Kraków Nobel laureate: wry, clear, humane poems that make the ordinary strange — a cat in an empty flat, an onion, a photograph. Endlessly re-readable. She lived and wrote in the city all her life and lies in Rakowicki Cemetery.

title: Zurich True Crime Uncovered: A Tour of Its Heists and Robberies
creator: YOUplore
desc: A modern true-crime walk through the wealthy city centre — art heists, jewel raids, and bank robberies. From the art museum, it follows getaway routes down the luxury shopping street, ending at a riverside park with a faked-robbery tale.

title: The Dark Side of Zurich: A Walking Tour Through Old Town
creator: myFive
desc: A dark medieval-history walk through the old town — executioners, witch trials, and torture. From the central bank square, it passes two great churches and the town hall where death sentences were read, ending near the site of a 1489 beheading.

title: Meltdown: Greed, Scandal, and the Collapse of Credit Suisse
creator: Duncan Mavin
desc: How a 167-year-old giant destroyed itself: the spies, the scandals, the blow-ups that ended with Credit Suisse’s emergency sale in 2023. Mavin makes high finance read fast. Its headquarters stood on Paradeplatz, the heart of Swiss banking.

title: Lenin on the Train
creator: Catherine Merridale
desc: April 1917: Germany ships an exiled Lenin across Europe in a sealed train, a bacillus aimed at Russia. Merridale tells it like a thriller. He set out from a cramped flat at Spiegelgasse 14, a few doors up from where Dada was being born.

title: Zwingli: God’s Armed Prophet
creator: Bruce Gordon
desc: The other Reformation. From the pulpit of the Grossmünster, Zwingli stripped the churches bare, banned music, and built a stern new faith — then died on a battlefield. Gordon makes the zealot human. The twin-towered church is where it began, in 1519.

title: Swiss Watching
creator: Diccon Bewes
desc: A funny, affectionate guide to how Switzerland actually works — direct democracy, punctual trains, quiet wealth, and the national soul behind the clichés. Bahnhofstrasse, the discreet luxury spine of Zurich, is the country in one street.

title: The Swiss, the Gold and the Dead
creator: Jean Ziegler
desc: A Swiss insider’s furious exposé of how his country’s banks laundered Nazi gold and kept the dead’s deposits. It caused a scandal at home. The banks still cluster at Paradeplatz, the square that is shorthand for Swiss money and Swiss silence.

title: The Tongue Set Free
creator: Elias Canetti
desc: The first volume of Canetti’s memoirs, and the warmest: a boy’s Zurich years, which he called the happiest of his life, drunk on books and languages. He lived up in Oberstrass, the quiet hillside district north of the centre, reading everything.

title: Travesties
creator: Tom Stoppard
desc: Stoppard’s dazzling comedy stitches together three men in Zurich in 1917 — Lenin, the Dadaist Tzara, and James Joyce writing Ulysses — as recalled by a muddled official. All used the Zentralbibliothek, the reading room where the play spins.

title: Dada: Art and Anti-Art
creator: Hans Richter
desc: The inside story of Dada, by a painter who was there. In 1916, refugees and draft-dodgers turned a Zurich cabaret into nonsense poetry and noise, a revolt against a war-mad world. It started at the Cabaret Voltaire, still open at Spiegelgasse 1.

title: Memories, Dreams, Reflections
creator: C.G. Jung
desc: Jung’s own account of his inner life — dreams, visions, the break with Freud, the descent that became his psychology. He made his name at the Burghölzli, the hillside asylum where he tested the unconscious on real patients.

title: Green Henry
creator: Gottfried Keller
desc: The great Zurich novel: a dreamy young man leaves to become a painter, fails, and comes home to reckon with it. Keller’s own life, lightly veiled. It’s long. Henry roams the old town below the Lindenhof, the linden-topped hill where Zurich first grew.

title: I’m Not Stiller
creator: Max Frisch
desc: A man jailed in Zurich insists he is not the missing sculptor Stiller, and fills notebooks denying a self everyone else can see. Frisch’s novel of identity and Swiss conformity. It circles the lakeside city around Bellevue, where the trams converge.

title: Paris Reborn
creator: Stephane Kirkland
desc: Napoleon III and a bureaucrat named Haussmann tore the medieval city apart and rebuilt it as boulevards, in twenty years. Half of Paris hated them for it. The Palais Garnier was the showpiece, and it sits where several boulevards meet.

title: Vanished Smile
creator: R.A. Scotti
desc: In 1911 someone walked out of the Louvre with the Mona Lisa under his coat. It was gone for two years, Picasso was arrested, and the empty wall became a tourist attraction. A funny, brisk book about how she got famous.

title: The Judgment of Paris
creator: Ross King
desc: Manet’s paintings were rejected and mocked, and the establishment star everyone loved is now forgotten. The story of how Impressionism won. The Musée d’Orsay, in a converted railway station, has the paintings the Salon threw out.

title: Is Paris Burning?
place: Le Meurice hotel, Rue de Rivoli
creator: Larry Collins & Dominique Lapierre
desc: Hitler ordered Paris destroyed as the Allies closed in. The German commander stalled, and the city survived. Written from interviews with the people involved, and it moves like a thriller. Von Choltitz gave the order not to burn it from the Hôtel Meurice.

title: The Chairfather: Père Lachaise Part I
creator: Joe Start
desc: A cemetery walk through one-third of Père Lachaise. From the Gambetta entrance, it visits the graves of Oscar Wilde, Édith Piaf, Modigliani, and Sarah Bernhardt, among others.

title: Occupation and Liberation with Context: A World War II Tour of Paris
creator: Context Travel
desc: A history walk tracing Nazi occupation and the Resistance. From Hôtel Lutetia — once a haunt of Hemingway and Josephine Baker, later Nazi counter-intelligence HQ — it passes the original Shakespeare and Company, ending at the Mémorial de la Shoah.

title: Le Marais: Secret Stories & Invisible Details
creator: Corey Frye
desc: A discovery-style walk through hidden details of the Marais. From Metro Saint-Paul, it passes Place des Vosges and Musée Carnavalet, ending on Rue François Miron.

title: Saint-Germain-des-Prés: An Authentic Paris Neighborhood
creator: Annie Sargent
desc: A history walk through the literary heart of the Left Bank. From Mabillon Metro, it passes Les Deux Magots and Café de Flore, where Sartre and de Beauvoir debated, and where the guillotine was perfected, ending at the Deyrolle cabinet of curiosities.

title: Le Marais: The Paris Neighborhood That Has It All!
creator: Annie Sargent
desc: A history walk through the medieval quarter Haussmann never modernized. From Pont Marie, it passes the Hôtel de Sens, with a cannonball still in its facade, and Place des Vosges, ending near the National Archives.

title: A Moveable Feast
creator: Ernest Hemingway
