desc: Hemingway remembers being young, broke, and happy in 1920s Paris, and settles scores with everyone. It’s short, and half the myth of literary Paris comes from it. Shakespeare and Company still trades on the Left Bank, opposite Notre-Dame.

title: Île de la Cité: Where Paris Was Born
creator: Annie Sargent
desc: A history walk tracing 2,000 years on the island where Paris began. From Pont des Arts, it crosses to the Île de la Cité past the Conciergerie, where Marie-Antoinette stood trial, and Sainte-Chapelle, ending at the Deportation Martyrs Memorial.

title: Seven Ages of Paris
creator: Alistair Horne
desc: Two thousand years of Paris in one readable narrative, told through the people who ran it and the mobs who threw them out. A good spine to hang everything else on. The Île de la Cité is the island where the city started.

title: The French Intifada
creator: Andrew Hussey
desc: The riots in the estates outside Paris are not new, and Hussey traces them back through Algeria and the empire. Uncomfortable and necessary. Saint-Denis, north of the ring road, is one of the places he means.

title: How Paris Became Paris
creator: Joan DeJean
desc: How Paris invented the modern city: pavements, street lighting, public parks, and the idea of walking around for pleasure. Most of it happened in the 1600s. The Pont Neuf was the first bridge built without houses on it, so people could look at the view.

title: Massacre: The Life and Death of the Paris Commune
creator: John Merriman
desc: In 1871 Paris rose, ran itself for ten weeks, and was then crushed by the French army, which killed thousands in a week. Merriman is furious and fair. The last Communards were shot against a wall in Père Lachaise cemetery.

title: Suite Française
creator: Irène Némirovsky
desc: A Russian-Jewish novelist wrote this in 1942 about France collapsing around her, and was then deported to Auschwitz and killed. Her daughters kept the notebook for sixty years without reading it. The Mémorial de la Shoah names the French dead.

title: At the Existentialist Café
creator: Sarah Bakewell
desc: Sartre, Beauvoir, Camus and their friends argued about freedom in cafés and made a philosophy out of it. Bakewell makes it clear and gossipy and alive. The Café de Flore on Boulevard Saint-Germain is where they sat and worked.

title: Marcel Proust: A Life
creator: Edmund White
desc: A short life of Proust, by a novelist: the asthma, the closet, the mother, the twelve years in a cork-lined room. It’s an ideal way in without reading three thousand pages. The Musée Carnavalet has his actual bedroom.

title: Paris Noir
creator: Tyler Stovall
desc: Black Americans came to Paris to be treated as people, from the jazz players of the 1920s to Baldwin and Baker. Stovall shows what they found, and what they didn’t. Montmartre was the first centre of it, full of clubs and musicians.

title: Down and Out in Paris and London
creator: George Orwell
desc: Orwell, broke on purpose, works eighteen-hour shifts as a plongeur in a hotel kitchen and reports exactly what poverty costs. Short and clear. He lived on the Rue du Pot de Fer, in the fifth, and called it the Rue du Coq d’Or.

title: My Life in France
creator: Julia Child
desc: A large American woman lands in France in 1948, eats a sole meunière, and decides to learn everything. Warm, funny, and about finding your life late. She trained at Le Cordon Bleu, and lived on the Left Bank.

title: Hergé: The Man Who Created Tintin
creator: Pierre Assouline
desc: The definitive life of the Brussels illustrator who gave the world Tintin — the boyish genius, the wartime compromises, the private torment behind the clear line. Frank and gripping. Brussels’ comic art lives on in this Horta-built museum.

title: Brussels: A Cultural and Literary History
creator: André de Vries
desc: A learned, affectionate walk through the city’s whole story — swamp village to Burgundian capital to Belgian crossroads — chasing its writers, painters and outsiders. It starts on the Grand-Place, the gilded square at the city’s heart.

title: Expo 58
creator: Jonathan Coe
desc: A gentle, funny Cold War spy caper: a mild London civil servant is sent to run a pub at the 1958 Brussels World’s Fair and finds sex, secrets and Belgian beer. It all revolves around the Atomium, the fair’s gleaming steel symbol.

title: Edith Cavell
place: Tir National memorial (Edith Cavell execution site)
creator: Diana Souhami
desc: The British nurse who ran a Brussels clinic, smuggled 200 soldiers out of occupied Belgium, and was shot by the Germans in 1915 — becoming a propaganda saint. She was executed at the Tir National, the old firing range.

title: The Burgundians: A Vanished Empire
creator: Bart Van Loo
desc: The rollicking rise and fall of the Burgundian dukes who, from Bruges to Brussels, forged the Low Countries into Europe’s richest realm — feasts, feuds, Van Eyck and Charles the Bold. Their Brussels seat was the Coudenberg palace, now ruins.

title: A Tall Man in a Low Land
creator: Harry Pearson
desc: An Englishman roams Belgium — its beer, chips, comics, surrealists and cheerful refusal to take itself seriously — and falls for the least glamorous country in Europe. Its spirit is the Manneken Pis, a statue of a weeing boy.

title: Magritte: A Life
place: René Magritte Museum (his house in Jette)
creator: Alex Danchev
desc: The bowler hats, the pipe that is not a pipe, the raining men: Danchev’s rich life of the surrealist who painted the impossible from a modest Brussels row house. Playful and deep. He worked for 24 years in this Jette home, now his museum.

title: Villette
place: St Michael and St Gudula Cathedral (area)
creator: Charlotte Brontë
desc: Charlotte Brontë’s intense masterpiece: a lonely Englishwoman teaches in a girls’ school in ‘Villette’ — Brussels barely disguised — and burns with longing and dread. Drawn from her own year here. The pensionnat stood by the cathedral.

title: The Passage to Europe
creator: Luuk van Middelaar
desc: The clearest account of how the European Union actually works and grew — written by an insider who watched the deals up close. Dry-witted and illuminating. Its engine is the Berlaymont, the cruciform tower where the Commission sits.

title: King Leopold’s Ghost
creator: Adam Hochschild
desc: How Belgium’s King Leopold II turned the Congo into a private rubber empire that killed millions — and the campaigners who exposed it. He never set foot there; he ran it from Brussels and spent the loot on arches like this one.

title: Wicked City: The Many Cultures of Marseille
creator: Nicholas Hewitt
desc: A lively cultural history of France’s oldest, unruliest city — Greek colony, pirate port, immigrant crossroads, drug capital, and eternal thorn in Paris’s side. The best single guide. It all radiates from the Vieux-Port, 2,600 years old.

title: The Count of Monte Cristo
creator: Alexandre Dumas
desc: The greatest revenge story ever told: a young Marseille sailor is framed, buried alive in an island fortress, escapes, and returns as a fabulously rich avenger. Pure, unputdownable. It opens in the port and darkens at the Château d’If.

title: Marseille Mix
creator: William Firebrace
desc: An architect’s kaleidoscopic tour of Marseille — its harbours, tower blocks, films, gangsters and food, assembled in fragments like the city itself. It lingers at Le Corbusier’s Cité Radieuse, the concrete ‘vertical village’ on the hill.

title: Marseille Noir
creator: Cédric Fabre (ed.)
desc: Fourteen local writers take you into the real Marseille — the markets, estates and back rooms where the crime stories live, far from the postcard. Gritty and various. Many begin in Noailles, the teeming immigrant market that is the city’s belly.

title: Surrender on Demand
place: Site of the Villa Air-Bel, La Pomme
creator: Varian Fry
desc: The American who came to Marseille in 1940 and smuggled 2,000 people out of Vichy France — Chagall, Ernst, Arendt, Breton — tells it himself. He hid artists at the Villa Air-Bel in La Pomme, holding surrealist parties as the net closed.

title: Transit
creator: Anna Seghers
desc: 1940: refugees trapped in Marseille chase visas, stamps and ships out of a doomed Europe, in a hypnotic novel of waiting and identity by a writer who lived it. A masterpiece. They haunt the consulates and cafés along the Canebière, going nowhere.

title: Total Chaos
creator: Jean-Claude Izzo
desc: The novel that invented Mediterranean noir: a burnt-out Marseille cop hunts the killers of childhood friends through a city of immigrants, racism, pastis and the sea. It lives in the Panier, the old quarter above the port.

title: Banjo
creator: Claude McKay
desc: A Harlem Renaissance novel set on the 1920s Marseille docks, among Black sailors and drifters from Africa, America and the Caribbean, living free and broke by the sea. Loose, jazzy, radical. Their world was the waterfront around the Joliette basins.

title: My Father’s Glory & My Mother’s Castle
creator: Marcel Pagnol
desc: Pagnol’s sunlit memories of a Provençal boyhood — summers in the hills of thyme and cicadas above Marseille, a schoolmaster father, a first hunt. Warm and golden. He was born in Aubagne, east of the city, at the foot of the Garlaban he made famous.

title: The Miniaturist
creator: Jessie Burton
desc: A young bride in 1686 gets a dollhouse-sized replica of her home, and a mysterious craftsman starts filling it. The real dollhouse it’s based on belonged to Petronella Oortman, and you can see it in the Rijksmuseum.

title: Van Gogh: The Life
creator: Steven Naifeh & Gregory White Smith
desc: Ten years of painting, 900 canvases, almost none sold. The big, definitive biography, built on his letters. It’s long. The Van Gogh Museum on Museumplein holds the largest collection of his work, hung in the order he painted it.

title: Amsterdam: A History of the World’s Most Liberal City
creator: Russell Shorto
desc: An American historian argues that Amsterdam invented liberalism: tolerance, free trade, free thought. It’s the best single book on why the city is the way it is. Dam Square, the plaza at the centre, is where the original dam across the Amstel stood.

title: The Diary of a Young Girl
creator: Anne Frank
desc: Two years hidden with seven other people in rooms behind a bookcase, written by a girl between 13 and 15. Then someone gave them away. The annex is at Prinsengracht 263, and the rooms were left unfurnished on purpose.

title: We Slaves of Suriname
creator: Anton de Kom
desc: The first history of Suriname written by a Surinamese man, furious and beautiful. Banned, then forgotten, then a Dutch bestseller after 2020. De Kom died in a Nazi camp. The square named for him is in the Bijlmer, the Surinamese heart of the city.

title: Tulipomania
creator: Mike Dash
desc: In the 1630s a single tulip bulb could cost as much as a canal house. Then the market crashed in a week. Dash tells it as a proper story, not a morality tale. The Bloemenmarkt, a floating flower market on the Singel canal, still sells the bulbs.

title: Nathaniel’s Nutmeg
creator: Giles Milton
desc: Tiny Run island grew nutmeg, so England and Holland fought over it for years. England gave up its claim in 1667 and took Manhattan instead. The deal was done by the Dutch East India Company, whose old headquarters still stands on Oude Hoogstraat.

title: The Hidden Life of Otto Frank
creator: Carol Ann Lee
desc: The father who survived, and the question nobody has answered: who betrayed them. A careful, unsettling biography. Before hiding, the Franks lived at Merwedeplein 37, a normal flat in a normal square in the south of the city.

title: Betraying Spinoza
creator: Rebecca Goldstein
desc: A philosopher’s warm, personal book about the glass-grinder who said God is just nature, and got thrown out of his community for it. He was 23. The ban was read aloud in the Portuguese Synagogue on Mr. Visserplein, which is still in use.

title: Murder in Amsterdam
creator: Ian Buruma
desc: In 2004 a filmmaker was shot and stabbed in the street for a film about Islam and women. Buruma asks what it cost the Dutch idea of tolerance. The memorial, a jagged steel sculpture called De Schreeuw, stands in the Oosterpark.

title: Amsterdam: A Brief Life of the City
creator: Geert Mak
desc: A short, beautiful life story of the city, by a Dutch historian. It starts with fishermen on a boggy river mouth and ends with the modern city. The Oude Kerk, the oldest building in Amsterdam, went up when the place was still mostly mud.

title: In the City of Bikes
creator: Pete Jordan
desc: An American moves over, falls for the bikes, and digs up the whole history: the 1890s craze, bikes in the resistance, the white bicycle scheme, the men who fish them out of the canals. Vondelpark is where the city rides on a sunny day.

title: A Short History of Byzantium
creator: John Julius Norwich
desc: A thousand years of Byzantium — emperors, icons, palace blindings and sieges — boiled down from Norwich’s three-volume epic into one propulsive read. Gossipy and grand. It all radiated from Hagia Sophia, the domed church at the empire’s heart.

title: Constantinople: City of the World’s Desire, 1453–1924
creator: Philip Mansel
desc: The definitive portrait of Ottoman Istanbul — sultans, eunuchs, dragomans, dervishes, the multi-faith street — across five centuries. It all turned on Topkapı Palace, the walled world the empire was run from and rarely left.

title: Empress of the East
creator: Leslie Peirce
desc: How a captured slave girl became Roxelana, wife and partner of Suleiman the Magnificent, breaking every rule of the harem. Peirce tells it with scholarship and verve. She lies beside Suleiman at the Süleymaniye, the great mosque their age built.

title: The Turkish Embassy Letters
creator: Lady Mary Wortley Montagu
desc: An English ambassador’s wife writes home from 1717 Istanbul — the harem, the baths, the smallpox inoculation she’d bring to Europe — with wit and a rare eye for women’s lives. Her famous bath scene unfolds in a hamam like Çemberlitaş.

title: Galata Photo Tour
creator: Kemal Nuraydin
desc: A photography walk through historic Galata, led by a former National Geographic Turkey editor. From a park over the Golden Horn, it passes a 700-year-old Genoese tower and tiled stairs through an old synagogue quarter, ending at a waterside fish market.

title: Under the Shadow
creator: Kaya Genç
desc: A young Istanbul writer maps his polarised country through its angry youth — secular and Islamist, both raised on grievance — around the 2013 Gezi protests. Sharp and even-handed. It begins where the revolt did, in Gezi Park above Taksim Square.

title: Midnight at the Pera Palace
creator: Charles King
desc: How Constantinople became Istanbul between the wars — the last caliph, Atatürk’s revolution, jazz, spies, White Russians and refugees. King makes it sparkle. Much of it played out at the Pera Palace, the grand hotel built for the Orient Express.

title: Constantinople: The Last Great Siege, 1453
creator: Roger Crowley
desc: The fifty-day siege that ended the Roman Empire, told hour by hour: cannon, a chain across the harbour, a boy-sultan and a doomed emperor. Crowley makes it thunder. The Turks broke through the land walls here at Edirnekapı, and the medieval world ended.

title: 10 Minutes 38 Seconds in This Strange World
creator: Elif Shafak
desc: As a murdered sex worker’s mind flickers out, she recalls her life and her five misfit friends — the Istanbul the city disowns. Warm and angry. It ends at the Cemetery of the Companionless in Kilyos, where the unclaimed are buried by number.

title: Istanbul: Memories and the City
creator: Orhan Pamuk
desc: Pamuk’s memoir of growing up in a fading city, and of hüzün — the shared melancholy of ruins, black-and-white winters and lost empire. The book that defines literary Istanbul. It centres on his family’s flats in Nişantaşı, where he still lives.

title: A Useless Man: Selected Stories
creator: Sait Faik Abasıyanık
desc: Quiet, tender stories of Istanbul’s small people — fishermen, layabouts, Greek and Armenian neighbours — by the writer who loved the city’s edges. A Chekhov of the Bosphorus. He wrote many on Burgazada, the island where his house is now a museum.

title: A Mind at Peace
creator: Ahmet Hamdi Tanpınar
desc: The great modern Turkish novel: a love affair in 1930s Istanbul shadowed by the coming war, steeped in Ottoman music and the ache of a culture between East and West. It breathes the Bosphorus shore, the yalıs and tea gardens of Emirgan.

title: Constantinople
creator: Edmondo De Amicis
desc: The most dazzling travel book about the 19th-century city: an Italian journalist drunk on its colour, squalor and crowds, sentence after sentence. Umberto Eco loved it. The whole human tide crosses at the Galata Bridge, where he lingers longest.

title: The Fall of Milošević: The October 5th Revolution
creator: Dragan Bujošević & Ivan Radovanović
desc: Two Belgrade journalists reconstruct 5 October 2000 hour by hour: the bulldozer, the crowd, the police who stood aside, a regime that folded in a day. The parliament they stormed and burned still stands on Nikola Pašić Square.

title: A Guide to the Serbian Mentality
creator: Momo Kapor
desc: Short comic pieces on how Serbs eat, argue, mourn and lie to foreigners, sold in every bookshop in the city. Kapor also backed the wars and reported from Bosnian Serb lines; read him knowing that. Skadarlija is his territory.

title: Black Lamb and Grey Falcon
creator: Rebecca West
desc: A British writer travelled Yugoslavia in 1937 and produced the strangest, richest travel book in English. She loves the place and is often wrong about it. It’s very long. She sees Belgrade from Kalemegdan, where the two rivers meet.

title: Tito
creator: Neil Barnett
desc: A short, sceptical life of the man who held six republics together for thirty-five years by charm, secret police and playing Moscow off against Washington. Tito is buried in the House of Flowers, in a garden above the city.

title: The Other Side of Everything (Druga strana svega)
creator: Mila Turajlić
desc: A locked door in the director’s Belgrade apartment, sealed when the communists split the family flat in 1945, opens onto a century of Serbian politics. Her mother, an opposition activist, is the spine. Vračar, the quarter of the apartment.

title: The Serbs: History, Myth and the Destruction of Yugoslavia
creator: Tim Judah
desc: How Serbs came to understand themselves through a battle they lost in 1389, and what that did in the 1990s. Judah reported the wars and writes without contempt or excuses. The Church of Saint Sava is that idea built in concrete and marble.

title: Belgrade: A Cultural History
creator: David A. Norris
desc: A literary historian walks the city through its writers and its twenty-odd destructions — Roman, Ottoman, Habsburg, Nazi, NATO. The best single book on why Belgrade looks unfinished. Knez Mihailova is the promenade where all of it gets rebuilt.

title: McMafia
creator: Misha Glenny
desc: Organised crime after communism, and the Belgrade chapters are the sharpest: paramilitaries who became gangsters, and the 2003 murder of the prime minister who tried to stop them. Đinđić was shot outside the government building on Nemanjina.

title: The Death of Yugoslavia
creator: Laura Silber & Allan Little
desc: Two BBC journalists reconstruct the break-up from the inside, having interviewed nearly everyone who caused it. Still the clearest account of how a country was talked into war. Republic Square is where Belgraders came out against it in 1991.

title: In the Hold
creator: Vladimir Arsenijević
desc: A hundred pages from Belgrade in the winter of 1991: young people, bad flats, heroin, a brother sent to the front, the war arriving as rumour and television. It won Serbia’s biggest literary prize. Zemun still feels like a separate town.

title: Conversations with Stalin
creator: Milovan Djilas
desc: Tito’s deputy went to Moscow three times, met Stalin and wrote it down: the flattery, the drinking, the menace. It explains the 1948 split that let Yugoslavia go its own way. The Ušće tower was the Communist Party headquarters.

title: The Book of Kells
place: Book of Kells, Old Library, Trinity College
creator: Bernard Meehan
desc: Trinity’s own manuscript keeper explains the 1,200-year-old gospel book everyone queues for: who made it, what the pictures mean, why the cats and snakes. The Old Library at Trinity College shows one page at a time.

title: Dublin: A Cultural History
creator: Siobhán Kilfeather
desc: A short cultural history of the city, organised by what’s actually there: the river, the pubs, the statues, the ghosts. Good for orientation without a lecture. The Spire on O’Connell Street stands where Nelson’s Pillar was blown up in 1966.

title: Dublin Tenement Life: An Oral History
creator: Kevin C. Kearns
desc: Dubliners who grew up in the tenements, in their own words. Whole families in one room, shared taps, and appalling landlords. It is often very funny. 14 Henrietta Street is a Georgian house kept exactly as it was, and you can walk through it.

title: Easter 1916: The Irish Rebellion
creator: Charles Townshend
desc: Just over a thousand rebels seized buildings in 1916, held out for a week, and lost. Then Britain shot the leaders and lost Ireland. Townshend is clear and unromantic. The GPO on O’Connell Street was headquarters; the bullet marks are still there.

title: The Speckled People
creator: Hugo Hamilton
desc: A boy grows up in 1950s Dublin speaking German to his mother and Irish to his father, and gets beaten in the street for both. A quiet, beautiful memoir about not belonging. The family lived in Dún Laoghaire, on the coast south of the city.

title: Michael Collins
creator: Tim Pat Coogan
desc: The guerrilla organiser who invented modern urban warfare, negotiated the treaty that split the country, and was shot at 31 by his own side. Coogan is partisan and gripping. Collins is buried in Glasnevin Cemetery, north of the river.

title: Are You Somebody?
creator: Nuala O’Faolain
desc: A woman in her fifties writes about a Dublin childhood of drink and neglect, and a life spent alone. It became a huge, unlikely bestseller because people saw themselves in it. She lived and worked around Ranelagh, south of the canal.

title: Republic of Shame
place: Former Magdalene laundry, Seán McDermott Street
creator: Caelainn Hogan
desc: Ireland locked up unmarried mothers and took their babies, into the 1990s. Hogan tracks down the women, the nuns, and the paperwork. The last Magdalene laundry, on Seán McDermott Street, closed in 1996 and still stands.

title: We Don’t Know Ourselves
creator: Fintan O’Toole
desc: A history of modern Ireland by a man born in 1958, who watched the Church, the state, and the whole official story fall apart. Superb, and very funny. O’Toole grew up in Crumlin, a corporation housing estate on the southwest edge.

title: Borstal Boy
creator: Brendan Behan
desc: Behan was sixteen when the English arrested him with explosives. This is the reform-school memoir he wrote about it: funny, filthy, and generous. He drank at McDaid’s on Harry Street, which is a working pub a minute off Grafton Street.

title: Ulysses
creator: James Joyce
desc: One ordinary Dublin day, 16 June 1904, followed hour by hour through real streets, pubs, and shops. It is hard, and you can read it in pieces. It opens at the Martello tower in Sandycove, which is now a small free museum you can climb.

title: The Almost Nearly Perfect People
creator: Michael Booth
desc: A funny, sharp tour of the Nordic countries and the myths around them — including oil-rich, self-satisfied, quietly anxious Norway. Oslo’s City Hall, where the Nobel Peace Prize is handed over, is the country’s civic stage.

title: Built, Burned, and Reborn: A Copenhagen Walking Tour
creator: Pernille Schlander
desc: A history walk tracing 1,000 years of fires, rebuilding, and royal ambition. At a castle-island square on a Viking-age harbor, it passes the site of five royal castles and an old astronomical tower, ending at a Dutch Renaissance palace and rose garden.

title: Danish Design: Classic Modern Style via Neo-Classicism and Art Nouveau
creator: Kay Xander Mellish
desc: An architecture walk tracing Danish design from postwar modernism back through Art Nouveau. Starting at a green-glass postwar hotel, it passes an Art Nouveau town hall and a canal lined with vintage design auction houses, ending at a design museum.

title: Room 606: The SAS House and the Work of Arne Jacobsen
creator: Michael Sheridan
desc: Arne Jacobsen designed a hotel and everything in it, down to the cutlery and the door handles. Room 606 is the last one kept as he left it. You can book it. The Radisson Royal on Hammerichsgade is the building, and it still looks like the future.

title: The Children of Ash and Elm
creator: Neil Price
desc: What the Vikings were actually like: their gods, their slaves, their ships, their strange minds. The best popular book on them by a mile. The National Museum holds the real objects, and it’s a short walk from the harbour.

title: Philosopher of the Heart: The Restless Life of Søren Kierkegaard
creator: Clare Carlisle
desc: Kierkegaard walked these streets picking fights, broke off the engagement that haunted him, and more or less invented modern anxiety. Carlisle makes him human and gripping. He is buried in Assistens Cemetery, in Nørrebro.

title: Copenhagenize
creator: Mikael Colville-Andersen
desc: Copenhagen rebuilt itself around bicycles on purpose, and this is the man who sells that idea to other cities. Practical, opinionated, and it explains what you’re looking at. Dronning Louises Bro carries about 40,000 cyclists a day.

title: Hungry
creator: Jeff Gordinier
desc: A food writer follows René Redzepi around for four years, foraging ants and closing restaurants. It’s about obsession more than food. Noma sits out on Refshalevej, in an old naval warehouse district, and it changed how the world eats.

title: Countrymen
creator: Bo Lidegaard
desc: In October 1943 the Danes moved 7,000 Jews to Sweden by boat in three weeks, nearly all of them. Lidegaard uses the letters and diaries of the people who did it. The Danish Jewish Museum tells the story where it happened.

title: The Almost Nearly Perfect People
creator: Michael Booth
desc: A grumpy Englishman living in Denmark asks why the Nordics keep winning happiness surveys, and finds the answers awkward. Funny and rude and useful. Rådhuspladsen, the City Hall square, is the middle of the country he is picking apart.

title: Hans Christian Andersen: The Life of a Storyteller
creator: Jackie Wullschlager
desc: The fairy tales came out of a cobbler’s son who arrived in Copenhagen at fourteen with nothing, and spent his life feeling ugly and unloved. A superb biography. Andersen lived on Nyhavn, the canal quay, in three different houses over the years.

title: Smilla’s Sense of Snow
creator: Peter Høeg
desc: A half-Greenlandic woman in Copenhagen refuses to believe a boy fell off a roof, and pulls at the thread of Denmark’s colonial hold on Greenland. The Christianshavn canals are where she lives, and where the book starts.

title: Copenhagen
creator: Michael Frayn
desc: In 1941 Heisenberg visited Bohr in occupied Copenhagen, they argued, and nobody knows what was said. Frayn’s play circles the mystery. It’s short. The Niels Bohr Institute on Blegdamsvej is where the conversation happened.

title: Isak Dinesen: The Life of a Storyteller
creator: Judith Thurman
desc: Before she wrote Out of Africa she was a Danish baroness who lost a farm, a husband, and a lover, and came home to write. Thurman won a National Book Award for this. Her house at Rungsted, north of the city, is a museum.

title: Vasa: A Swedish Warship
creator: Fred Hocker
desc: The king built the most heavily armed warship in the world, it sailed 1,300 metres, and it capsized. Three hundred years in the mud preserved it almost whole. Written by the museum’s own archaeologist. The Vasa is now the ship in the room.

title: Stockholm Walking Tour: A Tour from Sergels Torg to its City Hall
creator: Irina Kåvik
desc: A short walk through the modern centre to the landmark City Hall. From a downtown mall, it passes the cultural centre, main square, and central station, ending at the waterfront hall where the Nobel Prize banquet is held each year.

title: Our House Is on Fire
creator: Malena & Greta Thunberg
desc: A family falls apart as one daughter stops eating and starts protesting, written by her mother. It is about a child, and about climate, and it is not a polemic. She sat outside the Riksdag with a hand-painted sign.

title: Blood on the Snow: The Killing of Olof Palme
creator: Jan Bondeson
desc: In 1986 the prime minister walked home from the cinema with no bodyguards and was shot in the street. Nobody has been convicted. Bondeson lays out the mess. A plaque marks the spot on Sveavägen, and people still leave flowers.

title: Raoul Wallenberg
creator: Ingrid Carlberg
desc: A Swedish diplomat saved tens of thousands of Hungarian Jews in 1944, then vanished into Soviet custody and was never seen again. It’s long, and definitive. Raoul Wallenbergs torg is the square named for him.

title: The Nordic Cookbook
creator: Magnus Nilsson
desc: A Swedish chef spent years collecting the everyday food of the whole Nordic region, and it turns out to be much stranger than meatballs. Huge, beautiful, and genuinely useful. Östermalms Saluhall has been the city’s food hall since 1888.

title: Roseanna
creator: Maj Sjöwall & Per Wahlöö
desc: The first Nordic noir, and the two authors wrote ten of them as a deliberate critique of the Swedish welfare state. Cold, plain, and the ancestor of everything since. Martin Beck’s police headquarters was on Kungsholmen.

title: Astrid Lindgren: The Woman Behind Pippi Longstocking
creator: Jens Andersen
desc: The woman who invented Pippi Longstocking had a secret son, fought the Swedish tax system in public, and helped end corporal punishment. A brisk and surprising life. She lived at Dalagatan 46 for over sixty years.

title: Strindberg: A Life
creator: Sue Prideaux
desc: Strindberg wrote furious plays, hated women, hated men, believed in alchemy, and changed European theatre anyway. Prideaux is funny and unsparing. His last flat, the Blue Tower on Drottninggatan, is a museum with his library.

title: Bright Lights Dark Shadows: The Real Story of ABBA
creator: Carl Magnus Palm
desc: The definitive book on ABBA: four people, two marriages, both ending, and the songs written while it happened. Fair to the music and the mess. ABBA The Museum is on Djurgården, and it is more fun than it has any right to be.

title: The Nobel Prize: A History of Genius, Controversy and Prestige
creator: Burton Feldman
desc: Where the prizes came from, how the committees actually choose, and who they have shamefully missed. Gossipy and clear. The Nobel Prize Museum is on Stortorget, the square in the old town where the 1520 bloodbath happened.

title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo
creator: Stieg Larsson
desc: A journalist and a hacker dig into a rich family’s secrets. It is a thriller and the city is the backdrop, but the addresses are real and the walking tours exist. Blomkvist’s flat is Bellmansgatan 1, on Södermalm.

title: The Children of Ash and Elm
creator: Neil Price
desc: What the Vikings were actually like: their gods, their slaves, their ships, their strange minds. The best popular book on them by a mile. The Swedish History Museum holds the gold and the grave goods, out in Östermalm.

title: Edvard Munch: Behind the Scream
creator: Sue Prideaux
desc: The life behind The Scream: illness, drink, doomed love and breakdown, and the Oslo fjord light that Munch turned into raw feeling. His work now fills the MUNCH, the tall waterfront museum in Bjørvika built to hold it.

title: Oslo Walking Tour: A Waterfront Stroll from East to West
creator: Stormposten Lars Engerengen
desc: A scenic waterfront walk from the Munch Museum through Aker Brygge to Tjuvholmen. It passes the Opera House, Akershus Fortress, City Hall, the Nobel Peace Center, and the National Museum, ending at Albert Nordengens Plass.

title: Farthest North
creator: Fridtjof Nansen
desc: Nansen’s own account of the maddest polar gamble: freeze a ship into the ice and drift toward the North Pole, then ski off across the floes when it isn’t enough. His ship, the Fram, still stands in its Bygdøy museum.

title: Classic Oslo Walking Tour: Central Station to The Akershus Castle and Fortress
creator: Stormposten Lars Engerengen
desc: A history walk along the eastern waterfront to the 14th-century Akershus Fortress. From Central Station, it passes the Opera House and the Havnelageret warehouse, a WWII shelter, ending at panoramic bay views from the fortress.

title: Kon-Tiki
creator: Thor Heyerdahl
desc: In 1947 six Norwegians sailed a balsa-wood raft 8,000 km across the Pacific to prove ancient people could have. Heyerdahl tells it with boyish glee; it sold millions. The raft itself sits in its own museum on Bygdøy, next door to the Fram.

title: Hunger
creator: Knut Hamsun
desc: A starving young writer wanders 1890 Kristiania, too proud to beg, half-mad with hunger and pride, in a novel that invented the modern interior voice. It ends at the harbour, where he finally ships out of the city that broke him.

title: Henrik Ibsen: A New Biography
creator: Robert Ferguson
desc: The definitive life of the theatre’s great modern founder — the prickly, self-exiled Norwegian who turned drawing rooms into powder kegs with A Doll’s House and Hedda Gabler. He took his daily lunch here at the Grand Café, in his reserved chair.

title: The Redbreast
creator: Jo Nesbø
desc: The Harry Hole novel that made Nesbø: a neo-Nazi plot with roots in Norway’s shameful WWII collaboration, chased by a brilliant, self-destructive Oslo cop. Twisty and dark. Harry drinks at Schrøder, his real down-at-heel local pub.

title: In the Wake
creator: Per Petterson
desc: Six years after losing his parents in a ferry fire, a numb Oslo man tries to write, to father, to keep going. Petterson’s spare, aching novel of grief and slow repair. It circles the bookshop on Bogstadveien where the narrator once worked.

title: One of Us
creator: Åsne Seierstad
desc: The definitive account of 22 July 2011: how a lonely Norwegian built a bomb, drove it into Oslo’s government quarter, then shot 69 mostly teenagers on Utøya — and how the country reckoned with it. Devastating, humane. The bomb went off here.

title: The Half Brother
creator: Lars Saabye Christensen
desc: A sprawling, tender Oslo family saga across the 20th century — a boy, his mute giant half-brother, their actress mother and grandmother, secrets and film reels. Christensen’s big-hearted epic. It roams the west-end streets around Bislett.

title: The Nordic Theory of Everything
creator: Anu Partanen
desc: A Finnish journalist moves to New York and ends up explaining why Finland’s schools, healthcare and parental leave make people less dependent on one another, not more. Argumentative and warm. Oodi is that argument built as a building.

title: Engel to Aalto: A Helsinki Architecture Walking Tour
creator: Ed Morrow
desc: An architecture walk tracing 200 years of Helsinki styles, from neoclassicism to modernism. From the cathedral square, it passes an Art Nouveau building with national-epic sculptures and a converted fire station, ending at a striking wooden library.

title: A History of Finland
creator: Henrik Meinander
desc: The short, clear account of how a Swedish borderland became a Russian grand duchy and then a country that survived the twentieth century by very fine margins. Meinander writes without nationalism. Senate Square was built to look imperial, because it was.

title: The Final Act: The Helsinki Accords and the Transformation of the Cold War
creator: Michael Cotey Morgan
desc: Thirty-five leaders signed a document in Helsinki in 1975 that looked like a Soviet win and turned out to be a time bomb of human rights language. Morgan makes diplomacy gripping. Finlandia Hall is the room where they signed it.

title: The Kalevala
creator: Elias Lönnrot
desc: The oral folk poetry Lönnrot collected on foot in the 1830s, stitched into the epic that gave Finland a past to be a nation with. Strange, funny, full of magic singing. It’s long; dip in. The Ateneum hangs Gallen-Kallela’s paintings of it.

title: The Wednesday Club
creator: Kjell Westö
desc: Helsinki in 1938, six men who meet on Wednesdays, and the 1918 civil war none of them will name aloud. A novel about a country deciding what to forget. The Kämp is the kind of place they drink in, and it is still standing.

title: A Frozen Hell: The Russo-Finnish Winter War of 1939–1940
creator: William R. Trotter
desc: For 105 days in 1939 Finland fought the Soviet Union alone, in forty below, on skis, and did not lose. Trotter tells it as narrative and does not turn it into a fairy tale. Mannerheim commanded, and rides in bronze on the street named for him.

title: The Finnish Cookbook
creator: Beatrice Ojakangas
desc: A Finnish-American who learned it from her mother, writing down rye bread, cardamom buns, salmon soup and the pancake you bake in the oven. In print since 1964 and still the one people cook from. The Old Market Hall sells the ingredients.

title: Sculptor’s Daughter
creator: Tove Jansson
desc: Before the Moomins, Jansson wrote twenty short chapters about being a child in a Helsinki artist’s household: her father’s plaster studio, parties, ice, fear. Nothing is explained and everything is exact. Katajanokka is where the flat was.

title: Unknown Soldiers
creator: Väinö Linna
desc: The machine-gun company Finland recognised as itself: conscripts who mock their officers, dig, die and win nothing. Linna was there. The book ended the country’s heroic war story. Hietaniemi holds the graves and the tomb of the unknown soldier.

title: Alvar Aalto: Architect
creator: John Stewart
desc: An architect’s frank life of the architect: the buildings, the furniture you have already sat in, the drinking, the two wives who were both his working partners. Aalto built his own house in Munkkiniemi in 1936 and you can walk through it.

title: Letters from Iceland
creator: W.H. Auden & Louis MacNeice
desc: Two English poets tour 1930s Iceland and send home a giddy scrapbook of verse, jokes and travel notes — the most charming odd book about the country. They landed by ship at Reykjavík’s harbour, where their Iceland began and ended.

title: Names for the Sea: Strangers in Iceland
creator: Sarah Moss
desc: A British writer moves her family to Reykjavík just after the crash and files a wry, sharp-eyed dispatch on daily life — weather, food, debt, hot pools and reticent neighbours. She taught at the university on the city’s western edge.

title: Moonstone: The Boy Who Never Was
creator: Sjón
desc: Reykjavík, 1918: as the Spanish flu empties the streets and a volcano reddens the sky, a queer teenage boy who lives for the cinema drifts through it all. Short and luminous. He haunts the picture houses like this one, Gamla Bíó, the Old Cinema.

title: The History of Iceland
creator: Gunnar Karlsson
desc: A clear, readable thousand-year story: the settlement, the medieval free state, six centuries of Danish rule and cold poverty, then independence. It centres on Austurvöllur, the square before the little parliament house.

title: Jar City
creator: Arnaldur Indriðason
desc: The Reykjavík crime novel that launched Nordic noir here: a lonely man murdered in his flat, a gloomy detective, and a genetic database that unlocks a buried crime. The victim lived in Norðurmýri, a plain grid of little houses.

title: Meltdown Iceland
creator: Roger Boyes
desc: How a tiny nation’s banks ballooned to ten times its economy, then vanished in weeks in 2008, ruining thousands. Furious crowds banged pots outside parliament on Austurvöllur until the government fell — the ‘Pots and Pans Revolution.’

title: Devil’s Island
place: Site of Camp Knox barracks, Vesturbær (area)
creator: Einar Kárason
desc: A rowdy novel of a working-class family in the 1950s shanty town that grew in abandoned US Army barracks on Reykjavík’s edge — Iceland lurching from turf to television. It rose in the west of the city, near where Vesturbær now spreads.

title: The Fish Can Sing
creator: Halldór Laxness
desc: Iceland’s Nobel laureate on a boy raised at Brekkukot, a turf cottage on the edge of old Reykjavík, among eccentrics and a mysterious world-famous singer. Brekkukot sat by the Tjörnin, the town pond still full of birds and light.

title: 101 Reykjavík
creator: Hallgrímur Helgason
desc: A jobless thirty-something layabout sponges off his mother, chases women and drifts through the bars of downtown Reykjavík in a haze of TV and hangovers. Sharp and filthy. His whole small world is the 101 postcode, strung along Laugavegur.

title: The Sagas of Icelanders
creator: Anonymous
desc: The founding literature of Iceland: cool, violent, weirdly modern tales of settlers, feuds and outlaws, in prose that reads like yesterday. Why Reykjavík is a City of Literature. It begins here, where Ingólfur first made land.

title: My Life as a Spy
creator: Katherine Verdery
desc: An American anthropologist reads the vast file the Securitate kept on her — informers, absurdity, real menace — and confronts the neighbours who watched her. It leads back to the square where the secret state finally fell.

title: The Last Hundred Days
creator: Patrick McGuinness
desc: A young Westerner drifts into a job in Bucharest in 1989, in the last delirious months of Ceaușescu — a city being demolished, everyone watched, the regime rotting. Eerie and elegant. Whole neighbourhoods fell for the dictator’s vast palace.

title: In Europe’s Shadow
creator: Robert D. Kaplan
desc: A veteran American traveller returns to the Romania he first saw under Ceaușescu, threading history, geopolitics and memory across four decades. Learned and personal. Bucharest’s Arc de Triomphe still salutes the France it once tried to be.

title: Life Begins on Friday
creator: Ioana Pârvulescu
desc: A gentle, time-slipping mystery set in the last days of 1897, when Bucharest was ‘Little Paris’ — horse-drawn, hopeful, about to meet the century. Its characters stroll the Cișmigiu, the beloved central park, exactly as they did then.

title: Romania: Borderland of Europe
creator: Lucian Boia
desc: Romania’s leading historian explains his country to outsiders — the Roman-Slavic-Ottoman crossroads, the myths, the Latin island in a Slavic sea, the wounds of communism. It circles the university, stage of Bucharest’s modern quarrels.

title: Journal 1935–1944: The Fascist Years
creator: Mihail Sebastian
desc: A Jewish writer’s diary as his beloved Bucharest turns fascist and his brilliant friends embrace the Iron Guard. Intimate, heartbreaking, essential. He watched from a city whose Jewish heart was the Choral Temple, wrecked by Legionaries in 1941.

title: Nostalgia
creator: Mircea Cărtărescu
desc: Hallucinatory linked tales of childhood in the grey tower blocks of communist Bucharest, where a boy’s games open onto the infinite. Cărtărescu is the city’s dreaming genius. His visions rise from the Obor and Colentina districts of his boyhood.

title: Wasted Morning
creator: Gabriela Adameșteanu
desc: A poor, sharp-tongued old woman looks back across Bucharest’s brutal century — two world wars, communism, the wreckers’ balls — from her shabby room. Her city’s old heart was flattened for the boulevards around Unirii.

title: The Balkan Trilogy
creator: Olivia Manning
desc: An English newlywed couple washes up in Bucharest as war breaks out in 1939 — the phony calm, the refugees, the rumours, the parties at the grand hotel. It centres on the Athénée Palace, the era’s great nest of spies and gossip.

title: L’incoronazione di Poppea: Pur ti miro
creator: Claudio Monteverdi
desc: The title means “I gaze at you,” the closing love duet of an opera first staged in Venice in 1643, possibly finished by a younger colleague. Monteverdi ran the music at St Mark’s for 30 years and is buried in the Frari basilica.

title: Oboe Concerto in D minor, Op. 9 No. 2: II. Adagio
creator: Tomaso Albinoni
desc: Albinoni, son of a Venetian paper merchant, never needed a church or court post. This slow movement is really his; the famous “Adagio in G minor” is mostly 1950s work by Remo Giazotto. He died in 1751 in the parish of San Barnaba church.

title: La biondina in gondoleta
place: Palazzo Querini Benzon on the Grand Canal
creator: Antonio Lamberti (traditional)
desc: Venetian for “the little blonde in the gondola.” Antonio Lamberti’s 1770s verses seem to address Countess Marina Querini Benzon, whose salon in this Grand Canal palazzo drew Byron. Beethoven cited the tune as typical Venetian music.

title: La traviata: Libiamo ne’ lieti calici
creator: Giuseppe Verdi
desc: The title means “let’s drink from the joyful cups,” the opera’s party toast. La traviata flopped at its La Fenice premiere in March 1853; Rigoletto had opened in the same opera house two years earlier.

title: The Four Seasons, Spring, RV 269: I. Allegro
creator: Antonio Vivaldi
desc: Vivaldi, the “Red Priest,” taught violin at the Ospedale della Pietà, whose orphan girl musicians were famous across Europe. The Pietà church on the waterfront was rebuilt after his death; concerts are still held inside.

title: Tristan und Isolde, Act 2: O sink hernieder, Nacht der Liebe
place: Palazzo Giustinian on the Grand Canal, Dorsoduro
creator: Richard Wagner
desc: The title means “descend, O night of love.” Wagner wrote the opera’s second act, its long nocturnal love scene, while renting rooms in Palazzo Giustinian on the Grand Canal in 1858–59, listening to gondoliers at night.

title: Les contes d’Hoffmann: Barcarolle (Belle nuit, ô nuit d’amour)
place: Grand Canal at the Accademia Bridge
creator: Jacques Offenbach
desc: “Beautiful night, O night of love.” A barcarolle is a gondolier’s song in a rocking rhythm; this one opens the opera’s Venice act, set in a courtesan’s Grand Canal palazzo.

title: Venezia
place: Ospedale Civile city hospital, Scuola Grande di San Marco
creator: Francesco Guccini
desc: Written with Gian Piero Alloisio, it sets a Venice sold to tourists, with a pizzeria called San Marco and smoke from Porto Marghera, against a young woman dying in childbirth in a big hospital.

title: La lugubre gondola
place: Ca’ Vendramin Calergi palazzo, now the Venice Casino
creator: Franz Liszt
desc: The title means “the mournful gondola.” Liszt wrote it in December 1882 while staying with his son-in-law Wagner at Ca’ Vendramin Calergi, as if foreseeing a funeral barge. Wagner died in this palazzo, now the city casino, weeks later.

title: Pin Floi
place: Bacino di San Marco, site of the 1989 Pink Floyd floating stage
creator: Pitura Freska
desc: Venetian dialect for Pink Floyd. The local reggae band recounts singer Sir Oliver Skardy’s failed attempt to reach the concert played on a barge in St Mark’s Basin on Redentore night, 15 July 1989.

title: Que c’est triste Venise
creator: Charles Aznavour
desc: The title means “how sad Venice is”: a jilted lover finds gondolas, pigeons and the moonlit lagoon useless without love. The farewell verse names the Bridge of Sighs, the enclosed stone bridge behind the Doge’s Palace.

title: …sofferte onde serene…
creator: Luigi Nono
desc: The title means “suffered, serene waves.” Venetian composer Luigi Nono finished this piece for piano and tape at his home on Giudecca island, shaping it from the bells he heard across the water. Written for pianist Maurizio Pollini.

title: Nelle paludi di Venezia Francesco si fermò per pregare e tutto tacque
creator: Angelo Branduardi
desc: The title means “in the marshes of Venice Francis stopped to pray and all fell silent.” Sung with Portugal’s Madredeus. Saint Francis is said to have landed on San Francesco del Deserto island in 1220; friars still live there.

title: La bellezza
place: Grand Hotel des Bains, Lido di Venezia
creator: Roberto Vecchioni
desc: The title means “beauty.” Vecchioni retells Thomas Mann’s Death in Venice, an aging man’s hopeless infatuation on the Lido. Mann stayed at the Grand Hotel des Bains in 1911, and Visconti filmed his adaptation in the same hotel.

title: The Heart of Venice
creator: Erla Zwingle
desc: A history and everyday-life walk from St Mark’s Square, the city’s grand central piazza, past a 1310 coup memorial, back-street churches and the opera house, finishing at the old market and money district around the Rialto Bridge.

title: Finding the Forgotten Venetians: A Walk Around the Castello District
creator: Erla Zwingle
desc: A walk through overlooked local lives, starting at the Biennale gardens in eastern Castello, past monuments to resistance fighters and the city’s former cathedral island, ending by the naval history museum and its small seamen’s church.

title: Bacchus, Bridges and Bacari: A Cultured Pub Crawl of Venice
creator: A History of Italy Podcast
desc: A wine-bar crawl with history on the side, starting in Campo San Geremia, a square near the station, through five old-style bars serving small snacks and over the Rialto Bridge, ending in a quiet neighbourhood square in Santa Croce.

title: Vibrant Venice: A Walk through Rialto and San Polo with Context
creator: Context Travel
desc: A trade-and-art history walk starting at Campo San Bartolomeo, by a playwright’s statue, over the Rialto Bridge to the market and a medieval tavern, ending at the Frari, a vast Gothic friars’ church full of Titian paintings.

title: Vivaldi, Tintoretto and Marco Polo: A Venice Walking Tour
creator: Marina Proskurnina
desc: A walk through residential Venice tracing three famous locals, starting at a stone bridge by the Jewish Ghetto, past a painter’s house, the Rialto and a merchant explorer’s home, ending at the church where Vivaldi was baptised.

title: Banking, the Telescope, and Quarantine: A Venice Walking Tour
creator: Marina Proskurnina
desc: A walk through Venetian ideas, from banking and Galileo’s telescope to plague quarantine, starting on the Rialto Bridge, past a playwright’s childhood home and a fistfight bridge, ending at the wooden bridge by the Accademia gallery.

title: The Last Geniuses of Venice: A Casanova, Vivaldi and Tiepolo Walk
creator: Marina Proskurnina
desc: An 18th-century biography walk following a seducer, a composer and a painter, starting at the wooden bridge by the Accademia gallery, past the opera house and Vivaldi’s orphanage church, ending on a Castello lane near Tiepolo’s birthplace.

title: Zombie Tide: A Fictional Venice Walking Tour
creator: Mila
desc: An interactive zombie-outbreak story with history woven in, starting on top of the Rialto Bridge and running through back streets to St Mark’s Square and past the Bridge of Sighs, ending on the broad waterfront promenade beyond.

title: Tasty Traditions: A Venice Food Tour with Context
creator: Context Travel
desc: A sommelier-led food walk starting at Campo Santi Giovanni e Paolo, by an equestrian statue, through wine bars, a fry shop and old pastry shops across the Rialto, ending at a tavern by the bridge where rival gangs once brawled.

title: The Travels
place: Corte del Milion, Marco Polo’s family home
creator: Marco Polo
desc: Polo’s account of 24 years in Asia, dictated in a Genoese prison around 1298. People thought he exaggerated. The family house stood in Corte del Milion, a small courtyard behind the Rialto. The name comes from the book’s Italian title, Il Milione.

title: The Merchant of Venice
place: Campo del Ghetto Nuovo, Jewish Ghetto
creator: William Shakespeare
desc: Shakespeare’s play about Shylock, the Jewish moneylender, and a loan secured by a pound of flesh. It never names the Ghetto. But the Ghetto, the walled district where Venice made Jews live from 1516, was already eighty years old. It is still lived in.

title: The Story of My Life
place: Doge’s Palace and the Piombi prison cells
creator: Giacomo Casanova
desc: A selection from Casanova’s memoirs: gambling, seduction, cons and travel across 18th-century Europe. In 1756 he escaped from the Piombi, cells under the lead roof of the Doge’s Palace, through a hole in the ceiling. Few others ever did.

title: Death in Venice
place: Grand Hotel des Bains, Lido di Venezia
creator: Thomas Mann
desc: Mann’s short novel about an ageing writer who comes to Venice to rest and becomes obsessed with a boy, while cholera spreads in the city. It is about 70 pages. Mann stayed at the Grand Hotel des Bains on the Lido, the beach island, in 1911.

title: If Venice Dies
creator: Salvatore Settis
desc: An Italian archaeologist’s short polemic about what tourism, cruise ships and an emptying population are doing to Venice. The city has fewer than 50,000 residents. Large cruise ships docked at the Marittima terminal until a 2021 ban.

title: Polpo: A Venetian Cookbook (Of Sorts)
creator: Russell Norman
desc: A London restaurateur’s cookbook built on Venice’s bacari, the small wine bars that serve cicchetti, little snacks. It has real recipes and a lot of photos. The squid, crab and sardines come from the Rialto fish market, open in the mornings.

title: Venice Is a Fish
creator: Tiziano Scarpa
desc: A Venetian-born novelist’s short guide to the city by body part: feet, legs, hands, mouth. It is funny and practical. Campo Santa Margherita, a big square in Dorsoduro with a fish stall and students drinking spritz, is the city he describes.

title: The City of Falling Angels
creator: John Berendt
desc: Berendt arrived in Venice three days after La Fenice, the opera house, burned down in 1996. He stayed for years and reported on the inquiry, the rebuilding and the city’s feuds. Two electricians were convicted of arson. The theatre reopened in 2003.

title: Lagrime di San Pietro: Il magnanimo Pietro
place: Orlando di Lasso statue, Promenadeplatz square
creator: Orlando di Lasso
desc: From Lasso’s last work, “The Tears of St Peter”; this opening madrigal means “Great-hearted Peter.” He led the Wittelsbach dukes’ court music for nearly 40 years and died in Munich in 1594. His statue stands on Promenadeplatz square.

title: Idomeneo, K. 366: Overture
creator: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart
desc: Mozart’s first great opera, written for the Munich carnival, premiered on 29 January 1781 in the court’s rococo Cuvilliés Theatre. Its carved boxes survived wartime bombing in storage and were rebuilt in a wing of the Residenz palace in 1958.

title: Morgen!
creator: Richard Strauss
desc: The title means “Tomorrow!” Strauss was born in 1864 in a house on Altheimer Eck lane, marked by a plaque, the son of a court opera horn player. He wrote this song in 1894, the year he became a conductor at the Munich court opera.

title: Tristan und Isolde: Prelude
creator: Richard Wagner
desc: King Ludwig II paid Wagner’s debts and brought him to Munich, where “Tristan and Isolde” premiered at the National Theatre opera house on 10 June 1865. The unresolved chord in its opening bars is one of the most discussed sounds in music.

title: Carmina Burana: O Fortuna
creator: Carl Orff
desc: Munich-born Orff set poems from the Codex Buranus, a medieval manuscript found at Benediktbeuern Abbey and now kept at the Bavarian State Library on Ludwigstraße, which also holds Orff’s own score. The work premiered in Frankfurt in 1937.

title: I Feel Love
creator: Donna Summer
desc: Giorgio Moroder and Pete Bellotte built this all-synthesizer track with Summer, then living in Munich, at Musicland Studios in the basement of the Arabella high-rise in Bogenhausen. Led Zeppelin, Queen and the Rolling Stones recorded there too.

title: Skandal im Sperrbezirk
creator: Spider Murphy Gang
desc: The title means “Scandal in the restricted zone.” After the 1972 Olympics Munich banned prostitution almost citywide, even in the old red-light streets near the main station. This tale of a call girl named Rosi still hit No. 1 despite a radio boycott.

title: Archangels Thunderbird
creator: Amon Düül II
desc: Krautrock pioneers who grew out of a radical artists’ commune in Schwabing, the district that was Munich’s bohemian and countercultural heart along Leopoldstraße boulevard. This was the single from their 1970 double album “Yeti.”

title: Die weiße Rose
creator: Konstantin Wecker
desc: The title means “The White Rose.” Munich-born Wecker wrote it while scoring the 1982 film about the student resisters caught in 1943 dropping leaflets into the atrium of the university’s main building. It salutes anyone who stands up to fascism.

title: Ich, Roque
creator: Sportfreunde Stiller
desc: The title means “I, Roque.” A band from Germering, just west of Munich, sings as Roque Santa Cruz, FC Bayern’s Paraguayan striker and super-sub of 1999–2007, whose home ground was the Olympic Stadium until 2005. He still sings it at Oktoberfest.

title: Stadt die immer schläft
creator: Moop Mama
desc: The title means “City that always sleeps,” a jab at Munich’s small-mindedness and early closing times. The ten-piece hip-hop brass band held its first public rehearsal in the Englischer Garten park in 2009 and is known for unannounced street gigs.

title: Ohne dich (schlaf’ ich heut’ Nacht nicht ein)
creator: Münchener Freiheit
desc: The title means “Without you (I won’t sleep tonight).” The band named itself after Münchner Freiheit, “Munich Freedom,” the busy square at the heart of Schwabing. This ballad was their biggest hit, reaching No. 2 in Germany.

title: Living on My Own
place: Old Mrs Henderson nightclub (now Paradiso), Glockenbach
creator: Freddie Mercury
desc: Mercury spent long stretches in Munich in the early 1980s and recorded his solo album here. The video was shot at his 39th birthday, a black-and-white party at Old Mrs Henderson, a drag cabaret nightclub on Rumfordstraße in the Glockenbach quarter.

title: Lola Montez: A Life
creator: Bruce Seymour
desc: The Irish-born dancer who became Ludwig I’s lover in 1846 and helped cost him his throne two years later. A lively, well-researched life. Her portrait hangs in the king’s Gallery of Beauties at Nymphenburg Palace.

title: Gladius Dei
creator: Thomas Mann
desc: A short story that opens “Munich was radiant.” A gaunt young zealot demands that an art dealer near Odeonsplatz, the grand square by the Residenz, burn a picture of the Madonna. About twenty pages, in Penguin’s Death in Venice and Other Tales.

title: The Swan King: Ludwig II of Bavaria
creator: Christopher McIntosh
desc: The standard readable life of Bavaria’s strange, shy king. He paid Wagner’s debts, and Tristan and Die Meistersinger premiered at the National Theatre, the opera house on Max-Joseph-Platz. Ludwig later sat there alone for private shows.

title: A Time of Gifts
creator: Patrick Leigh Fermor
desc: An 18-year-old walks from Holland toward Constantinople in 1933–34. In Munich he spends an evening in the Hofbräuhaus, the old beer hall by Platzl square, among huge drinkers and brownshirts. He wrote it forty years later.

title: Where Ghosts Walked: Munich’s Road to the Third Reich
place: Site of the Bürgerbräukeller beer hall, Gasteig
creator: David Clay Large
desc: How the easygoing art city of 1900 became the Nazi party’s home base. Clear and well told. Hitler’s 1923 putsch began at the Bürgerbräukeller beer hall in Haidhausen. The hall is gone; the Gasteig arts centre stands on the site.

title: Concerning the Spiritual in Art
creator: Wassily Kandinsky
desc: Kandinsky wrote this short manifesto for abstract painting while living in Schwabing. It came out in 1911, the year of the Blue Rider group. The Lenbachhaus, a villa museum by Königsplatz, holds the biggest Blue Rider collection.

title: The Munich Art Hoard: Hitler’s Dealer and His Secret Legacy
place: Hofgarten arcades, site of the 1937 Degenerate Art show
creator: Catherine Hickley
desc: In 2013 customs officers found over a thousand artworks in a quiet Schwabing flat. The owner’s father had sold Nazi-banned art. That “Degenerate Art” show opened in 1937 in the Hofgarten arcades, a building by the palace garden.

title: The White Rose: Munich 1942–1943
creator: Inge Scholl
desc: Hans and Sophie Scholl’s sister on the student resistance group. In 1943 they threw leaflets into the atrium of the university’s main building and were executed four days later. Bronze leaflets are set in the pavement outside. It is short.

title: Munich
creator: Robert Harris
desc: A novel built closely on the record of the 1938 conference, told by two invented diplomats. The deal was signed in the Führerbau on Arcisstraße, Hitler’s office building. It survived the war and is now a music university.

title: One Day in September
creator: Simon Reeve
desc: The 1972 Olympic hostage-taking, in which eleven Israeli team members died, and the botched rescue. Reeve interviewed one of the surviving attackers. The team lived at Connollystraße 31 in the Olympic Village. A plaque is by the door.

title: Munich Through the Centuries: Highlights of the Historic City Centre
creator: Simone Brokmeier
desc: A local guide’s history overview of eight centuries of Munich, starting on Marienplatz, the main square, and passing the open-air food market and the city’s oldest parish church before finishing a few streets north of the square.

title: Munich’s Third Reich: The City’s Role in Nazi Germany
creator: Simone Brokmeier
desc: A history of Hitler’s rise in Munich, starting at the Isartor, a medieval city gate, and passing the beer hall where he joined the party and a book-burning square, ending at the memorial to a synagogue the Nazis demolished in 1938.

title: Munich’s Old Town: A Family-Friendly Tour of Its Secrets and Legends
creator: Beardedman
desc: A family-friendly tour of old-town legends and odd details, starting on Odeonsplatz, a royal square, and passing the former royal palace and the open-air food market, ending at the fish fountain on Marienplatz, the main square.

title: Nazi History of Munich: A Tour with Context
creator: Context Travel
desc: A historian’s account of how Munich became the Nazi “Capital of the Movement,” starting on Marienplatz, the main square, and passing a monumental loggia and the former party quarter, ending at a fountain in an old botanical garden.

title: Munching on Munich: A Guide to its Cafés and Culinary Highlights
creator: Jo Eckardt
desc: A short café and food walk, starting at the Isartor, a medieval city gate with a café in its tower, and passing a chocolate shop and the open-air food market, ending at a café overlooking Marienplatz, the main square.

title: Flavors of Bavaria: A Food Tour in Munich with Context
creator: Context Travel
desc: A food tour of Bavarian traditions and newer tastes, starting at the Sendlinger Tor, a medieval city gate, and passing a bakery, the open-air food market and a coffee roaster, ending at a wine bar in the old town.

title: Munich’s Beer Culture: A Walking Tour of its Biergartens with Context
creator: Context Travel
desc: A beer sommelier’s history of Munich brewing, from monks and the 1516 purity law to Oktoberfest, starting on Karlsplatz, a busy city square, and passing old breweries and beer gardens, ending at a beer cellar across the river.

title: Watermark
place: Brodsky’s grave, San Michele cemetery island
creator: Joseph Brodsky
desc: Brodsky, an exiled Russian poet, came to Venice most winters for seventeen years. This is a short book of fog, water and light, not sights. He is buried on San Michele, the cemetery island between the city and Murano.

title: The Aspern Papers
place: Palazzo Soranzo Cappello on Rio Marin
creator: Henry James
desc: A short novel about an editor who rents rooms from an old woman to get at a dead poet’s letters. It is based on a real hunt for Shelley’s papers. James set it in a palazzo modelled on Palazzo Soranzo Cappello, on a quiet canal in Santa Croce.

title: City of Fortune: How Venice Won and Lost a Naval Empire
creator: Roger Crowley
desc: A fast narrative of five centuries when Venice ran a sea empire, from the sack of Constantinople in 1204 to its slow decline. The Arsenale, the state shipyard, could build a war galley in a day. Its lion-guarded gate is still there.

title: Miami Bici
creator: Killa Fonic
desc: The title puns ‘Miami Beach’ with ‘bici’ (whip) — the hit from a hometown comedy blockbuster. Killa Fonic, born in Bucharest, is one of the sharpest voices of the city’s current rap wave, pinned to the southern Berceni blocks.

title: Venice
creator: Jan Morris
desc: Morris’s portrait of the whole city: its people, boats, food, dialect and long history. She starts where Venice started, in the lagoon. Torcello, an island now almost empty, had a cathedral and thousands of people before Venice did.

title: Saint Tropez
creator: Florin Salam
desc: Florin Salam is the ‘king of manele,’ the Roma-rooted, keyboard-and-trumpet party music of Bucharest’s working-class mahalale. Adored at every wedding, sneered at by the elite; this is one of its biggest hits. Pinned to Ferentari.

title: Un 2 și trei de 0
creator: B.U.G. Mafia
desc: The title spells out the year 2000. B.U.G. Mafia invented Romanian gangsta rap in Pantelimon, the tough eastern district they never stopped repping; this is their millennium anthem.

title: Stereo Love
place: National University of Music, Știrbei Vodă
creator: Edward Maya
desc: That mournful accordion hook conquered the planet in 2009. Edward Maya, a Bucharest producer trained at the city’s music conservatory, made one of the biggest dance records ever to come out of Romania.

title: Underground Folclor
creator: Subcarpați
desc: The title fuses ‘underground’ and ‘folklore’ — exactly the trick. Subcarpați lace Bucharest hip-hop with Romanian folk samples and pan-pipes; pinned to the Museum of the Romanian Peasant they plunder for sound.

title: Zaraza
creator: Cristian Vasile
desc: A smoky interwar tango named for an unattainable woman, the signature of Bucharest’s great romance crooner. Vasile sang it in the glittering cafés of the Calea Victoriei, the boulevard of ‘Little Paris’ between the wars.

title: Pe ape
creator: Iris
desc: The title means ‘On the Waters.’ Iris are Romania’s flagship hard-rock band, filling the Bucharest arenas for decades with anthemic, big-hearted metal. Pinned to the Sala Polivalentă, their concert home.

title: Ciocârlia
creator: Grigoraș Dinicu
desc: The title means ‘The Lark’ — a violin tour de force that mimics birdsong until the strings seem to take flight. Dinicu came from a celebrated Bucharest family of lăutari, the Roma professional musicians who ruled the old town’s taverns.

title: Romanian Rhapsody No. 1
creator: George Enescu
desc: A whirling medley of tavern tunes and folk dances that rises to a delirious gallop — Romania’s most beloved orchestral showpiece. Enescu made his musical life at the Athenaeum, the domed concert hall at the heart of Bucharest.

title: Way Down We Go
creator: Kaleo
desc: A stomping, bluesy howl that became a global sync-licensing juggernaut. Kaleo formed in Mosfellsbær, the greater-Reykjavík town in the lava fields, before decamping to America.

title: Near Light
creator: Ólafur Arnalds
desc: A hush of piano and strings, recorded live across a week of living-room sessions. Ólafur Arnalds, from Mosfellsbær on the city’s edge, helped define the Icelandic neoclassical sound now heard in film scores everywhere.

title: Reykjavík
creator: Emmsjé Gauti
desc: A rapped love letter to the city itself. Emmsjé Gauti is one of the biggest names in Icelandic hip-hop, whose cradle is Breiðholt — the concrete outer suburb that is Reykjavík’s answer to the banlieue.

title: Jungle Drum
creator: Emilíana Torrini
desc: A giddy, whistling pop smash that topped charts across Europe. Emilíana Torrini — Italian-Icelandic, raised in Kópavogur just south of the capital — sings it like a schoolgirl crush.

title: Believe
creator: GusGus
desc: Aching, slow-building house from the shape-shifting collective GusGus. Their sound is inseparable from Kaffibarinn, the tiny 101 bar once part-owned by Damon Albarn, at the centre of Reykjavík nightlife.

title: Green Grass of Tunnel
creator: múm
desc: Music-box electronica — glitch and glockenspiel and whispered voices — from múm at their most childlike. A harbour-district reverie for Reykjavík’s early-2000s laptop scene down by the Grandi docks.

title: Jóga
creator: Björk
desc: Named for Björk’s best friend, this is her ‘state of emergency’ hymn to Iceland’s shuddering landscape, strings grinding like tectonic plates. The Grótta lighthouse on the Seltjarnarnes tip matches its elemental scale.

title: From the Start
creator: Laufey
desc: Bossa-nova heartbreak with a viral wink, from the Reykjavík-born, conservatory-trained Laufey, who has made a generation fall for jazz. The old-town lake, the Tjörnin, mirrors the genteel classical side of the city that raised her.

title: Ekki enn
creator: Purrkur Pillnikk
desc: The title means ‘Not Yet.’ Purrkur Pillnikk — featuring a young Einar Örn, later of the Sugarcubes — fired off jagged 90-second bursts. Hótel Borg on Austurvöllur was a hub of the scene captured in the film ‘Rokk í Reykjavík.’

title: Spáðu í mig
creator: Megas
desc: The title means roughly ‘Read me / figure me out.’ Megas, the sardonic ‘Icelandic Dylan,’ has needled the nation since 1972. His scabrous, literary songs belong to the old-town heart of 101 Reykjavík around Ingólfstorg.

title: Birthday
creator: The Sugarcubes
desc: Björk’s first international moment, all coos and swells, with the band she led before going solo. The Sugarcubes grew out of the anarchic Smekkleysa — ‘Bad Taste’ — collective and its record shop on Laugavegur.

title: Little Talks
creator: Of Monsters and Men
desc: The ‘hey!’-chanting duet that took Iceland’s folk-pop worldwide, trumpets and ghosts and all. Of Monsters and Men came up through the Reykjavík scene along Laugavegur and the Iceland Airwaves festival.

title: Minni Íslands (Iceland Overture), Op. 9
creator: Jón Leifs
desc: Iceland’s fierce national composer wove the old hymns into this early overture. Leifs founded the country’s composers’-rights society in Reykjavík; the Iceland Symphony that records him plays the glass-fronted Harpa on the harbour.

title: Chasing Highs
creator: Alma
desc: Alma was born in Kuopio but raised from a few weeks old in Vuosaari, the 1990s tower-block suburb at the eastern end of the metro line, caring for two chronically ill parents. Her breakout single carries all of that hunger for escape.

title: Cha Cha Cha
creator: Käärijä
desc: Jere Pöyhönen’s Eurovision phenomenon — industrial rap that flips into a schlager chorus, sung in Finnish about drinking away a working week. He grew up in Ruskeasanta, Vantaa; the city thanked him with a 37-metre mural on this supermarket wall.

title: In the Shadows
creator: The Rasmus
desc: Four boys at a lower-secondary school in Suutarila, northern Helsinki, formed a band in 1994 and played their first gig at the school Christmas party. Nine years later this made them Finland’s biggest rock export of the decade.

title: Join Me in Death
creator: HIM
desc: Ville Valo called it ‘love metal’ — gothic romance with pop hooks, and Finland’s first real rock export. He was born in Vallila and raised in Oulunkylä, the leafy northern rail suburb, forming the band with a schoolfriend in 1991.

title: Oi maamme Helsinki
creator: Ege Zulu
desc: The title rewrites Finland’s national anthem, ‘Oi maamme’ (‘Oh, Our Land’), as an East Helsinki one. Ege Zulu is Finnish-Congolese, born in the city and raised in Roihuvuori. Puhos is the crumbling 1965 mall that became East Helsinki’s immigrant heart.

title: Freestyler
creator: Bomfunk MC’s
desc: Finland’s biggest global hit: breakbeat with a rapper and a kid freezing time with a Walkman. The video was shot here and on the concrete decks of Merihaka next door — still the world’s best-known image of the Helsinki metro.

title: Nothing Else Matters
creator: Apocalyptica
desc: Four cello students met at the Sibelius Academy and decided to play Metallica. Their reading of the 1991 ballad turned a conservatoire in-joke into a thirty-year career. This is the Academy building where they studied.

title: Voittamaton
creator: Fintelligens
desc: The title means ‘Unbeatable.’ Elastinen and Iso H’s debut single is the accepted starting gun for commercial Finnish-language rap. Iso H grew up in Herttoniemi, in East Helsinki, where their Rähinä Records label kept its studio for years.

title: Malibu Beach Nightmare
creator: Hanoi Rocks
desc: Hanoi Rocks formed in Helsinki in 1979 and invented the look Guns N’ Roses later wore. Michael Monroe was born in the city; the band became a national act on the stage of Tavastia, the club that has anchored Finnish rock since 1970.

title: Ampukaa komissaarit, nuo hullut koirat!
creator: Ultra Bra
desc: The title means ‘Shoot the commissars, those mad dogs!’ A left-wing student choir-pop collective founded in Helsinki in 1994, they won a socialist song contest with this. Kallio, the old working-class district, was their natural ground.

title: Fairyport
creator: Wigwam
desc: Wigwam formed in Helsinki in 1968 from the wreckage of Blues Section and became Finland’s great prog band. This sprawling title track came off a double album cut at Finnvox, the studio that was the engine room of the Love Records era.

title: Håper du har plass
creator: Cezinando
desc: The title means ‘Hope You Have Room.’ Oslo-born Cezinando writes searching, wordy Norwegian rap; the diverse inner-east district of Grønland reads as its natural setting.

title: Brother Wind
creator: Jan Garbarek
desc: Mysen-born but Oslo-based, the saxophonist cut his glacial ECM classics at Grünerløkka’s Rainbow Studio, where engineer Jan Erik Kongshaug shaped the label’s famous glassy ‘ECM sound.’

title: Inspector Norse
creator: Todd Terje
desc: Sun-bright, gurgling space-disco that soundtracked a decade of Scandinavian cool. Terje Olsen studied astrophysics at Oslo’s Blindern campus and built his sound in the city’s cosmic-disco scene.

title: Alt kan repareres
creator: Jokke & Valentinerne
desc: The title means ‘Everything Can Be Repaired.’ Joachim ‘Jokke’ Nielsen’s raw, plain-spoken Norwegian rock is inseparable from Oslo’s east end; the pin sits in the Grünerløkka he sang from and drank in.

title: Take On Me
creator: a-ha
desc: The world’s favourite synth-pop hook, with that pencil-sketch video. The trio formed in Oslo in 1982 before chasing the hit to London; there’s no single ‘a-ha address,’ so their homecoming arena stands in.

title: Romance for Violin and Orchestra, Op. 26
creator: Johan Svendsen
desc: Christiania-born Svendsen ran the young capital’s musical life as its leading conductor. This tender violin song is his best-loved miniature, all Nordic warmth; the National Theatre is heir to the Christiania stage he presided over.

title: i wanna be your girlfriend
creator: girl in red
desc: The SoundCloud confession that made Marie Ulven a queer bedroom-pop hero worldwide. She’s from Horten but lives and records in Oslo’s hip east-side Grünerløkka.

title: Alexander Kiellands plass
creator: Lillebjørn Nilsen
desc: Oslo’s great troubadour names the song for the working-class square on the Grünerløkka–Ila border where he grew up, turning a tram junction into the most literally place-pinned song in the whole set.

title: Mother North
place: Former Helvete record shop, Schweigaards gate
creator: Satyricon
desc: Norway’s black metal remade extreme music out of Oslo in the early ’90s, amid real church-burnings and worse. Satyricon are the tasteful pick over the crime-shadowed Mayhem; the pin is the old Helvete shop, the scene’s hub.

title: Påfugl
creator: Karpe
desc: The title means ‘Peacock.’ Magdi and Chirag — Karpe — are the definitive voice of multicultural Oslo, rapping identity and belonging; Holmlia, the mixed southern district, stands in as a thematic home.

title: Retko te viđam sa devojkama
creator: Idoli
desc: The title means ‘I Rarely See You with Girls’ — sly, deadpan, and daring for 1980. Idoli led Belgrade’s Novi Talas out of the SKC, the student cultural centre that housed the whole new-wave scene.

title: Žao mi je što sam ostario
creator: Lenhart Tapes
desc: The title means ‘I’m Sorry I Grew Old.’ Vladimir Lenhart plays three cassette decks live as instruments, here wrapped around Svetlana Spajić’s traditional village singing — the Drugstore aesthetic exactly: industrial ruin and folk memory.

title: Hoću da znam
creator: Partibrejkers
desc: The title means ‘I Want to Know.’ Partibrejkers were the band Belgrade’s anti-war youth actually trusted through the sanctions years. At Kosovska 11 they helped launch Rimtutituki, the anti-war supergroup that played from a moving truck.

title: Suženi snovi
creator: Repetitor
desc: The title means ‘Narrowed Dreams.’ Repetitor are two-thirds women and the loudest heirs to Belgrade’s post-Šarlo noise lineage, having come up through DIY spaces like the Cetinjska brewery courtyard rather than the industry.

title: Par godina za nas
place: Milan Mladenović’s former home, New Belgrade
creator: Ekatarina Velika
desc: The title means ‘A Few Years for Us,’ voted the greatest song of the former Yugoslavia in a 2006 poll. Milan Mladenović lived in this New Belgrade block until his death at 36; the plaque there is carved with EKV lyrics.

title: Ona se budi
place: Site of Akademija club, Knez Mihailova
creator: Šarlo Akrobata
desc: The title means ‘She Is Waking.’ Šarlo Akrobata lasted barely a year but rewired Belgrade music — Milan Mladenović went on to EKV, Koja to Disciplina Kičme. Akademija’s basement was the scene’s physical centre.

title: Lutka sa naslovne strane
creator: Riblja Čorba
desc: The title means ‘Cover Girl.’ Bora Đorđević’s snarling debut made Riblja Čorba a national band. It was cut in Studio V of state radio, a few hundred metres from Skadarlija — the establishment recording the insurgents.

title: Crni leptir
creator: YU Grupa
desc: The title means ‘Black Butterfly.’ The Jelić brothers formed YU Grupa in Belgrade in 1970 and gave Yugoslavia its first great hard-rock band, folk modes and all. Dom omladine was the youth house where that generation played.

title: Deseta rukovet (Pesme sa Ohrida)
creator: Stevan Stojanović Mokranjac
desc: A ‘rukovet’ is a garland — folk songs woven into choral art music. Mokranjac founded Belgrade’s first music school and led its choral society, more or less inventing Serbian art music single-handedly. Kolarac is still its home stage.

title: Prokleta nedelja
creator: Toma Zdravković
desc: The title means ‘Damned Sunday.’ Toma Zdravković sang heartbreak in the taverns of Skadarlija for thirty years; his monument now stands on the cobbles at No. 26, a few doors from Dva jelena, where he played.

title: Firuze
creator: Sezen Aksu
desc: The title is a woman’s name, from the word for turquoise. Sezen Aksu, the ‘Queen of Turkish Pop,’ has staged her Istanbul reign for decades under the pines of the Harbiye open-air theatre. İzmir-raised, Istanbul-crowned.

title: İstikrarlı Hayal Hakikattir
creator: Gaye Su Akyol
desc: The title means ‘Consistent Imagination Is Reality.’ Istanbul-born Gaye Su Akyol wraps Anatolian melody in surf and psych; she’s the figurehead of Kadıköy’s restless new scene on the Asian side.

title: İstanbul’da Sonbahar
creator: Teoman
desc: The title means ‘Autumn in Istanbul’ — rakı, rain, and heartbreak. Teoman set the city’s melancholy to guitar rock; Nevizade’s tavern alley off İstiklal is exactly the wet, lamp-lit Beyoğlu the song walks through.

title: Gülpembe
creator: Barış Manço
